(3) It enters company name, address, tax ID, MCC, website, product description, a representative, every director and owner, and the payout IBAN (a Connect table).

m-560f9d37.t: JCC's published terms (v2.10) say JCC 'will create a Collateral' at signing if, in its sole judgment, the merchant's activities might damage its interests. It consists of either or both of: a rolling reserve — a percentage of each day's gross sales (less MSC) retained for a period, both set in the individual agreement — and a bank guarantee for a percentage of anticipated gross purchases. JCC may also withhold or delay payments to build a chargeback reserve or collateral (§6.2, §7.5), and after termination keeps the collateral for one year from the last transaction, or indefinitely after material breach. Where the law requires, withheld amounts are safeguarded in segregated client accounts.

m-50af1633.t: JCC's Terms for the Participation in Card Schemes changed little between Version 2.9 (file path 2024/03) and Version 2.10 (file path 2026/08), by a word-level comparison of the two PDFs made on 4 October 2026: new clause 6.7 has withheld amounts held as safeguarded client funds in segregated accounts where the law requires; clause 5.3 now says interchange and card-scheme fees inside the Merchant Service Charge are third-party costs whose increases or decreases the merchant bears; clause 5.1 adds scheme fees for merchants classed as high-risk; clause 15.2(g) adds breach of card-scheme rules as a ground for termination without notice; and notices may now be delivered by email.

m-4e925060.t: JCC does not publish its Merchant Service Charge (MSC): as of 2026-10-04 its merchant FAQ answers 'How can I obtain my MSCs?' with 'Please call our 24-hour helpline', its POS and gateway pages show no prices, and its Terms v2.10 (§5.3) say the MSC is paid 'as provided in the Agreement'. It does publish the components: a document 'Access criteria & pricing' (file dated 22/10/2018, still linked) says JCC prices euro-area consumer cards as 'MIF++' — interchange 0.2% debit / 0.3% credit, plus scheme fees, plus an acquirer fee set by risk factors — and the FAQ links Visa and Mastercard scheme-fee schedules dated 16/07/2026. Under §5.3 changes in interchange and scheme fees fall on the merchant.

m-4b511b58.t: Mastercard mandates MATCH Pro for all acquirers with merchant activity, unless excused by Mastercard or prohibited by law (Security Rules and Procedures - Merchant Edition, 4 August 2026, sections 11.3, 7.1.1). An acquirer must check MATCH Pro before signing a merchant or enabling acceptance (section 11.6) and, when either side acts to terminate while a listed reason-code condition is believed to exist, must add the merchant within five calendar days (11.5). Records stay five years and are then purged automatically (11.10). A listing does not bar onboarding (11.2), and MATCH Pro may not be used or threatened as a collection tool for minor discretionary merchant activity (11.4, item 8).

m-49193204.t: A row in the Central Bank of Cyprus passport register does not show market presence. Squareup International Limited (Ireland) is listed as notified for Cyprus on 29 November 2021 for services 3(b,c) and 5 (file of 23 September 2026), yet Square's own help page, read on 4 October 2026, says: 'Card payment acceptance with the Square app is currently available in the US, Canada, Australia, Japan, the United Kingdom, Republic of Ireland, France and Spain. We currently don't support payment card processing outside of these countries'.

m-4517d635.t: PayPal's merchant fee page served for Cyprus (one page for 13 markets including CY), last updated 7 September 2026, sets the standard rate for receiving domestic commercial transactions - sender and receiver both in the EEA - at 3.4% plus a fixed fee, €0.35 when euros are received; card payments by buyers without a PayPal account cost 1.9% plus the fixed fee. Payments from UK senders add 1.29%, from all other markets 1.99%. The standard dispute fee is €14.00 (high-volume €28.00); a €16.00 chargeback fee applies to card transactions not processed through a buyer's PayPal account or guest checkout. Currency conversion costs 3% above the base exchange rate.

m-44f413c1.t: Card payments reported by Cyprus-resident payment providers, second half of 2025 (Central Bank of Cyprus release of 22 July 2026): 70% by number were made in person at a point of sale and 30% online, but online carried 60% of the value; the average payment was about €38 at a point of sale and €129 online (euro area: €33 and €60). Cross-border transactions were 45% of the volume and 56% of the value; among EEA countries other than Cyprus, Lithuania ranked first by country of the counterpart provider and Ireland by country of the merchant. Cards were 75% of non-cash payments by number. This is the paying side: the release says card acquiring 'is not presented separately nor analyzed'.

m-448ea3cd.t: myPOS serves Cyprus merchants through myPOS Limited, an Irish electronic money institution (licence no. C475122) that describes itself as 'a member of major international card associations including MasterCard, VISA and AMEX'. Its Legal Agreement (effective 17 July 2023, last updated 3 April 2026) defines a 'Reserve' as an amount, usually a percentage of acquired transaction value, withheld for a set period to cover chargebacks, fraud or other disputes, and makes the client liable for any reversed payment plus fees applied by myPOS or a card scheme (definitions; clause 12.1); the CBC incoming-passport register shows myPOS Limited notified for Cyprus on 20 September 2022 for services 3 and 5.

m-4259da53.t: JCC Payment Systems Ltd is a 75%-owned subsidiary of Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd: the bank's Annual Financial Report 2025 lists it among subsidiaries with a 75% holding as at 31 December 2025 and the activity 'Development of inter-banking systems, acquiring and processing of card transactions, other payment services and other activities', and reports JCC net fee and commission income of €30 million for 2025 (10% of the group's non-interest income). The report describes the group's 'Payment Services' segment as comprising JCC; it does not say whether the bank itself also acquires card payments, and does not name the holder of the other 25%.

m-41bf0220.t: ISX Financial (Xryma PLC, Cyprus) publishes one PDF with two prohibited-and-restricted lists. The e-money account list (updated 29 November 2024) prohibits shell and bearer-share companies, non-EU crypto exchanges, unlicensed activity and online pharmacies, restricts clients with annual credit turnover above €40 million, and says a MATCH or VMSS listing 'may be prohibited' but 'does not automatically result in prohibition'. The cards list (updated 9 April 2025) goes by merchant category: gambling, crypto purchases, high-risk securities, dating and online pharmacies are restricted (scheme registration); unlicensed CFD and forex platforms, counterfeits and escort services are prohibited.

m-416bb851.t: Walk-through (ii), café with an online-onboarded provider, part 2 of 2 - published Cyprus tariffs as of 2026-10-04, restated, nothing computed. EEA consumer cards in person: myPOS 1.69% + €0.05; Viva 1.69% (minimum €0.03); SumUp 1.95%, or 0.89% on its €19-a-month plan (1.95% stays for Amex, premium, international and corporate cards); Revolut 0.8% + €0.02, with a Business plan from €10 a month (its Cyprus FAQ excludes sole traders, its Business Terms admit them). myPOS and Viva credit takings at once to their own account; a SEPA transfer out costs €4.00 at myPOS, €0.80 at Viva. SumUp and Revolut advertise next-day payout. Viva's free plan has a €4.99 monthly minimum. JCC's merchant service charge is unpublished; Stripe Terminal is listed for Cyprus only as a preview.

m-40fb66ec.t: In-person acceptance through Stripe in Cyprus is still a preview product on 4 October 2026. Stripe's Terminal availability page lists 23 countries where Terminal 'is available' and 17 under 'Available in Preview', Cyprus among them with Bulgaria, Croatia, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Romania, Slovakia and Slovenia. Its Tap to Pay page - a phone used as the terminal - lists Cyprus under 'Availability in Public preview' for Tap to Pay on iPhone, and notes that for platforms its use 'is subject to the Apple Acceptance Platform User Terms and Conditions'. Stripe's Cyprus price list nonetheless already prices Terminal payments.

m-404be4b7.t: In the Central Bank of Cyprus register of EU e-money institutions notified into Cyprus (file dated 23 September 2026), the 22 rows marked '5(acq)' come from 9 home states: France 7, Luxembourg 5, Greece 2, Lithuania 2, Netherlands 2, and one each from Bulgaria, Croatia, Finland and Germany; none has a Greek-letter country code. With the payment-institution file that makes 92 notifications in which service 5 is limited to acquiring, from 22 home states (Bulgaria only in the e-money file). They are not acquiring-only firms: just 21 of the 92 rows (20 payment institutions, 1 e-money institution) list '5(acq)' as the only payment service; the other 71 also notify services such as 3, 6, 7 or 8.

m-4005489d.t: Visa requires an acquirer to hold a Merchant Agreement with each merchant, and a payment facilitator to hold one with each sponsored merchant; the agreement must oblige the merchant to follow applicable law and the Visa Rules, not to submit illegal transactions, and must reserve Visa's right to limit or terminate it (Visa Core Rules section 1.5.2.1, ID# 0003356, edition 18 April 2026, last updated Oct 2025). The acquirer or facilitator may accept transactions only from an entity with which it has a valid Merchant Agreement.

m-3b815656.t: Mastercard's public manuals have no 'marketplace' participant category. A case-insensitive search for 'marketplace' on 4 October 2026 found 0 hits in the Mastercard Rules (2 June 2026), 0 in the Security Rules and Procedures - Merchant Edition (4 August 2026) and 3 in the Transaction Processing Rules (9 December 2025): the name of MCC 5262 'Online Marketplace' and two examples in Rule 5.10 on merchant-initiated transactions, none a definition. Rule 5.1.2.2 of the Rules instead defines a 'Platform Merchant' hosting third-party sellers, whose Merchant Agreement must make it verify each seller and its principal owners, contract with it before submitting transactions and monitor legality.

m-37090a5c.t: Three amending decrees widened the Cyprus card-acceptance list: K.D.P. 446/2021 (Official Gazette No. 5624, 5 November 2021) added private kindergartens (85.10.2), cultural education (85.52) and specialised design (74.10); K.D.P. 52/2022 (No. 5664, 4 February 2022) added taxi operation (49.32); K.D.P. 248/2022 (No. 5711, 24 June 2022) added laundries and dry-cleaning, funeral services, physical well-being and other personal services (96.01, 96.03, 96.04, 96.09) - each with three months to comply, taking the annex from 87 to 95 activity-code entries. CyLaw's K.D.P. indexes for 2022-2026 (to K.D.P. 372/2026, read 4 October 2026) list no later amending decree.

m-34fedf0b.t: Stripe's Acquirer Disclosure for Visa and Mastercard transactions (Cyprus-locale page, undated, read 4 October 2026) states for the European Economic Area: 'Payment Method Acquirer is Stripe Technology Europe, Ltd.' - Stripe's own Irish e-money institution is the acquirer. The same page describes Stripe as 'a Payment Facilitator' of named acquiring banks in the United States, Canada, Japan and Thailand and as an Independent Sales Organization of Network International in the United Arab Emirates. A Cyprus business contracting with Stripe is therefore a direct merchant of the acquirer, not a sponsored merchant of a payment facilitator (the last sentence is an inference from the page).

m-3299bdeb.t: Intraclear Limited, a Cyprus payment institution (licence 115.1.2.35, HE 389967, services 3 and 5), states in the footer of each of six pages of its site opened on 4 October 2026: 'Intraclear Limited is a Visa and Mastercard Principal Member (Acquiring Bank) pursuant to license agreements duly executed', and on the home page 'We are a direct Acquiring Bank for Visa and Mastercard'. Its card-acquiring page addresses 'a brick-and-mortar store or an online enterprise' and starts onboarding with a Merchant Pre-Check Form sent by email; card issuing is 'Coming Soon'. No price list or prohibited-business list is linked, and the home page still shows placeholder 'Lorem Ipsum' testimonials.

m-326a6393.t: Hellenic Bank (now Eurobank Limited) carries its JCC shareholding as an unlisted equity security at fair value through other comprehensive income, not as an associate: €12,592 thousand at 31 December 2023 and €13,138 thousand at 31 December 2024, per its Annual Financial Report 2024. The report gives no percentage. Its 2022 report put the same investment at €10,053 thousand at end-2022 and €7,575 thousand at end-2021, and said a 15% change in unobservable valuation inputs would move the JCC value by €1.5 million. In both reports the dot is a thousands separator ('€13.138 thousand').

m-2c55abb2.t: JCC's document 'Access criteria & pricing' (file name dated 22/10/2018, still linked from its resources page on 2026-10-04) states that for consumer cards issued in the euro area JCC applies 'MIF++' pricing: the multilateral interchange fee (0.2% for debit and 0.3% for credit consumer cards), plus card scheme/processing fees, plus 'fixed costs and acquirer fees' based on risk factors such as the merchant's method of doing business, anticipated transaction amounts and expected annual volume. For non-consumer cards and cards issued outside the euro area it says other interchange fees apply under the card schemes' pricing. No acquirer margin is given.

m-2b6b20bc.t: PCI DSS v4.0 was published in March 2022 and its future-dated new requirements became effective on 31 March 2025; v3.2.1 was retired on 31 March 2024. The PCI Security Standards Council published the limited revision v4.0.1 on 11 June 2024 with 'no additional or deleted requirements' and retired v4.0 on 31 December 2024, after which v4.0.1 is the only active version it supports; no later version was found on 4 October 2026.

m-25cad76f.t: Stripe's Cyprus price list, as of 2026-10-04, charges €20.00 per dispute received ('in rare cases, network fees also apply') and a further €20.00 'dispute countered fee' for each dispute the merchant answers manually, returned only if the dispute is won. For in-person payments through Stripe Terminal it lists 1.4% + €0.10 per successful charge for EEA cards and 2.9% + €0.10 for non-EEA cards, with readers at €59.00 (BBPOS WisePad 3) and €259.00 (Stripe Reader S710), excluding VAT. Stripe's Terminal availability page on the same date lists Cyprus only under 'Available in (Preview)', not among the countries where Terminal is generally available.

m-25a0a6e4.t: Hellenic Bank's last annual report before it became Eurobank Limited shows no merchant-acquiring business of its own. In the Annual Financial Report for 2024 (approved 20 March 2025) the word 'merchant' does not occur, 'acquiring' appears only for share purchases and credit-acquiring companies, and its one disclosed link to card acceptance is an unlisted shareholding in JCC Payment Systems Ltd. Read with the Central Bank's statement that payment and e-money institutions are the exclusive providers of card acquiring in Cyprus, this places Eurobank Limited's merchants with such an institution - JCC being the one it part-owns - or with a provider outside Cyprus; no document read names which.

m-2336e252.t: Bank of Cyprus weighed selling JCC and decided to keep it. Its results announcement of 12 November 2024 said it was 'undertaking a strategic review which may result in a potential disposal of part or all of its holding in JCC, although no decision has been taken at this stage'. Its Annual Financial Report 2024 (file dated 27 March 2025) says: 'Following a strategic review the Board of Directors concluded that in line with the Group’s strategy and capital allocation policy, there is greater value to stakeholders through retaining JCC as part of the Group.' The reports for 2022, 2023 and 2025 carry no such sentence; neither document says when the review began or whether bids were invited.

m-1bb35520.t: Before signing a merchant, Visa requires the acquirer or payment facilitator to ensure the prospective merchant is financially responsible, not engaged in activity that could harm the Visa system or brand, operating within an allowed jurisdiction and not misrepresenting its outlet location (section 1.5.1.3, ID# 0008478), and to 'conduct an adequate due diligence review, including a site visit to the business premises (if applicable) or suitable alternative' (section 5.2.1.2, ID# 0005251). The acquirer must assign to the outlet the MCC 'that most accurately describes its business' (section 1.5.1.11, ID# 0003133); all three in the edition of 18 April 2026.

m-1a7a588b.t: Stripe's payouts documentation, read on 2026-10-04, gives Cyprus an initial settlement timing of 7 calendar days (applies to the first payout) and a default settlement timing of 3 business days for subsequent payouts; it adds that the first payout is typically scheduled to complete within 7–14 days after the first live payment, and that risk criteria may prevent an account from moving to the default timing. Payouts go to the merchant's bank account by IBAN on the schedule chosen in the Dashboard.

m-18122243.t: JCC Payment Systems Ltd (company registration HE29914, LEI 5493004UL7QITGOF5F14) is listed in the Central Bank of Cyprus register of electronic money institutions under licence no. 115.1.3.55 with EMI licence date 12 December 2022; the register's licensing-dates sheet shows an original payment-institution licence of 23 April 2010, a subsequent one of 13 July 2018 and an extension to services 6 and 7 on 10 February 2022. Its authorised payment services are numbers 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8 of Annex I - cash withdrawals, issuing of payment instruments and/or acquiring, money remittance, payment initiation and account information (register file dated 28 September 2026).

m-16bb0678.t: Mastercard's Europe Region chapter (Mastercard Rules, edition 2 June 2026, archive snapshot of 28 September 2026) changes three acquiring rules relevant to Cyprus: under Rule 1.7 'In the EEA, the License covers the entire EEA as the Area of Use'; under Rule 7.6.5.1 an acquirer holding central acquiring authorisation for a sponsored merchant's country needs no licence or Area-of-Use extension; under Rule 5.1.2 each Merchant Agreement with a merchant in the EEA, Gibraltar or the United Kingdom must require the merchant to respond to cardholder disputes and handle chargebacks under the Chargeback Guide. The chapter does not modify Rule 7.8, the USD 10,000,000 sponsored-merchant threshold.

m-136206f5.t: payabl. presents itself as an acquirer for online and in-store trade. On 4 October 2026 its gateway page offered 'Domestic and global card acquiring, and over 300 of the most popular payment methods', and its POS page three terminals plus tap-to-pay on a phone, accepting Visa, Mastercard and American Express cards and Google Pay, Apple Pay and Samsung Pay. The about page names two entities - Payabl. CY Limited (HE289380, payment-institution licence 115.1.2.9/2018 'until the full activation of the EMI license') and Payabl. (UK) Limited (FCA 967259) - not saying which signs a merchant. No page read states Visa or Mastercard membership; no merchant terms, price or prohibited list is published.

m-111f0813.t: Bank of Cyprus's company-only financial statements show dividend income from its 75%-held subsidiary JCC Payment Systems (€ thousand): 2015: 3,000; 2016: 15,000; 2017: 5,250; 2018: 3,750; 2019: 2,250; 2020: 3,270; 2021: 5,078; 2022: 9,000; 2023: 9,000; 2024: 6,000; 2025: 5,055. The group statements print 'Dividends paid to non-controlling interests' of 3,000 (2022), 3,000 (2023), 2,000 (2024) and 1,685 (2025) - each exactly one third of the bank's JCC dividend, which fits a 25% minority share of JCC payouts of 12,000, 12,000, 8,000 and 6,740. The match also holds for 2016-2020 but not for 2015 (1,918 against 1,000) or 2021 (2,110 against 1,693).

m-0b92d579.t: SumUp's Cyprus Payment Terms (effective 07/02/2022, read 4 October 2026) say it has agreements with partner banks, and that card-network rules may require some merchants, depending on payment volume, to sign a separate agreement with a partner institution or the networks, which SumUp would supply (section 3). The linked 'list of acquirers' names Worldpay Limited and First Data Europe Limited (Fiserv), both at UK addresses, Adyen N.V. and, for Amex, 'American Express Service Europe Limited'. The list is not Cyprus-specific - SumUp's Irish site shows the same four - and does not say which acquirer serves Cyprus. SumUp does not call itself a payment facilitator.

m-08bf1c9d.t: JCC Payment Systems Ltd (HE 29914, LEI 5493004UL7QITGOF5F14) was 75% owned by Bank of Cyprus at 30 June 2026 (Bank of Cyprus Interim Report 2026); its net fee and commission income was €15 million in that half-year.

m-00487b25.t: Revolut Business offers card acceptance in Cyprus through Revolut Bank UAB (Lithuania). The Bank of Lithuania register shows a banking licence valid from 2021-12-13 and Cyprus among countries served without a branch, with 'issuing of payment instruments and/or acquiring' from 2022-06-01; the ECB lists it as a directly supervised bank (cut-off 1 July 2026). Its Cyprus (en-CY) price page, as of 2026-10-04: Visa/Mastercard domestic and European consumer cards 1% + €0.20 online, 0.8% + €0.02 in person; domestic commercial and all international cards 2.8% + €0.20 and 2.6% + €0.02; chargeback €15; terminals €189 or €139 plus VAT; next-day payout advertised; a Revolut Business plan is required.

m-fcdef4bb.t: Paphos Municipality announced in December 2025 (press report of 12 December; its own page is dated 15 December) that a physical survey of business premises had found 'over 3,000' operating without the required annual operating licence under ss. 55 and 56 of the Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022 - among them banks, workshops, professionals' offices (accountants', lawyers', architects'), clinics, shops, leisure premises under 50 m2 and fast-food outlets - put down to 'wilful breach or ignorance or negligence'. To end 'the regime of tolerance' it said that from 1 March 2026 it would take legal action and immediately suspend every unlicensed premises; applications are made only online.

m-fbd7aef1.t: The fee for a Cyprus catering-establishment operating licence is set by the class the Deputy Ministry of Tourism assigns. The Second Table of the Catering Establishments Regulations 1986-2005 (reg. 6(1)), in the Law Commissioner's consolidation, charges for issue or renewal €170 for class A, €85 for class B and €51 for class C, €17 per copy and €17 inside a licensed hotel. The business portal (updated 18 September 2026) gives €170.86, €85.43 and €51.26, payable on approval, and a decision within three months of a complete application; it says the licence goes only to persons resident in Cyprus or EU citizens, or legal persons situated in an EU state.

m-f9e32597.t: Whoever keeps or uses business premises in a Cyprus municipality - an office, a shop or a cafe - is charged a yearly professional or trade fee under s. 56(5) of the Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022, within the Fifth Schedule's ceilings: self-employed craftsmen EUR 50; professionals, traders and businessmen working as individuals EUR 200; private companies with up to 5 employees EUR 150, 6-15 EUR 250, 16-30 EUR 350, over 30 EUR 500; partnerships the same; insurance, shipping, airline, banking, financing and portfolio companies and public companies EUR 1,000; others EUR 300. Premises opened in the second half-year pay half; rises are capped at 10% a year; the council may exempt kinds of business.

m-f5a52059.t: Fire safety of Cyprus buildings is designed to Annex IV ('Fire Protection Regulation') of the Streets and Buildings Regulations, as replaced by decree K.D.P. 400/2020 (Gazette 27 August 2020) for developments without a planning or building permit or application by 31 August 2020; the designer applies it, and the Fire Service may set other conditions when consulted (paras 1.3, 1.9). Alterations, additions or repairs to an existing licensed building must at least meet Chapter 7 (emergency evacuation) and use suitable products (Chapter 9) (para. 1.10). Shops need emergency lighting on escape routes, except ground-floor shops under 100 m2 of sales area with exits within 15 m (Table 33).

m-ea6181fa.t: Cyprus has one collective system for packaging, Green Dot (Cyprus) Public Co Ltd, which its FAQ calls 'the only Collective Compliance System for Packaging Waste in the country'. Its approval as posted on the Department of Environment's EPR page (No 2/2020/ΣΣ under K.D.P. 747/2003, signed by the Minister on 19 June 2020) states that it expires on 30 June 2026, and Green Dot's licence page says the same. As read on 6 October 2026, neither the Department's page (updated 29 September 2026) nor Green Dot's site posts a renewal, although Green Dot keeps operating and published member guidance on 2 October 2026.

m-e9aac0c4.t: Larnaca's Finance Department set the 2025 refuse fees, professional tax, fees for use/keeping of business premises, property tax and cemetery fee payable online (JCC Smart) by 29 December 2025 or in person at the citizen service centres of Larnaca, Livadia and Voroklini by 30 December 2025, after which an extra charge applies 'as the Municipal Regulations' provide; objections for 2025 closed on 28 November 2025 (announcement of 11 December 2025). On 26 February 2026 it said the final deadline for these 2025 fees was 27 February 2026, payable only at the citizen service centres. Neither notice gives amounts.

m-e51456b3.t: A Cyprus cafe selling alcohol needs a retail licence under the Sale of Intoxicating Liquors Law, Cap. 144, from the municipal council, or the District Officer outside municipalities (s. 2). Its Annex sets the yearly fee for a general retail licence for consumption on or off the premises at CY£80 inside a municipality, CY£50 elsewhere, and CY£200 where entertainment by artists with music or songs is offered (€136.68, €85.43, €341.72 in the portal's table); half is due for a licence granted after 13 September (s. 13(1)). A licence expires on the 12 March following issue (s. 11); an application not answered within two months of complete papers, extendable once, is deemed granted (s. 11A).

m-e3baf4f6.t: For premises needing planning permission (e.g. a café's change of use), the Interior Ministry's Manual of Planning Control (first revision, January 2025) lets the owner - registered or entitled to be registered - or his authorised representative apply (reg. 3(1)), through a designer the owner authorises, with a copy of his ETEK practising licence. Co-owners all sign or act by an authorised representative, signatures certified by a certifying officer or the designer; for a company owner all directors or persons authorised sign. Since 1 July 2024 applications are filed only online via IPPODAMOS (Limassol DLGO). Our inference: a tenant needs the landlord's authorisation and a designer.

m-e2f239b3.t: Two different bills on catering-premises licensing were before Cyprus's outgoing House in 2025-2026. The Government bill 'Ο περί της Ίδρυσης και Λειτουργίας Χώρων Εστίασης και Διασκέδασης Νόμος του 2025' (file 23.01.066.228-2025), tabled 9 October 2025, was withdrawn on 19 March 2026. A member's bill by MP Kyriakos Hadjiyiannis, 'Ο περί της Ίδρυσης και Λειτουργίας Χώρων Αναψυχής Νόμος του 2026' (file 23.02.067.054-2026), was tabled and sent to the Energy, Commerce, Industry and Tourism Committee on 26 March 2026; its vote was postponed on 2 April and the plenary passed it on 6 April 2026, per Nomoplatform's records read 6 October 2026. Ant1 reported 41 votes for and three abstentions.

m-e008a351.t: Besides the Greek lists on gov.cy, the Deputy Ministry of Tourism's portal visitcyprus.com carries editions of the district lists of catering and entertainment establishments that fall between them: for Nicosia, editions dated 02/10/2024, 22/10/2024, 15/01/2025, 08/04/2026, 13/05/2026 and 11/08/2026 were read there on 6 October 2026, and its 'Catering and Entertainment Establishments' page (modified 11 August 2026) links the 11/08/2026 Nicosia list and English June 2026 lists of the other districts. The English editions of 2025-2026 seen carry no licence-expiry column. A Limassol edition dated 06/11/2025 survives as a web-archive copy of a gov.cy file.

m-de80f13c.t: Yearly ceilings under the Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022 (Schedules read 6 October 2026), as we map the reader's cases (the council sets the category): a person trading in his own name from a shop, café or one-person office most plausibly fits the Fifth Schedule's 'traders ... and businessmen, working as individuals', up to €200 (a self-employed craftsman €50; unlisted €300), and owes no s. 56(6) fee, which falls on legal persons only. A private company with up to five employees: up to €150 for premises plus up to €1,000 under the Sixth Schedule (€4,000 if its registered office is with a law, accounting or audit firm). No floor-area criterion; a second-half-year start pays half.

m-cc79d991.t: The opening-hours rules of Cyprus's Shops Law (Part IV of Law 155(I)/2006) bind only shops in municipal areas (except Pano Lefkara), in communities bordering a municipality (26 listed communities excepted) and in seven named communities (s. 3(1)); its employment rules (Parts I-III, V) apply to all shops. Part IV does not apply to restaurants and leisure premises as to service on the premises, to shops selling only drinks and ready food prepared there for consumption elsewhere, to pharmacies and petrol stations, among others (s. 3(2)). cylaw text to Law 65(I)/2020, read 6 October 2026.

m-caacc06c.t: A Cyprus trader selling goods to consumers must show the selling price and the unit price (per kg, litre, metre, m2 or m3, or per item) including VAT and all taxes, in euro, clearly and legibly, on the goods, the packaging or the shelf; where goods in a shop are not within the customer's reach a price list must be displayed (ss. 42, 44 of the Consumer Protection Law 112(I)/2021). Advertisements that state a price give the unit price too (s. 43). Any announced price reduction must state the earlier price - the lowest in the 30 days before the reduction, except for goods that perish or expire quickly or have been on the market under 30 days (s. 45(2)). Read 6 October 2026.

m-c71c5894.t: Batteries, also those built into appliances: the Department of Environment's 2026 application for its register of battery producers (file modified 20 March 2026, read 6 October 2026) rests on reg. 18(2) of the Waste (Batteries and Accumulators) Regulations K.D.P. 125/2009 to K.D.P. 201/2021 and on Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, whose waste-battery chapter (arts 54-76, incl. producer register and responsibility) applies from 18 August 2025 (art. 96(2)(c)). A producer includes a Cyprus firm first supplying batteries brought from abroad and a distance seller from abroad; the form asks whether sales include distance selling and yields a compliance certificate for 2026.

m-c40a3992.t: Cyprus's Catering Establishments Law 29/1985 (cylaw text to Law 170(I)/2020; in force on 6 October 2026; its 2026 replacement was referred by the President to the court, per press) fixes three points of a café's order: the operator applies for classification and licence before operation starts (s. 6(2)); the licence issues on a sanitary certificate, the fee and the legal conditions (s. 6(3)); none issues for premises the certificate of final approval under the Streets and Buildings Regulation Laws deems unsuitable (s. 6(7)). Plans of a new or altered establishment go to the Deputy Ministry after the planning permit, filed by the site or building owner (form F-KEN-01/1).

m-c3d3cddb.t: A Cyprus planning application for a night club, beer hall, bar, music or dance centre or hall, discotheque, cinema, theatre, gym, swimming pool and similar uses (unless incidental to a home, school or hospital) must be advertised beforehand in at least two daily newspapers in the Minister's form, and the application must carry the signer's declaration that the notice was published and proof of it (K.D.P. 62/2016, reg. 5(1)-(3)(δ)). For these categories the planning authority must also consult any local authority that may be affected (reg. 7(1)(α)). A cafeteria or restaurant without music is not named, though reg. 5(3)(ιβ) lets the authority add any development. Read 6 October 2026.

m-bfb1af09.t: Cyprus's Ministry of Health keeps a register of food business establishments under the Director of Medical and Public Health Services, citing Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and national food hygiene regulations of 2006-2011. Its application form (T-Φ-032A/7, English version posted July 2025) is filed at the Public Health Services district office where the establishment is, by a natural person (two copies of his identity document) or a company (two copies of its certificate of incorporation); it asks for the activities, among them 'online sales' with the website's address, and names no fee and no time limit. Whether premises under a municipal health service file it too is not stated.

m-bd0d54df.t: A Cyprus trader who provides services to consumers in a shop must post a price list of its main services showing final prices including VAT and all taxes (or the price per unit where the charge depends on time, distance, weight or volume), visibly inside the shop and, where technically feasible, also on its front. Sectors whose price information is set by special legislation, and services whose nature does not allow prices fixed in advance, are exempt (s. 47 of the Consumer Protection Law 112(I)/2021; Part VI covers services as well as goods, s. 40(1)). Read 6 October 2026.

m-bcb8cd7a.t: Since 1 July 2024 applications for planning permission and building permits are filed only electronically in the IPPODAMOS system, by a designer (architect or civil engineer) the owner engages, with a verified CY Login profile, per the FAQs of the Famagusta and Larnaca district Local Government Organisations (read 6 October 2026). The fees, set by regulations, are computed in IPPODAMOS by type and intensity of development and paid only electronically there; the one refund case the FAQs name is a hierarchical appeal accepted by the competent Ministerial Committee. Asked whether a planning application can be expedited, the Famagusta FAQ answers: 'No. There is no such procedure.'

m-bc265643.t: Why a Nicosia business's municipal charges could differ in 2025: announcing on 23 June 2025 that refuse-fee bills for residential premises and then the professional fees and charges would soon be sent, Nicosia Municipality said the fees were fixed by equating the existing categories of its municipal districts into single categories for the whole Municipality, so that sums charged that year might rise or fall against the previous year's 'with the aim of observing the principles of equality and proportionality'. It gave no amounts in the announcement.

m-bc1267e8.t: Cyprus's Waste (Management of Non-Packaging Paper Waste) Regulations K.D.P. 430/2017 make a 'producer' of anyone who, in business, first places non-packaging paper on the Cyprus market (packaging, toilet paper and napkins are excluded; reselling paper already on the Cyprus market does not make one a producer). Producers must join a collective system or run an approved individual one (reg. 5(2)), show the Cyprus Ports Authority proof of it before such products leave the port (reg. 16(1)), and enter the register of producers, filing an annual report by 31 March each year (reg. 18(1)); distributors may not deal with producers lacking a participation certificate (reg. 16(3)).

m-ba6a88f6.t: Per Green Dot Cyprus, the packaging scheme, on its own pages (read 6 October 2026; questions page dated 14 February 2023), the obligated company is the one that first places packaged products on the Cyprus market - the first producer or importer. It lists firms packing goods for trade (neutral or own-label packaging), importing packaged goods to trade or for own use (raw materials, spare parts), retailers packing own-label goods, users of 'facilitation' packaging such as carrier bags, wrapping paper or pizza boxes, and givers of free samples; exports are outside. Obligated firms report yearly to the Department of Environment the packaging mass placed on the market and proof of recovery.

m-b4dedcf7.t: Nicosia's council on 22 January 2026 unanimously approved a memo of 8 December 2025 on 'Refuse fees - professional licence fees - fees for keeping/using business premises - immovable property fee for 2026', attached to the agenda, with changes to refuse discounts; it also added €100,000 to the budgeted revenue from business premises. The ratified minutes do not reproduce the amounts, and the agenda page carries no attachments. In the debate Engomi's deputy mayor Panikos Konstantinou said that in charging business premises, both refuse and professional-licence invoices had overcharged Engomi and Ayios Dometios and undercharged Nicosia proper, and that corrections must be made at once.

m-b277b906.t: Under Cyprus's Catering Establishments (Sound Emission Licences) Law 50(I)/2016 (as amended to 2021; read 6 Oct 2026), a catering establishment sited where it causes or may cause noise nuisance to nearby homes may not emit sound beyond its plot unless its owner first obtains a sound emission licence from the municipality, or the District Officer outside municipalities, unless a ministerial decree names another body (ss. 2, 3(1)). The owner posts a 15-day notice of intent; neighbours may object within 15 days after; the application has the planning and/or building permit and the operating licence. It is issued within one month of a complete application and runs up to three years (s. 3(9)).

m-afb19543.t: Per the Department of Environment's EEE-register application form (file named 2022, read 6 October 2026), a producer is: a firm established in Cyprus that makes EEE, or has it designed or made, and markets it under its own name or brand; one that resells under its own name or brand equipment made by others; one that professionally imports EEE from a third country or another Member State and places it on the Cyprus market; or a distance seller established abroad selling to users in Cyprus. The form adds that the reseller 'is not considered a producer' where the maker's name or brand appears on the equipment.

m-ab7907f8.t: Cyprus's Services Law 76(I)/2010 (transposing Directive 2006/123/EC; no amendments in cylaw's history, text read 6 October 2026) requires licensing procedures and formalities to be clear, made public in advance and easily accessible, and any charges on applicants to be reasonable, proportionate to and not above the cost of the procedure (s. 13(1)-(2)). Section 45(1) of the Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022 refers only to s. 13(3) of that Law; whether s. 13(1)-(2) binds a municipality's s. 56 premises licence for every kind of business, neither text says.

m-aa713d95.t: Section 45(1) of Cyprus's Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022 opens 'without prejudice to' s. 13(3) of the Services Law 76(I)/2010 (cylaw text read 6 October 2026). That provision sets a default three-month limit from submission of all required documents unless a special law sets another, and lets the competent authority extend it once, for a limited period, with reasons notified to the applicant before the original limit expires; s. 13(4)-(7) add the deemed grant, the acknowledgement of receipt, notice of missing documents and notice of rejection. Whether a municipality may use that single extension against its own four months, neither text says expressly.

m-a5be9d40.t: On submission, both of Paphos's PafosNow premises-licence forms (read 6 October 2026) are set to e-mail a 'confirmation of receipt': 'Your application has been received successfully. A copy of your application is attached. On completion of processing you will be informed of the result by e-mail', with phones 26822570 and 99647737. As configured, it states no time limit, no remedies and nothing about a deemed grant - the three items s. 45(3) of Law 52(I)/2022 requires in an acknowledgement of receipt. Paphos's 2022 citizens' guide (under the repealed 1985 Law) said an officer of the Technical Services tells the applicant the result; neither source prints a fee for the premises licence.

m-a2faa7f6.t: Fees for a Cyprus planning application are fixed by the Town and Country Planning (Fees) Regulations 2013 (K.D.P. 29/2013), paid on submission (reg. 3(1)). For restaurants, catering and entertainment establishments (κέντρα αναψυχής), discotheques, beer halls and the like (Table para. 3) - and for shops and offices, which pay 'as in para. 3(a)-(c)' (para. 4) - the fee is EUR 125 per 40 m2 of covered space or part for new development; EUR 80 plus EUR 90 per 40 m2 (or part) of added space for alterations or additions that add covered space; EUR 110 for alterations without added space. A change of use pays the fee set for the new use (para. 32). Read 6 October 2026.

m-9d5c9452.t: Larnaca Municipality's FAQ (undated, read 6 October 2026) publishes a uniform business fee for legal persons whose registered office or management is with law, accounting or audit firms or administrative-service offices: EUR 150 for an active legal person in a group, EUR 250 for one not in a group, nothing for a dormant one (on an auditor's certificate, or an accountant's or lawyer's if it has no accounts). The premises fee is paid by only one legal person per premises, and by none other where a licensed administrative-service provider pays it. The page cites the repealed 1985 Municipalities Law; its line that only companies pay 'professional tax' conflicts with s. 56(5) of Law 52(I)/2022.

m-9bef0991.t: The portable-battery collective system is AFIS Cyprus Ltd (ΑΦΗΣ ΚΥΠΡΟΣ ΛΤΔ): the Minister's approval No 1/2025/ΣΣ, posted on the Department of Environment's EPR page, runs to 31 August 2031. The Department's register of battery producers (spreadsheet dated 2023, modified 15 February 2023) lists 291 companies: 288 in the AFIS collective system and three, all lead-acid battery sellers, marked 'not applicable'. No later register is linked on the page (read 6 October 2026).

m-98cc3086.t: Per Ant1's report of the plenary vote of 6 April 2026 (press; the passed text is not published), Cyprus's leisure-premises law as passed sets other opening hours than the bill as tabled: 'Catering and Leisure' premises and bars may open 7.00-2.30 Monday-Thursday and Sunday and 7.00-3.30 Friday-Saturday from May to September, to 2.00 and 3.00 from October to April, and the District Officer may extend or cut hours by special licence for up to six months at a time. The tabled s. 19 had 6.00-3.30 (bars 8.00-3.30) all year. The 18-month period for new premises and the three-year special licence, renewable twice, for unlicensed premises that Ant1 also reports were already in the tabled s. 14.

m-98c042b2.t: Paphos Municipality extended again, to 30 January 2026, the payment of its 2025 refuse fee on homes and business premises, of the 'right on business premises for the exercise of business (professional tax)' and of the trade or profession fee (announcement of 30 December 2025, read 6 October 2026). Bills are paid only through the municipality's website, www.pafos.org.cy; after the new deadline a 10% surcharge is added. Queries go to its Finance Department (26950572) or Citizen Service Centre (26623420 / 427). No amounts are given.

m-93c572fd.t: Under the Electricity Law (Cap. 170, cylaw text read 6 October 2026) the Council of Ministers may empower the Director of Electrical and Mechanical Services (EMS), another person or a board to examine, license and register electrical engineers, senior technicians, appliance maintainers, electricians and installation contractors, certify them, and strike off those in breach (s. 12); regulations set qualifications and fees (s. 10(1)(ε)-(η)). EMS forms 58.18-1 and 60.18-1 ask the designer and the contractor for an EMS register number and a kVA responsibility limit; that a founder without such registration cannot sign them is an inference from the forms.

m-8f18f78f.t: A Cyprus draft law would let owners regularise buildings finished without a building permit - which a cafe over 50 m2 must show for its municipal licence (s. 55(2)(α) Law 52(I)/2022). The Interior Ministry's draft Streets and Buildings Regulation (Amendment) (No. 2) Law of 2026, prepared with ETEK and put to consultation on 18 March 2026 (comments by 20 April), adds a s. 4Δ: designers' studies and inspection certificates, and fire and accessibility rules 'as far as feasible', lead to a permit, a certificate of approval with notes and a note on the title deed; fees under reg. 62 are doubled; the window is 18 or 36 months. Status on 6 October 2026: draft, 'under processing'; not in Cap. 96.

m-8c78b24d.t: Under s. 55(1) of Cyprus's Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022 a prior municipal licence is needed not only for a restaurant, tavern, snack bar, cafeteria or pizzeria over 50 m2 (s. 55(1)(γ)) but for any building or space, of any size, used for a theatrical, dance, cinema or music performance, any cultural, social, entertainment or sports activity, or any public spectacle (s. 55(1)(α)), and for music-and-dance venues, discotheques, cabarets, beer halls and bars over 50 m2 (s. 55(1)(β)). Every s. 55 licence needs the same certificates, the Fire Service's among them (s. 55(2)), and covers one performance or a period of up to three years (s. 55(3)). Read 6 October 2026.

m-88ff3d16.t: Every licence a Cyprus municipality issues under the Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022 - including the premises licence of a shop or a small cafe without performances (s. 56) and of a restaurant or cafe over 50 m² (s. 55(1)(γ)) - is examined within four months of receipt of all required documents; if the municipality does not answer in that time 'the licence is deemed to have been granted', and the acknowledgement of receipt must say so (s. 45(1)-(3)). A s. 56 licence must conform to the Town and Country Planning Law and the Streets and Buildings Regulation Law (s. 56(2)(α)); keeping premises without it is punishable by a fine of up to €500 (s. 56(3)). Read 6 October 2026.

m-86c412a2.t: The Packaging Regulation (EU) 2025/40, in force since 11 February 2025, applies from 12 August 2026 (art. 71). A 'producer' is a manufacturer, importer or distributor that first makes packaging or packaged products available in its own Member State, or directly to end users in another, by any sales method, or unpacks packaged goods without being the end user (art. 3(1)(15)). Producers must register in each State where they do so and may not sell unregistered; a producer responsibility organisation they entrust registers unless the State says otherwise (art. 44(2), (4)). Cross-border sellers appoint an authorised representative (art. 45(3)); platforms get sellers' numbers (art. 45(4)).

m-81e77c66.t: The Deputy Ministry of Tourism publishes lists of recreation centres (catering and entertainment venues), one PDF per district: on gov.cy (posted 22 June 2026, topic 'Αδειοδότηση Κέντρων Αναψυχής και Εστίασης') lists dated 19/06/2026; on its portal visitcyprus.com English editions, the newest seen a Nicosia list dated 11/08/2026. Entries give trade name, category (restaurant, tavern, cafeteria, snack bar, bar and others), address and mostly a telephone. Greek editions from 06/11/2025 and the Pafos list of 19/06/2026 add a licence-expiry column, blank for some rows; older and English 2025-2026 editions lack it. None seen (6 October 2026) names a holder or gives a licence number or issue date.

m-805d3759.t: For a shop selling consumer products online, the EU General Product Safety Regulation (EU) 2023/988 applies from 13 December 2024 (art. 52). A product may be placed on the market only if an economic operator established in the EU is responsible for it (art. 16(1)); its name and postal and electronic address go on the product, its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document (art. 16(3)). Each online offer must show the manufacturer's name and postal and electronic address, the EU responsible person where the manufacturer is outside the EU, a picture and type or other identifier of the product, and warnings or safety information in a language consumers understand easily (art. 19).

m-7ecdebe8.t: Two municipal forms for outdoor tables on public space, read 6 October 2026: Limassol (PDF of October 2025) asks for the building permit with permitted and current use, a cadastral plan, floor plans, the lease if any, and an identity card or passport - for a company its certificates of incorporation, directors and shareholders and the director's ID or passport; Nicosia (scan of 24 February 2026) asks for the applicant's identity-card number (no passport field), planning and building permit numbers, a survey plan or photos of the area and photos of the tables, chairs and umbrellas, and a declaration that the applicant is the tenant and director of the business. Neither states a fee or a time.

m-7d7f2562.t: Four Cyprus texts give the catering licence's term, as read on 6 October 2026. The Catering Establishments Law 29/1985, s. 6(4) as replaced by Law 170(I)/2020: the licence 'expires every three (3) years from the date of its issue' and may be renewed on payment of the fee; the Deputy Ministry of Tourism's guidance on operators' duties (PDF of 31 March 2021, posted on its gov.cy site 28 May 2024) repeats three years. The Regulations of 1986-2005 (reg. 5(3) and the licence form in their First Table, read in an archived consolidation), not amended to match, still say one year to 31 December, and the business portal (updated 18 September 2026) follows them: 'valid for maximum for one year'.

m-7cbff0bd.t: Outdoor tables on a pedestrian street in a Cyprus municipality need a licence or sub-licence of use from the municipality under s. 44(1)(ιδ) of the Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022 (as substituted by Law 87(I)/2024), which may be granted 'also for the purposes of outdoor dining'. The council decides which premises uses and streets qualify, the procedure, forms and documents (including a reasoned report or a proposal on drawings), and may impose conditions on hours, exact space, equipment, the type and colour of the furniture, and free passage for pedestrians, disabled persons and emergency vehicles. Fees are left to the council (s. 46(α)). Read 6 October 2026.

m-7a4a0e6d.t: Under s. 25(1) of the ETEK Law 224/1990 (cylaw text through Law 33(I)/2026, read 6 October 2026) no one in Cyprus may practise a branch of engineering unless registered in that branch's ETEK register, holding ETEK's annual licence and having the Greek needed; ETEK special-list licensees (e.g. licensed building technicians) may do limited work, on buildings of up to two floors and set volumes (s. 25(6)-(7)). Unlicensed practice is an offence (s. 25(4)); only a registered person may charge for engineering services (s. 25(5)). A study company may file plans under the Streets and Buildings Regulation Law only if signed by the licensed person who prepared them (s. 6Δ(2)).

m-794c87b9.t: The certificates a Cyprus municipality requires before licensing a café or restaurant over 50 m² (Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022 s. 55(1)(γ), in force on 6 October 2026) are issued by public officers (s. 55(2)): safety of premises, fittings, lighting and ventilation by the Municipal Engineer, or where there is none the Public Works Director; the electrical installation by the Director of Electrical and Mechanical Services or his representative; fire prevention and escape by the head of the Fire Service in the municipality; the facilities by the municipal health service. A building permit is also required. Hired professionals prepare part of what the officers check.

m-76f54afa.t: Per a Green Dot Cyprus news item of 15 April 2026, Temu signed agreements with Green Dot Cyprus (packaging), AFIS Cyprus (batteries) and WEEE Cyprus (electrical and electronic equipment) that set up a process to help sellers on Temu meet their extended-producer-responsibility obligations in Cyprus; the terms were not published. The item quotes a Department of Environment officer that Temu, 'as an online platform falling within the scope of the EU Regulation on packaging and packaging waste', lets Cypriot consumers contract at a distance with sellers, whom she calls producers. Green Dot itself operates AFIS Cyprus and WEEE Cyprus, per its own overview page.

m-745daaac.t: The Cyprus Fire Service's page 'Αρμοδιότητες' (published 4 June 2026) describes its role in building licensing: the building authorities send plans through IPPODAMOS to its Fire Protection Department, whose conditions on escape and fire measures go into the planning or building permit; after completion its views are sought again for an inspection towards the certificate of approval and/or of suitability; and it may inspect any premises at the authority's request or on its own motion. Its Fire Protection Department page says views for a building permit are obtained 'ONLY through' the EOAs of all districts. Neither page describes a fire certificate a business applies for, or a fee or time.

m-7225ea1a.t: Breaching s. 9(1) of Cyprus's Packaging Law 32(I)/2002 (who bears packaging-waste costs), the other duties s. 26 lists (packaging requirements, marking, carrier-bag data) or the regulations and orders under the Law is a criminal offence carrying up to three years' imprisonment or a fine up to €85,500, or both (s. 26); a director or manager whose consent, connivance or tolerance is proved can be prosecuted with the company. Inspectors may settle out of court for up to €3,400, doubled if the breach is repeated or not ended within 48 hours of the notice, each further day then being a new offence for court; otherwise paying within 14 days bars prosecution (s. 26A). Read 6 October 2026.

m-71586bfd.t: Limassol's 'Methodology for imposing fees and charges for 2026' (read 6 October 2026) says the professional tax was imposed under s. 56(6) of Law 52(I)/2022 'and values as stated in the Sixth Schedule', and the charge for using business premises under s. 56(5) 'and values as stated in the Fifth Schedule'; it prints no amounts for either. It sets its own household refuse fees (€158 to €243). Objections are accepted only before the due date printed on the invoice: by hand at Arch. Kyprianou 23 or at the Mesa Geitonia district office (Griva Digeni 14), by post to P.O. Box 50089, 3600 Limassol, or by e-mail to taxes@limassol.org.cy.

m-71378c09.t: Under s. 45 of Cyprus's Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022 (s. 45 unamended since enactment; cylaw text read 6 October 2026) a municipality examines any licence application within four months 'from the time of receipt of all the required documents'; if it is incomplete, the applicant is told without delay of the need for supplementary documents and of the possible effects on that deadline (s. 45(1) proviso). It may ask to see originals of documents issued by another authority (s. 45(4)). Where criteria, conditions or fees are left to the council's discretion, it publishes its decision at least one month ahead on its notice board and/or official website (s. 45(5)).

m-71106a37.t: Under Cyprus's Delegation of Powers Order 2026 (K.D.P. 350/2026, Gazette 25 September 2026, replacing K.D.P. 307/2024, same rows for these uses), planning applications for cafeterias, restaurants and bars (row A.10) and for shops up to 1,500 m2 (A.29) are decided by the Head of the Planning Licensing Sector of the district EOA; shops over 1,500 m2 by the EOA Director of Licensing; organised shopping centres, complex commercial developments and out-of-zone hypermarkets by the Town Planning Director. A change of use follows the new use (B.1). If the local authority objected with reasons, the EOA official needs the EOA Council's consent, failing which the Council decides (para. 10).

m-706c6236.t: Under reg. 22(2) of Cyprus's WEEE Regulations K.D.P. 73/2015, the Department of Environment's Director ensures that a producer established in Cyprus that sells electrical or electronic equipment at a distance into another Member State appoints there an authorised representative responsible for its producer obligations, by written mandate (reg. 22(3)); under the proviso to reg. 21(1), distance sellers register in the Member State of sale through such representatives unless already registered there. The EU duty behind it (Directive 2012/19/EU art. 17(2)) is the subject of a suspension proposal not adopted as of 20 September 2026.

m-6ec7826c.t: The government business portal lists three conditions on which Cyprus's catering licence 'can be granted only': the operator is resident in Cyprus, an EU citizen or a legal person situated in an EU state; 'The planning permit and building permit for the specific use have been obtained'; and 'The manager of the catering and entertainment establishment must be approved by the Deputy Ministry of Tourism' (catering page, updated 18 September 2026, read 6 October 2026). The portal cites no section of Law 29/1985 for them; the Deputy Ministry's procedure sheet of December 2018 likewise issues the licence only on the issued building or change-of-use permit.

m-6c783500.t: A Cyprus planning authority must promptly tell the applicant the date of receipt and the decision deadline, and give written notice of its decision (or referral to the Minister) within three months of receipt or a longer period agreed in writing (Town and Country Planning (Applications and Hierarchical Appeals) Regulations 2016, K.D.P. 62/2016, reg. 6(1)-(2)). Silence is not a grant: under s. 32 of Law 90/1972 the applicant may then appeal to the Council of Ministers as if refused, within 30 days of the missed deadline (reg. 8(2)). Bodies it must consult get at least 21 days' notice before examination, unless another law sets other limits (reg. 7(4)). Read 6 October 2026.

m-67cf73b1.t: No regulation fixes a fee for the sound emission licence of a Cyprus catering establishment: Law 50(I)/2016 leaves the fees to regulations (ss. 3(9)(α), 13) and cylaw's indexes to K.D.P. 372/2026 hold none. The draft Catering Establishments (Sound Emission Licences and Fees) Regulations 2021 - EUR 95 to apply, EUR 125 on issue, yearly renewal for EUR 95 plus EUR 125 - were tabled on 16 September 2021, withdrawn on 2 December 2022 and re-tabled on 19 January 2023; Nomoplatform lists them as pending as of 6 October 2026. Its summary says fees are needed because collecting them 'has not happened so far', to cover the cost of licensing and enforcement.

m-626cc214.t: Where placing an advertising sign needs planning permission in Cyprus, the planning fee is EUR 100 (Town and Country Planning (Fees) Regulations 2013, K.D.P. 29/2013, Table para. 34; unchanged by the only amendment, K.D.P. 249/2015). This is the planning fee alone; any municipal sign licence or fee is separate. Read 6 October 2026.

m-607b7eca.t: Cyprus's building-permit fees are set in regulation 62 and Annex II of the Streets and Buildings Regulations, a system the Interior Ministry calls 'complex'. Its draft amending Regulations of 2026, put to public consultation on 8 February 2026, would replace them with flat rates per m2 of covered space: EUR 10 for commercial use and offices and for leisure and entertainment, EUR 3.50 residential; alterations, additions and changes of use by the area affected, at least EUR 100; a certificate of approval 5% of the permit fee, at least EUR 150. As of 6 October 2026 it is a proposal: the consultation is marked 'under processing' and no such Regulations are in cylaw's 2026 index.

m-5b11dff1.t: Paphos Municipality's practice when the sound-emission rules were reissued in 2022, per its notice of 26 September 2022: after the Sound Classification Decree K.D.P. 263/2022 and the Interior Minister's Order K.D.P. 264/2022 took effect on 1 July 2022, it called every catering establishment emitting sound to apply online, attaching the Deputy Ministry of Tourism operating licence, the municipal premises licence, the planning and building permits and a copy of the notice of intent; an acoustic study was added for sound after midnight or next to housing. Licences ran only to 31 December 2022 and 'no fees will be paid' for them.

m-553641ad.t: Nicosia's form for a reduction of business-premises fees (Word file created 27 January 2026, read 6 October 2026) asks for a reduced invoice and review 'on the basis of the criteria decided by the Municipal Council', against a declaration and attachments: evidence of reduced turnover (VAT returns, number of employees and the like), certificates that a company is dormant or struck off, or other supporting documents. Objections may be filed online, by e-mail to taxes@nicosia.org.cy, or at the municipality's citizen service offices; information on 22797000. The criteria themselves are not printed on the form.

m-4b405a97.t: Where the hours rules of Law 155(I)/2006 apply (see its s. 3), a general shop may not open before 5:00 and must close by 19:30 on weekdays in winter (1 November-31 March) and 20:00 in summer (1 April-31 October), by 15:00 on Wednesdays, and by 19:00 (winter) or 19:30 (summer) on Saturdays; it stays shut on Sundays (s. 20; cylaw text to Law 65(I)/2020, read 6 October 2026). Exceptions: December (daily to 20:00), the ten days before Easter, special shops such as bakeries, kiosks and off-licences (s. 21), and shops in tourist zones fixed by ministerial decree (s. 27). Breach by the shopkeeper: up to a year's imprisonment, a EUR 30,000 fine, or both (s. 30(1)).

m-48437523.t: Per WEEE Cyprus's own news item (read 6 October 2026), on 26 November 2025 it received authorisation from the Cyprus authorities to manage waste photovoltaic panels on behalf of its members, and members importing photovoltaic panels were asked to sign an amendment to their agreement. The licence the item links is page 1 of the 2020 licence No 1/2020/ΣΣ, which states expiry on 30 June 2026; no later licence document is linked there.

m-44eb71e9.t: Some goods need a licence before they are sold, per the government business portal (read 6 October 2026): alcoholic drinks need a retailer's or dealer's licence for the sale of intoxicating liquors, and tobacco products a licence for their sale, each from the municipality where the premises are or else the District Officer (tobacco: €51.25 plus €0.85 stamp duty, valid to the next 12 March); food supplements need a notification to, or for some products a licence from, the Director of Medical and Public Health Services, Ministry of Health. The portal's 'Wholesale and Retail Trade' category lists 25 activity pages, from optical stores to firearms; not all impose a licence (cosmetics: none).

m-41e15609.t: For electrical and electronic equipment the Department of Environment's EPR page (footer: last updated 29 September 2026) links one collective-system licence, No 1/2020/ΣΣ for WEEE (CYPRUS) LTD, signed 19 June 2020, stating 'Expiry date of the licence: 30/6/2026'; no renewal is posted there or on WEEE Cyprus's own site, which links the same 2020 licence (read 6 October 2026). The page's text calls the system approved in 2009 'WEEE Electrocyclosis Cyprus Ltd'. Its national register of EEE producers (PDF created 21 February 2022) has 457 numbered rows: 456 marked as WEEE Cyprus members and one individual system; one company is listed twice, so 456 distinct names.

m-41798010.t: Nicosia Municipality's licence table for a 'κέντρο αναψυχής' (PDF of 12 September 2024, read 6 October 2026) lists: planning permit, building permit and final-approval certificate from the EOA, once each; food-business registration with the Ministry of Health, once; health certificate, yearly; liquor licence (municipality or District Officer), yearly, expiring 12 March; loudspeaker licence, yearly, needing the s. 55 licence; s. 55 licence, up to 3 years; Deputy Ministry of Tourism licence, 3 years if the health certificate and s. 55 licence are renewed. The planning permit goes to the Deputy Ministry for classification and stamping of plans before the building-permit application.

m-40de5eeb.t: Cyprus's General Development Order 2024 (K.D.P. 181/2024, Gazette 10 May 2024) lets a building used for a purpose in use classes I-VIII of its Second Annex be used for another purpose of the same class without planning permission (para. 5(1)), unless a permit condition bars it (para. 5(3)). Class I is 'shop', excluding hot-food shops, car showrooms and kiosks; class III is 'restaurant without music, cafeteria'. A hot-food shop, car showroom or pet shop may also become any shop (First Annex, category V). Nothing exempts a shop becoming a cafe. Para. 6 ties commencement to a Gazette notice none was found, but ETEK and the EOAs apply it from 10 May 2024. Read 6 October 2026.

m-40b2fc34.t: For a new or altered café building the business portal (catering page updated 18 September 2026, read 6 October 2026) sets an order and puts the first three steps on the owner of the site, not the operator: the owner submits plans to the Planning Authority for planning permission; then the plans with the permit to the Deputy Ministry of Tourism for approval; then the approved plans to the local authority for the building permit. At least one month before opening, the operator applies to the Ministry for classification and licensing, with the title deed, the 'Property Owner's Solemn Declaration', the proposed manager's details, a health certificate and the planning permit for the use.

m-3e06687e.t: Cyprus applies the GPSR through the General Product Safety Law 116(I)/2025 (Gazette No 5045, 4 July 2025), repealing the 2004-2010 laws. Its competent authority is the Consumer Protection Service (Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry) or, for products under EU harmonisation legislation, the authority named for each product (s. 2). It may fine a breach of the Law or the Regulation up to €30,000, a later breach up to €60,000, and €500 a day while a fined breach continues (ss. 17-18); making a seriously dangerous product available or giving the authority false or misleading information carries up to two years' imprisonment or €100,000, or both, on first conviction (s. 21).

m-3d8ca7e1.t: Under Cap. 50 (Display of Advertisements (Control) Law) s. 6(3), a Cyprus business needs no council approval for a 'point of sale' sign about the business carried on in the building if it is fixed to that building, not hung across the street, does not project over it unless at least 12 feet up (then by at most 2 feet), with other such signs covers no more than one fifth of the facade up to 15 feet, and is at most 15 feet above ground. Signs inside a ground-floor shop window are outside the Law (s. 3(1)(e)). Other signs need approval, to be decided within four months of complete papers; silence does 'not' grant the licence (s. 10, as substituted by Law 70(I)/2012).

m-3aa692f5.t: Cyprus's Sale of Intoxicating Liquors Law, Cap. 144 (consolidated text read 6 October 2026) does not tie a retail liquor licence to a legal form, nationality or residence: its full text names no condition on companies, legal persons, nationality or residence, and under the Interpretation Law, Cap. 1, s. 2, 'person' includes a company or other body of persons with or without legal personality. Of the applicant it requires, before grant, that he is 'of good character', shown by a Chief of Police certificate of no conviction for listed offences, and a 'fit person' (s. 5(α)); the premises must also be suitable (s. 5(β)). The Law does not say how a company shows good character.

m-3a5de0fc.t: A member's bill tabled in the Cyprus House on 23 October 2025 (file 23.02.066.195-2025, Kyriakos Hadjiyiannis, MP for Famagusta) would make every sound emission licence of a catering establishment run three years instead of 'not exceeding three years' (Law 50(I)/2016, s. 3(9)(στ)); its memorandum calls this 'a chronic issue' for businesses renewing licences 'most often issued with a short validity'. Nomoplatform still shows it pending in the Interior Committee on 6 October 2026 with no discussion recorded, but House rule 84B deems such bills withdrawn when a new term starts if discussion had not begun or the proposer was not re-elected, so after the May 2026 elections it has probably lapsed.

m-37bb27a4.t: The building permit for a Cyprus cafe or shop is issued by the 'competent authority', which the Streets and Buildings Regulation Law (Cap. 96, s. 2; cylaw text to Law 23(I)/2026, read 6 October 2026) defines as the Director of Development Licensing of each district Local Government Organisation (EOA), not the municipality. The consolidated Law, scanned for day and month limits, sets no time for deciding an application. An owner who does not apply for a certificate of approval within 21 days of finishing the work gets a notice, and a fine of up to EUR 5,000 only if he does not remedy it in time (s. 21(1)(δ), (2)). A stale Larnaca Municipality FAQ still claims the permit and a 3-month limit.

m-37b05320.t: Infringing Cyprus's Consumer Protection Law 112(I)/2021, which carries the distance-selling rules, can cost a trader up to 5% of its turnover in the year immediately before the infringement, or up to EUR 3,000,000 where turnover information is not available: the Director of the Consumer Protection Service imposes this fine by reasoned decision after hearing the trader (s. 57(1)(ια)), and may add up to EUR 5,000 a day while an infringement continues (s. 57(1)(ιβ)). The fine is payable at once; recourse to the Minister or the court does not suspend collection (s. 61(1)). Read 6 October 2026, text consolidated to Law 122(I)/2026.

m-370039ee.t: Larnaca Municipality's form for a licence to use or keep business premises (one-page scan of 14 January 2026, listed under applications to the Hygiene Service as 'Application for a license for business premises 2026-27', read 6 October 2026) is addressed to the Mayor and Council for 01/01/2026-31/12/2026 and asks only for a central-register number and date, the applicant's name, ID-card number, address, phone and e-mail, and the premises' name, use, address and phone, with a signature. It lists no attachments and states no fee or decision time; a note says the application is passed to the Larnaca Police Directorate and the District Fire Stations officer.

m-35c086c8.t: A shop that imports cosmetics from outside the EU - Korean skincare, say - is the 'responsible person' for each product it imports, unless it designates another EU-established person by written mandate (art. 4(5) of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009); the responsible person must, before placing the product on the market, submit by electronic means to the Commission its category and name, the responsible person's address, the country of origin, the Member State of sale and other data (art. 13(1)). Cyprus's business portal says 'Selling Cosmetics' needs no specific licence (page last updated 29 July 2020, read 6 October 2026) and does not mention this notification.

m-34d39bd1.t: Some businesses need a regulator's consent before a Cyprus company can be registered. The Registrar of Companies' page 'Objects' (read 6 October 2026) lists the nature of business for which permission, consent or pre-approval is filed with the name application or the incorporation: medical and dental services (the Medical and Dental Councils), legal services (Law Office of the Republic), administrative services (CySEC or the Law Office), investment funds and their managers (CySEC), credit, payment, e-money and exchange services (Central Bank), higher education, casinos, radio and television, insurance (Superintendent of Insurance) and wine production.

m-314191d5.t: What Paphos treats as obligatory in a s. 56 premises-licence application, per the '[ΣΗΜΑΝΤΙΚΟ]' note on its two PafosNow forms (read 6 October 2026): for a natural person, the identity card (both sides), the building permit and the certificate of final approval must be attached; for a company, the identity card, the building permit, the certificate of incorporation, the certificate of directors and shareholders and the certificate of final approval. A shop or kiosk must also attach a photo of its front. The company form adds the company name, registration number and a legal representative (name, capacity, ID or passport, address), offers eight uploads and requires at least four files.

m-2ff05601.t: Per Phileleftheros, as summarised by the legal portal Dikaiosyni on 28 April 2026, Cyprus's President referred the leisure-premises law passed on 6 April 2026 to the court after the Legal Service found that 'a number of its provisions' conflict with the Constitution; neither names the provisions, and no Presidency statement of grounds or reference text was found on 6 October 2026. On 8 June 2026 the owners' association PASIKA said (via the Cyprus News Agency) that no issue of unconstitutionality 'so clear' arises 'as to justify' a reference instead of a return to the House, and that the President had used up his constitutional time, so a return to the dissolved House was no longer possible.

m-2fe1dbca.t: Nicosia Municipality's guidance table for the premises licence of a 'κέντρο αναψυχής' (PDF of 12 September 2024, served 6 October 2026) says: the Fire Service inspects by appointment with the manager and issues a fire-safety certificate valid 3 years, but only for premises whose plans and conditions it approved at the planning or building-permit stage; the municipal technical service's certificate is valid 3 years and needs a building permit; the municipal health certificate needs a €50 prepayment, is valid 1 year and is also required by the Deputy Ministry of Tourism. Since 1 July 2024 planning and building permits come from the district local-government organisation (EOA).

m-2ed715fd.t: The person who will manage a Cyprus café - the founder himself if he qualifies, or a hired manager - is approved by the Deputy Ministry of Tourism on an application 'for the Position of the Manager of a Catering Establishment', filed through the Point of Single Contact or by post or hand at the Ministry's offices. Per the business portal (page last updated 2 April 2021, read 6 October 2026) it needs copies of academic qualifications, original work-experience certificates (including the Social Insurance record) and a criminal-record certificate issued within 365 days; there is no fee and the decision comes within 3 months of a complete application. No page read times it before the licence.

m-29251ce9.t: A business importing goods from outside the EU registers with customs (EORI): under art. 9(1) of the Union Customs Code, Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, economic operators established in the EU customs territory 'shall register with the customs authorities responsible for the place where they are established'. In Cyprus this is form C.1000 of the Department of Customs and Excise (file of 26 August 2019, read 6 October 2026), filed at District Customs offices by a self-employed person, partnership or company and signed by the person, a director or another listed officer before a customs officer or with a certified, revenue-stamped signature. It states no registration fee and no processing time.

m-2919a09b.t: Limassol extended the due date of its bills for professional tax, refuse fees and the charge for use of business premises to Tuesday 30 December 2025 (announcement of 26 November 2025, read 6 October 2026). They are paid at the tax collection office at Arch. Kyprianou 23 next to the Town Hall, at the Mesa Geitonia district cashiers (Griva Digeni 14), online on limassol.org.cy, through jccsmart.com or in the 'Δημότης Λεμεσού' app; anyone who received no notice is asked to call 25884400 or write to invoicing@limassol.org.cy and update the postal address.

m-271f00e6.t: A Cyprus municipality may not license a cafe or restaurant of over 50 m2 until the applicant produces a certificate from the head of the Fire Service in the municipality that adequate provision has been made to prevent and extinguish fire and for everyone's safe escape (Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022, s. 55(2)(δ)). No fee or time for it was found: the Fire Service Law 100(I)/2021 lets the Council of Ministers set by regulation the classes of buildings subject to fire-protection control (s. 10(1)), but cylaw's indexes 2021-2026 hold only staff, discipline and reserve regulations under it, and the Service's pages give neither.

m-1f8eb951.t: As of 6 October 2026 Cyprus's Supreme Constitutional Court lists presidential references in its cause lists by number only, so which one is the 2026 leisure-premises law is not established. Its September 2026 list set hearings of References 3/2026 (7 Sep), 4/2026 (9 Sep), 2/2026 (16 Sep), 5-8/2026 (22 Sep), 1/2026 (24 Sep), 9/2026 (28 Sep) and 10/2026 (30 Sep); its October list sets 11/2026 on 8 October, 5-8/2026 with 12/2026 on 20 October and 13/2026 on 23 October. Its decided list for 2026 shows only 2/25 (6 May) and 4/26 (30 September, a civil-procedure law). No such law is in CyLaw's 2026 list; no date for an opinion is published.

m-1ea8651e.t: The Department of Environment's application forms for its registers of EEE producers (file named 2022, under reg. 21 of K.D.P. 73/2015 to 200/2021) and of battery producers (2026), read 6 October 2026, ask the applicant to attach the Registrar's certificate of incorporation with its HE number (a company based abroad: its EU or national tax number with a certificate), a certificate of participation in the approved collective system or the Department's approval of an individual system, and, where a director signs, the directors' certificate. The forms thus need incorporation and membership of WEEE Cyprus or AFIS before the register application.

m-1e9f5de8.t: Larnaca files business-premises licences at its Hygiene Service, 3rd floor of the Municipality's head office (Athinon Avenue), by appointment. A notice of 8 January 2026 said applications for alcohol, business-premises use and s. 55 licences for '2026-2027' would be taken from 2 February 2026, appointments on 24816562 / 24816563, with the health certificate applied for at the same time on a €50 prepayment. On 26 August 2026 it called entertainment and food-and-drink businesses to contact the Service by 11 September 2026 and file by appointment, 08:30-12:30, for 13/03/2026-12/03/2027, said the required documents are on its website, and warned of legal measures 'without further notice'.

m-1e41e492.t: The Department of Environment's page on extended producer responsibility (last updated 29 September 2026, read 6 October 2026) describes packaging producers as those who pack products and import packaged products 'in volumes at least, up to 2 tonnes per material per year' and says they must set up individual or collective systems under K.D.P. 747/2003. The phrase is garbled, and no such threshold is in Law 32(I)/2002 or K.D.P. 747/2003. The passage is old text: it lists the Law's amendments only to 2012, says the Department made 40 inspections in 2014 and served out-of-court notices on non-complying producers (number not given), and cites data from 1,800 economic operators for 2012.
