m-1e27e47d.t: Cyprus's Packaging Law 32(I)/2002 (consolidated to Law 97(I)/2022, none later on CyLaw; read 6 October 2026) puts the cost of managing packaging waste on anyone who manufactures, imports, transports, supplies or in any way trades products in packaging (s. 9(1)). Its Regulations K.D.P. 747/2003 (no amendment found) oblige 'packaging managers' - suppliers, makers, packers, importers of packaged products and distributors - to run an individual system or join a collective one, each approved for six years (regs 2, 4), and to report yearly (reg. 9(1)); a member of a collective system is relieved of any other packaging-management responsibility (reg. 6(4)). Neither text sets a quantity threshold.

m-1b094472.t: An EEE seller is a 'producer' under the Waste (WEEE) Regulations K.D.P. 73/2015 (as amended) if, established in Cyprus, it makes EEE or rebrands others' EEE, or professionally imports and places EEE on the market, or if, established abroad, it sells EEE at a distance directly to households or other users in Cyprus. Producers enter the Department of Environment's register (reg. 21) and declare each March the previous year's quantities (reg. 21(2)(στ)); the Department's form asks for the Registrar's certificate and proof of scheme membership and says registration 'must be renewed in March of each year'. A producer from another Member State may act through a written-mandate agent (reg. 22).

m-1b04a5c0.t: No 2025 or 2026 amounts per category of the s. 56(5) trade fee were found published by Nicosia, Larnaca or Paphos on 6 October 2026, and Limassol's 2026 methodology cites the Fifth Schedule's values without printing them. Searched: Nicosia's forms, online-applications and FAQ pages and its 2025-2026 council minutes (13 of 35 PDFs have a text layer; the 22 scans were not read); Larnaca's FAQ, forms and Finance Department pages and its site's posts and pages; Paphos's forms page, 2022 citizens' guide and its site's posts. The amount a given business owes therefore shows on its yearly invoice or must be asked of the municipality's tax office.

m-19e402ca.t: Limassol's application for a premises licence under s. 56 of Law 52(I)/2022 (undated form; PDF of 7 October 2024) asks for the period 'from .../.../20.. to 31/12/20..', so the licence ends with the calendar year though s. 56 sets no term; Paphos calls it 'annual'. Its categories are food and drink premises (catering under 50 m2, groceries, kiosks, coffee-shops, clubs, take-away, off-licences). A company attaches certificates of incorporation, directors and shareholders, the lease or use permission, the building permit, the health certificate and, for most of these, the Deputy Ministry of Tourism licence. Neither Limassol's s. 55 or s. 56 form nor Nicosia's guidance prints the licence fee.

m-185d1822.t: Cyprus's Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022 provides no certificate that a licence has been deemed granted by silence ('deemed to have been granted' occurs only in s. 45(2) and (3)(γ); text searched 6 October 2026). The one document it obliges the municipality to send, 'as soon as possible' for every licence application, is an acknowledgement of receipt stating the four-month limit, the remedies against a refusal and that the licence is deemed granted if the limit is not kept (s. 45(3)). That this acknowledgement serves as evidence of a deemed grant is an inference; no ruling was searched. A rejection for procedural defects is notified as fast as possible.

m-17bbcb6b.t: Turning a Cyprus shop or office into a cafe engages building and planning law: s. 3(1)(ε) of Cap. 96 (Streets and Buildings Regulation Law) forbids anyone to change, or permit or tolerate a change of, the approved use of a building without a permit obtained beforehand from the competent authority - now the district EOA's Director of Development Licensing (s. 2). The paragraph stands apart from building works (para. (β)), so on its wording it applies even where no works are done. Planning permission is needed too: only changes within a use class are free of it, and shop (class I), office (II) and cafe (III) are different classes (General Development Order 2024, para. 5, Second Schedule).

m-172c85d5.t: The business portal says Cyprus's catering licence 'can be granted only to physical persons or legal entities ... Resident in Cyprus or citizens of another E.U. member state or legal persons situated in an E.U. member state', and asks a non-EU national for a residence and employment permit (page updated 18 September 2026, read 6 October 2026). The Catering Establishments Law 29/1985 (consolidated to Law 170(I)/2020) and its Regulations 1986-2005, searched for residence, nationality and EU terms, carry no such condition; the portal cites no section for it.

m-171f1b69.t: No dataset of licensed catering establishments is on Cyprus's open-data portal: searches of data.gov.cy on 6 October 2026 (αναψυχής, εστίασης, εστιατόρια, Υφυπουργείο Τουρισμού, catering, restaurants) found only Nicosia Municipality's 'Εστιατόρια του Δήμου Λευκωσίας' - name, description and coordinates, modified 16 January 2024, no licence data. The Deputy Ministry of Tourism publishes PDF lists by district instead. In the five lists dated 19 June 2026 about 1,988 licence expiry dates run from 19 June 2026 to 18 June 2029 (many entries show none): none past, none more than three years ahead, consistent with the three-year licence term of Law 29/1985 s. 6(4) since 2020.

m-137ac67c.t: Paphos Municipality takes s. 56 premises-licence applications only online, via its PafosNow portal (announcement of 15 December 2025: 'exclusively electronically'). Its forms page (pafos.org.cy/entipa, read 6 October 2026) links two web forms subtitled 'Article 56 of the Municipalities Law', for natural persons (pafosnow.org/fisika-prosopa/) and companies. The natural-person form asks for name, ID or passport no., premises name, use, plot, sheet/plan, m2, staff, address and contacts; seven uploads: ID (both sides), building permit, final-approval certificate, lease or use permission, a refuse bill, a photo of the premises, the last receipt paid to the Custodian of Turkish Cypriot Properties.

m-12928911.t: Nicosia's forms page (read 6 October 2026) offers no application under s. 56 of Law 52(I)/2022: its two premises-licence forms (PDFs of 2020) cite ss. 112-117 of the repealed 1985 Law - a three-year licence for entertainment and food premises (now s. 55) and one for a performance or up to a year - and its online-applications page lists no premises licence. The three-year form wants building permit, approval certificate, municipal technical, electrical, fire and health certificates, title deed or lease and an equipment list, and says that 'to be accepted' an application must be duly completed with all required documents. A 2020 notice: file by post to Eptanisou 11 or by hand at the Town Hall.

m-10c88967.t: Municipal advertising regulations under s. 7 of Cap. 50 set sign charges, and two merged municipalities adopted another municipality's regulations: Paralimni-Deryneia took Strovolos's of 2000 with a new fee table (K.D.P. 439/2024, Gazette 20 December 2024), repealing its predecessors' 1977 rules - for a licence to erect a private sign, EUR 68 a year for the first 2 m2 plus EUR 17 per extra m2 up to 10 m2 if illuminated, EUR 51 plus EUR 8.50 if not; EUR 854-3,417 a year above 10 m2; double for two-sided signs. Kourion adopted Latsia's regulations of 2012, fee table included, by K.D.P. 226/2026 (Gazette 8 May 2026). Read 6 October 2026.

m-0c3cc2ae.t: For the electrical certificate a café needs for its municipal licence, Nicosia Municipality's guidance table (PDF of 12 September 2024, served 6 October 2026) says €30.50 is paid at the Electrical and Mechanical Services (EMS) offices with application form EMS 53.1.23 for the inspection; form EMS 60.18-1 is completed and signed by the electrical designer and the electrical contractor; and the EMS electrical inspector inspects on site and signs. The certificate is valid at most 2 years from the inspection of the existing installation. Form 60.18-1 (PDF of 2019) asks the designer and the contractor each for an 'EMS register number' and a limit of responsibility in kVA.

m-0bddf52b.t: Per Green Dot Cyprus's 'Packaging Declarations 2026' page (modified 18 February 2026, read 6 October 2026), member companies must declare every year by 29 February the packaging they placed on the market in the previous year, on one of five forms (detailed, pesticides, catalogue, drinks catalogue, or a 'declaration with categorisation' for members in the small tonnage bands); Green Dot says it audits about 20 member companies a year through chartered auditors.

m-051635c7.t: To be charged the premises and trade fees, Nicosia asks a business to register on its form 'for registration in the tax register for the issue of business-premises fees and the carrying on of a business, trade or profession under s. 56(5) and (6)' of Law 52(I)/2022 (Word file saved 15 October 2024, read 6 October 2026). It asks for the company's or natural person's name and trade name, director and ID, company number, home address of the director or self-employed person, premises address, kind of work, number of persons employed or to be employed, start date, and an e-mail for bills. It goes by fax to 22752311 or to invoices@nicosia.org.cy; information on 22797342/348.

m-048938cf.t: Limassol's forms page (read 6 October 2026) says its s. 56 form is to be completed and e-mailed to an officer (aconstantinides@limassol.org.cy; phone 25884418); no online service is named. The form covers only food and drink premises (restaurants or tavernas under 50 m2, groceries and supermarkets, kiosks, coffee-shops, clubs, take-away, off-licences, other eating places under 50 m2) and lists: ID copy (natural person); a company's certificates of incorporation and of directors and shareholders; lease or use permission; building permit; health certificate; previous licence (existing premises); tourism licence, except coffee-shops, take-away, clubs and premises under 8 m2 without alcohol.

m-03a10732.t: As tabled on 26 March 2026, Cyprus's member's bill on leisure premises moves catering licensing from the Deputy Ministry of Tourism to the municipal or community council of the area (the Interior Minister may delegate a community council's power to the District Officer); merges the council's leisure-and-entertainment licence under the Municipalities and Communities Laws with the new operating licence where a premises needs both; and has the licence issued within two months of application, valid three years and renewable. The Deputy Ministry keeps a register, may inspect and recommend corrective measures. Laws 1985-2020 and Regulations 1986-2005 would be repealed.

m-0314eaaf.t: Since 15 November 2024 an Interior Ministry circular (ΥΠΕΣ Γ.Ε. 057 of 14 November 2024, to the EOA Directors of Licensing) exempts low-risk buildings - houses up to two dwellings, terraced houses, and purely residential blocks of up to 4 floors and 20 flats - from consulting the Fire Service for a Cyprus building permit; the designer files an ETEK self-check form instead. Cafes and shops are not in the two exempt categories, so they stay under the existing consultation framework. The circular states an intention to amend the simplified-procedure decrees K.D.P. 388/2020 and 357/2022 so that Fire Service consultation under them runs in IPPODAMOS during examination, not before filing.

m-dd4ded87.t: Central Bank of Cyprus register of payment institutions (file of 17 September 2026): six withdrawn licences are listed - AlgoPay (21 Nov 2016), Jet Money Services (4 Apr 2017), WeCollect (Europe) (28 Nov 2018), Mediterranean Finance (4 Jan 2024), Silvergate Technologies (29 Apr 2024) and Masari Payment Services (28 Jan 2026). Of the ten payment institutions listed, five show a licence date of June-August 2018 - for four of them the re-issue of a licence first granted in 2011 - and five were authorised on 10 Feb 2022, 19 May 2022, 27 Jan 2023, 29 Jun 2023 and 1 Nov 2023. JCC Payment Systems Ltd held a payment institution licence from 23 April 2010 and an e-money licence from 12 December 2022.

m-d98c430a.t: The ECB dates the end of Eurobank Cyprus Ltd's banking licence: 'With effect from 20 September 2025, Eurobank Cyprus Ltd's licence was withdrawn' (changes sheet of the list of supervised entities with cut-off 1 November 2025, published 18 December 2025). The same sheet records that Hellenic Bank Public Company Limited changed its legal name to Eurobank Limited on 2 September 2025. This is one of the two credit-institution licence withdrawals shown for 2025 in the Central Bank of Cyprus Annual Report 2025 (Table 5.3): subsidiaries of EU banks went from four on the register of 16 June 2025 to three at year-end.

m-d640526a.t: Two Central Bank of Cyprus documents count the locally licensed payment and e-money institutions differently. The statistical release 'Payment Statistics: second half of 2025' (22 July 2026) says their total 'increased from 34 at the end of the second half of 2024 to 38 at the end of the second half of 2025'; the Annual Report 2025 gives 28 electronic money institutions and 12 payment institutions at end-2025, 40 in all. Neither document states its counting base, so the difference of two is unexplained; a count of Cyprus payment and e-money institutions should name the document it comes from.

m-cfb269c1.t: For a third-country national the business portal adds a document the catering Law does not mention. Its catering page (updated 18 September 2026) grants the licence only to persons 'Resident in Cyprus or citizens of another E.U. member state or legal persons situated in an E.U. member state' - the first limb is residence, not nationality - and lists a 'Copy of Residence and Employment Permit' for a non-EU national. Law 29/1985 sets no nationality or residence condition for operator or manager; the Deputy Ministry of Tourism's form F-KEN-02/1-13 (May 2025) asks for the operator's identity card (English note: 'or passport'), the manager's details and, for a company, four Registrar documents.

m-c915c368.t: A government bill to replace Cyprus's catering-establishment framework was before Parliament in 2025-26; no such law appears in the published lists as of 5 Oct 2026. Per the Cyprus Mail, the Deputy Ministry of Tourism had submitted it by 10 October 2025 (ending classification by class and price-list approval, new opening hours), and on 13 February 2026 the House energy committee was examining it article by article, 'final decisions' expected in the plenary 'by April', before the House dissolved for elections. cylaw's numbered lists of laws for 2021-2026 (through Law 125(I)/2026, file of 3 October 2026; No. 98(I)/2026 is absent) hold no Catering Establishments law after Law 170(I)/2020.

m-bdc1f225.t: A restaurant, taverna, cafeteria, bar or similar place serving food or drink for payment in Cyprus may not operate without a licence under the Catering Establishments Law 29/1985 (s. 6(1)), issued by the Deputy Ministry of Tourism (Law 123(I)/2018). Section 2 excludes traditional coffee-shops ('καφενεία'), take-away-only shops, certain canteens, and shops with a service area under 8 m² serving no alcohol. The licence needs a sanitary certificate and the fee (s. 6(3)) and, since Law 170(I)/2020, expires every three years. The business portal (18 September 2026) still says one year, to 31 December; it also says to apply at least one month before opening, with a decision within three months.

m-bc765db2.t: Cyprus has no licence aimed at selling online as such. Section 7(1) of the Electronic Commerce Law 156(I)/2004 (amended by Law 97(I)/2007; in force 5 Oct 2026) says taking up and pursuing the activity of an information-society service provider is not subject to prior authorisation or any requirement of equivalent effect - without prejudice to authorisation schemes not aimed specifically at such services. The Law requires disclosure (s. 8(1)): name, geographic address, contact details including e-mail, register and registration number, the supervisory authority where the activity needs approval, the VAT number where VAT applies; prices must say whether tax and delivery are included (s. 8(2)).

m-b32a775d.t: AstroBank's licence end, narrowed but not dated. The ECB's list of supervised entities with cut-off 1 November 2025 (published 18 December 2025) still names AstroBank Public Company Limited among Cyprus's less significant banks; the lists with cut-off 1 March 2026 (published 23 April 2026) and 1 July 2026 do not. The Central Bank of Cyprus counted 5 local authorised credit institutions at 31 December 2025 and licensed none during 2025, so AstroBank was still one of them: its authorisation ended between 31 December 2025 and 1 March 2026. No Central Bank announcement on the withdrawal was found (the Gazette was not searched); the ECB's change annexes cover significant institutions only.

m-a6bc8e59.t: Who issues the sanitary certificate for a Cyprus café depends on the licence. Law 29/1985 (s. 2) defines it as the certificate issued by the Health Service of the Ministry of Health or by a municipal health service, as the case may be; the Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022, s. 55(2)(ε), requires a municipal health service certificate for the municipal licence of premises over 50 m². The business portal follows unevenly: its catering page (18 September 2026) names the Ministry's services, its alcohol-licence (7 December 2023) and premises pages the municipality. The alcohol list also asks, where applicable, for the tourism licence and a criminal record certificate under 3 months old.

m-a65243be.t: The Cyprus Consumer Protection Service's page for businesses selling at a distance (undated, footer 2022, read 5 Oct 2026; it links to the Consumer Protection Law of 2021) lists: pre-contract information - the trader's identity and address, the total price with all charges, the terms of withdrawal; confirmation on a durable medium at the latest on delivery or before the service starts; 14 days to withdraw (from delivery for goods, from the contract for services), up to one year more if the information was not given; refund within 14 days of the notice; delivery within 30 days unless agreed otherwise. It names no registration and does not reflect the Law's 2026 amendments.

m-9f9358c3.t: Since 19 June 2026 a Cyprus trader who concludes distance contracts with consumers through an online interface must offer a withdrawal function there: section 22A of the Consumer Protection Law 112(I)/2021, added by Law 30(I)/2026 (Gazette 5080, 23 March 2026; transposing Directive (EU) 2023/2673). The function bears the words 'Πατήστε εδώ για υπαναχώρηση' or an equivalent, stays available through the withdrawal period, prominent and easy to reach; the consumer gives name, contract and an electronic address and confirms with a control marked 'επιβεβαίωση υπαναχώρησης'; the trader acknowledges on a durable medium without undue delay. Pre-contract information must say that it exists and where.

m-9d02e684.t: For the Cyprus catering licence the business portal sets an age limit on Registrar certificates that the licensing authority's own form does not. Its catering page (updated 18 September 2026) lists, for a company, copies of the memorandum and articles, the certificate of incorporation, the certificate of directors and secretary and the certificate of registered office, which 'should have an issue or validation date by the Registrar of Companies of no later than 60 days'; it gives no legal basis. The Deputy Ministry of Tourism's form F-KEN-02/1-13 (May 2025) names the same four documents without an age limit and has the applicant declare that they match what the Registrar's website shows.

m-8bbb7a0a.t: Entries in the Central Bank of Cyprus register of credit institutions in dated web-archive snapshots (local / EU subsidiaries / non-EU subsidiaries / EU branches / non-EU branches): 16 Apr 2016 - 7 banks + 19 cooperative / 4 / 2 / 8 / 15; 8 May 2017 - 8 + 19 / 3 / 2 / 7 / 15; 25 Mar 2019 - 7 / 3 / 2 / 5 / 15, the cooperative sector gone; 31 Dec 2020 and 13 Dec 2021 - 7 / 3 / 1 / 5 / 13; 4 Dec 2023 - 6 / 3 / 1 / 4 / 11, seven of the non-EU branches footnoted as closing; 16 Jun 2025 - 5 / 4 / 1 / 3 / 5. Totals: 55, 54, 32, 29, 29, 25, 18. No usable snapshot exists between July 2017 and March 2019.

m-85f506e6.t: The Deputy Ministry of Tourism's procedure sheet for a catering licence (dated December 2018, posted 28 May 2024, read 5 Oct 2026) has five stages: (A) planning permission, sought by the owner; (B) approval of the plans by the Deputy Ministry (form F-KEN-01/1); (C) a building or change-of-use permit - from the municipality or District Officer in the sheet, now the District Local Government Organisation (Law 37(I)/2022, s. 20(2)(β)); (D) after the works, verification by district inspectors and filing of forms F-KEN-02/1 and F-KEN-05/1, even while the permit is pending; (E) classification and the licence, on conditions that include a copy of the permit, a sanitary certificate and the fee.

m-79c85729.t: Read one by one on 4 October 2026, the Central Bank of Cyprus annual reports for 2015-2023 contain no table or stock count of licensed credit institutions, e-money institutions or payment institutions. What they give instead: banks in TARGET2-CY - 22 (18 direct, 4 indirect) in the 2015 report (p. 33), 21 (17 + 4) in 2016 (p. 30) and 2017 (p. 31), 19 (16 + 3) in 2018 (Table 4.1, p. 30); and flows - 'fifteen institutions' licensed in 2022 (p. 28) and 'nine entities' in 2023 (p. 31), across all licence types, with no breakdown. The 2019, 2020 and 2021 reports give neither. The first stock figure is in the 2024 report: 26 EMIs and 11 PIs.

m-5cb1acdb.t: Staff who handle unpacked food in a Cyprus food business need a Health Certificate for Food Handlers from a Chief Medical Officer of the Ministry of Health: per the business portal (updated 2 May 2024) there is no application form; a stool sample is tested for salmonella and parasites at the person's own cost, then the officer issues the certificate the same day for €22 plus a registration fee; it is valid twelve months. In a licensed catering establishment every person employed must hold a sanitary certificate (Law 29/1985, s. 17(2)). Article 6(2) of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 obliges each food business operator to notify the competent authority of every establishment for registration.

m-43a67aef.t: A licensed catering establishment in Cyprus must have a manager who meets statutory conditions, and the owner may fill the post only if he meets them (Law 29/1985, s. 16; read 5 Oct 2026). The manager must be a graduate of a recognised hotel or tourism school with knowledge of food and drink, or hold a secondary-school leaving certificate and one year's catering experience, or have at least three years' experience judged satisfactory by the licensing authority; and must be of good character, shown by a Chief of Police certificate of no conviction for listed offences. For class A and B establishments only the school route counts. The Law sets no nationality condition for the manager.

m-3fb7e56b.t: Law 73(I)/2009 has a general route for sanctions under EU acts assigned to CySEC by notification: article 37(1A) (consolidated text on cylaw.org, read 5 October 2026) obliges the Commission to impose the administrative sanctions and measures laid down in European Union acts for whose application it is designated competent authority 'either under those acts or by notification of the Minister'; article 37(1) sets the general fine at up to EUR 350,000, EUR 700,000 on repetition. Read with K.D.P. 310/2024 this would cover MiCA without a dedicated law - an inference, not a CySEC statement. The provision speaks of the Commission only; the Central Bank's corresponding power was not checked.

m-1e92bcc3.t: Inside a municipality a café needs municipal licences beside the tourism licence. Under the Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022, premises over 50 m² used as a restaurant, taverna, snack bar, cafeteria or pizzeria need a prior municipal licence under s. 55(1)(γ), for up to three years, on a building permit and engineer's, electrical, fire and municipal-health certificates; s. 56(1), the licence for any business premises, excepts those cases and so covers smaller ones. Section 44(1) adds sound-emission and alcohol licences; under Cap. 144, s. 11, an alcohol licence expires on 12 March. The business portal, still citing the 1985 Law, gives four months for the premises decision, two for alcohol.

m-0ca78a88.t: Since 27 September 2026 a Cyprus distance seller's pre-contract information must also include: a reminder of the legal guarantee of conformity and its main elements, including its minimum two-year duration, shown by the EU 'harmonised notice'; the 'harmonised label' where the producer gives a free durability guarantee of over two years on the whole good and has told the trader; environmentally friendly delivery options where available; and, where the producer supplies it, the minimum period of software updates. Source: Law 122(I)/2026 (Gazette 5093, 17 July 2026), amending s. 17(1) of the Consumer Protection Law 112(I)/2021 and adding s. 17A, to transpose Directive (EU) 2024/825.

m-0a512147.t: The Central Bank of Cyprus 'Register of Credit Institutions operating in Cyprus', as archived on 22 November 2015, listed 57 credit institutions: 7 local banks (one of them, Cyprus Popular Bank, under resolution), the Cooperative Central Bank with 18 affiliated cooperative credit institutions, 4 subsidiaries of EU banks, 2 subsidiaries of non-EU banks, 9 branches of EU banks and 16 branches of non-EU banks (among them FBME Bank Ltd, whose licence was revoked on 21 December 2015), plus 2 representative offices. The figure counts entries on the page, including institutions under resolution or with restricted licences.

m-f1ad473f.t: The legal basis of the Cyprus MiCA designation is article 56A of the CySEC Law 73(I)/2009, inserted by section 6 of Law 65(I)/2014 (Gazette 23 May 2014): the Minister may issue a notification, published in the Official Gazette, designating and authorising the Commission to act as competent authority for the application of any act of the European Union. The article names CySEC only, yet K.D.P. 310/2024 also designates the Central Bank of Cyprus. No dedicated Cyprus law implementing MiCA was found on 4 October 2026: cylaw.org's indexes of numbered laws for 2024, 2025 and 2026 (to Law 125(I)/2026) have no title containing 'κρυπτο', and the Central Bank's MiCAR page cites only the Regulation.

m-ee243819.t: Law 196(I)/2012 regulates 'administrative services' in Cyprus (s. 4(1)): trustee services; company management, including providing directors, a secretary, nominee shareholding, a registered office or official address, partners, opening or managing bank accounts and safekeeping of financial instruments; and investment-programme residence or naturalisation applications. Only 'eligible persons' may provide them (s. 5(1)): companies licensed by CySEC, or exempt persons - advocates and law firms supervised by the Bar Council, and ICPAC members and their firms supervised by the ICPAC Council. Forming companies stays the exclusive competence of advocates. Read on cylaw 4 Oct 2026.

m-e3e76791.t: Section 4(3) of Cyprus Law 196(I)/2012 exempts from licensing an individual acting as director of fewer than ten companies (provided such persons do not together control the board), as director of a company at least 25% owned by himself or his family or of his sole employer, or, if resident in Cyprus, as secretary of a company at least 50% owned by himself or his family, on condition that the service is not advertised, used to attract clients or offered to others. A founder directing his own company needs no licence. A directorship service marketed to clients falls outside the exemption and may be provided only by an eligible person; licences go to companies only (s. 2). Read 4 Oct 2026.

m-d33bfeb3.t: A Cyprus business using PayPal contracts with PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. et Cie, S.C.A. (R.C.S. Luxembourg B 118 349). The CSSF register lists it as a bank under number B00000351, valid from 1 July 2007, and the ECB list of supervised entities (cut-off 1 July 2026) as a less significant credit institution. The PayPal user agreement, last updated 7 September 2026, applies to accounts of residents of 13 countries including Cyprus and is governed by Luxembourg law. It states that money in the account is electronic money, not a deposit, so the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme cannot protect it.

m-b30d7cfc.t: payabl. operates in Cyprus as Payabl. CY Limited (formerly Powercash21 Limited), HE289380. The Central Bank of Cyprus registers show payment-institution licence 115.1.2.9/2018 with services 3, 5, 7, 8 (PI register file dated 17/09/2026; service 5 is issuing of payment instruments and/or acquiring) and an EMI licence 115.1.3.36 dated 04/01/2024 that is not yet activated (EMI register file dated 28/09/2026), so it operates as a payment institution; payabl.'s legal page states the same PI licence. As of 2026-10-04 payabl.com/pricing returns 404, and the legal page offers card terms, account terms and a chargeback guide but no merchant acquiring agreement, price list or onboarding checklist.

m-9cc0a8ae.t: CySEC's public list of approved administrative service providers under Law 196(I)/2012 carried 126 licensed companies on 4 October 2026 (126 distinct licence numbers, the highest 233/196; licence dates from 4 March 2013 to 12 December 2025), each with its permitted services: 117 entries name trust management under s. 4(1)(a) and/or company management under s. 4(1)(b), three of them adding s. 4(1)(c); eight read 'All'; one is in Greek. Companies licensed by CySEC are one of three groups of eligible persons; CySEC's 'Eligible Persons' page points to the Cyprus Bar Association and ICPAC for the other two, and a separate CySEC list shows former providers.

m-5a65ba14.t: Cyprus designated its MiCA competent authorities by ministerial notification, not by a dedicated law: K.D.P. 310/2024, Gazette Annex III(I) No. 5896, 13 September 2024, issued by the Minister of Finance under article 56A of the CySEC Law 73(I)/2009. CySEC covers offers of crypto-assets other than asset-referenced and e-money tokens, service providers authorised under Art. 63, investment firms, market operators, depositories and fund managers acting under Art. 60, and issuers of asset-referenced tokens that are not banks or e-money institutions. The Central Bank covers banks and e-money institutions that provide crypto-asset services under Art. 60 or issue asset-referenced or e-money tokens.

m-496750fb.t: ESMA's interim MiCA register of crypto-asset service providers (CASPS.csv, last modified 30 September 2026) holds 364 rows, 25 with Cyprus as home member state - fourth after Germany (99), France (36) and the Netherlands (29). All 25 name CySEC as competent authority, none the Central Bank of Cyprus. One row has an end date (Stratos Europe Ltd, 24 April 2026), leaving 24 in force. The earliest Cyprus entry is eToro (Europe) Ltd, 16 January 2025; 13 of the 25 are dated 8 June 2026 or later, around the end of the transitional period on 1 July 2026. The file has no column for the legal basis: a free-text comment marks Art. 60 for three rows of other states and is empty for all 25 Cyprus rows.

m-40c9b261.t: Viva.com's terms for EEA users, effective 30 September 2026, are concluded with VIVABANK BANKING S.A. ('VIVA BANK'), tax number 999846755. The Bank of Greece's list of credit institutions incorporated in Greece (workbook last modified 14 September 2026) carries it as code 057, 'VIVABANK SINGLE MEMBER BANKING S.A', same tax number, LEI 213800A3YBCKWVF3DM64. A Cyprus merchant using Viva therefore contracts with a Greek bank; that it serves Cyprus under freedom of services is the terms' own statement, and the Cyprus price list shows the Viva.com account carrying a Greek ('GR') IBAN. Acquired funds are credited to that account according to a payout schedule 'as published on www.viva.com'.

m-2ac37573.t: The Cyprus Bar Association's public register of administrative service providers ('Μητρώο ΕΠΔΥ', cyprusbar.org) showed 1,442 entries on 4 October 2026 (the grid's own counter: 'Page 1 of 145 (1442 items)'). Each row gives the provider company's name and registration number, the lawyer or law firm it is connected with, contact details, compliance officer, directors, the services offered and the employees providing them. By this count the Bar's register holds about eleven times as many providers as CySEC licenses (126) and several times ICPAC's 316 firms. Each supervisor keeps its own register (Law 196(I)/2012, s. 25(2) proviso); CySEC only links to the other two (s. 25(6)).

m-25ebd052.t: The ECB's list of supervised entities (cut-off date 1 July 2026) shows Revolut Bank UAB as a credit institution in the significant group Revolut Holdings Europe UAB, directly supervised by the ECB, and lists as less significant credit institutions Adyen N.V. (under De Nederlandsche Bank), PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. et Cie, S.C.A. (Luxembourg) and Vivabank SA (under the Bank of Greece). The same list shows Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd, Eurobank Limited and Alpha Bank Cyprus Ltd as credit institutions in significant groups, the latter two as subsidiaries of Eurobank S.A. and ALPHA BANK S.A. and 'among the three largest credit institutions in Cyprus'.

m-627a91de.t: Dated editions of the Deputy Ministry of Tourism's district lists of recreation centres reachable on 6 October 2026, by the date printed on them: Nicosia 09/12/2020, 24/11/2021, 05/01/2022, 21/09/2022, 22/11/2023, 18/06/2024, 06/11/2025, 16/02/2026 and 19/06/2026; Limassol 09/12/2020, 05/01/2022, 21/09/2022, 27/06/2023, 22/11/2023, 18/06/2024, 16/02/2026 and 19/06/2026. Older ones sit on visitcyprus.com, newer ones on gov.cy. The 06/11/2025 Nicosia edition survives only as a web-archive copy of 14 November 2025: its gov.cy address now answers 'not found' (HTTP 404).

m-f72a525b.t: The Tax Department's announcement of 9 April 2026 (with a PDF of the same day; read 6 October 2026) sets the CY Login rule by Registrar number prefix: from 1 July 2026 a tax-register request by a legal person whose number begins ΗΕ (companies of any kind), ΑΕ (overseas companies) or Σ (registered general and limited partnerships) is accepted only when the Tax For All login is made through CY Login, and requests made otherwise 'will be rejected'; entities with any other prefix still register in Tax For All without CY Login. It adds that the measure concerns only the login through CY Login. It does not say whose CY Login profile, the company's own or an officer's, is meant.

m-d665a785.t: The Cyprus Tax Department's news lists (Tax For All news, 43 items; main-site news to 2 October 2026) carry no item on registering legal persons after the CY Login notice of 9 April 2026, and its documents index (67 items) lists nothing dated after 23 June 2026 (read 6 October 2026). The one later text on whose CY Login a company uses is its guide 'TFA - CY Login' (course updated 29 September 2026), and it speaks of log-in, not registration in terms: a legal person's first log-in must be 'with the personal CY Login credentials of the Legal Person', and a taxpayer without a TIN may start registration 'through his CY Login account'. The registration page asks the ID of the officer who submits.

m-bd75d051.t: What Limassol Municipality charged companies run from professional offices, per its own documents (read 6 October 2026). Since a council decision of 26 September 2019 it levies an annual fee on legal persons whose registered office or management is with law, accounting or audit firms or secretarial offices: for 2019 EUR 150 standalone, EUR 85 in a group, EUR 50 dormant; for 2022 EUR 195 and EUR 111, and from a decision of 20 June 2023 EUR 222 and EUR 127, with shipping companies EUR 150 and dormant ones, on an auditor's certificate, nothing. The Union of Cyprus Municipalities' uniform policy for such companies (letter of 20 October 2021) proposed EUR 250 and EUR 150.

m-9bb6c627.t: Derived from the rates in force on 6 October 2026, for company profit of tax year 2026 or later paid out in full as a dividend to a Cyprus tax-resident individual: corporate tax 15%, then on the remaining 85% a 5% special defence contribution if the shareholder is also domiciled in Cyprus, and 2.65% GeSY on the dividend, which has no domicile test - in all 15% + 85% x 7.65% = 21.5025% of the profit, or 15% + 85% x 2.65% = 17.2525% for a non-domiciled resident. A sole trader's profit instead bears the personal scale (0% up to €22,000, 35% above €72,000), social insurance at the applied 16.6% between his category minimum and the ceiling, 4% GeSY and, from 6 April 2026, a 0.5% training levy.

m-8e50b115.t: Since 1 January 2026 a director of a Cyprus company stays answerable under the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Law 4/1978 for liabilities that arose during his term even if, when administrative or court proceedings begin, he has been deleted from the register of directors and secretaries kept under s. 192 of Cap. 113 (new s. 53A(1), added by Law 243(I)/2025, art. 34). If the notice of the change of officers is filed late, his term is deemed to end on the date of the change when the notice is filed within 12 months of it, and otherwise only on the same calendar day one year before the notice is filed (s. 53A(2)).

m-83aea166.t: A Cyprus partnership is taxed through its partners, not as an entity. Under s. 7 of the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Law 4/1978 (consolidated text read 6 October 2026), where a business or profession is carried on jointly by two or more persons, each partner's taxable income from the partnership is his share of its income for the tax year, entered in his own return; and a partner who must register in the tax register files each year a return of the partnership's income naming the other partners and each one's share. The Income Tax Law's definition of 'company', which the 15% corporate rate applies to, excludes a partnership (Law 118(I)/2002, s. 2).

m-7bcf3bc1.t: The Cyprus Tax Department's Tax For All portal is at https://taxforall.mof.gov.cy/; an account is opened at https://taxforall.mof.gov.cy/CreateAccount (both served 6 October 2026). The sign-up form asks for name, date of birth, a telephone number with any country code, e-mail, a user name, a password and three security questions, and activates the account by an e-mail confirmation; it asks for no Cypriot identity or alien registration number. The Department's registration page (updated 28 September 2026) says a Tax Register request is filed 'ONLY' electronically through this portal; the documents are uploaded with the request. Helpline on the form: 17700.

m-749e2fbe.t: Losses are used differently by rung in Cyprus. Under s. 13(1) of the Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002 (consolidated text read 6 October 2026) a loss not wholly set off against the same person's other income of that tax year is carried forward - on this wording a sole trader's business loss first reduces his other income of the year. For a person obliged to keep books, have accounts audited and file a return, carry-forward ends seven years after the loss year (five before 1 January 2026). A company's current-year loss may be surrendered within a 75% group to a Cyprus-resident company (s. 13(4)-(8)); in a merger or other reorganisation, accumulated losses pass to the receiving company (ss. 27, 29A).

m-7486a2fa.t: The Cyprus Tax Department's directory (modified 7 September 2026, read 6 October 2026) lists separate district offices for direct taxation and for VAT. Direct: Nicosia, 2 Tseriou Avenue, 2042 Strovolos; Limassol, 3 16th June Street, 3022; Larnaca, 50 Spyrou Kyprianou, Iris 3 building, 6057; Paphos, Neofytou Nikolaidi, Building C, 8011. VAT: Nicosia and Larnaca at the same addresses; Limassol, 76 Franklin Roosevelt, 3011; Paphos, Neofytou Nikolaidi, Building A, 8011. The Department's home page gives public service hours of 08:00-14:00; neither it, the directory nor the contact page states an appointment requirement.

m-71353449.t: A request for a Cyprus tax number can be filed without the EU registration certificate: the Tax Department's page on registering individuals (updated 28 September 2026, read 6 October 2026) has a category 4 for EU or third-country citizens holding neither it nor a residence permit - a foreign tax-number certificate, identity card or social-insurance certificate, a photograph and a letter of reasons with evidence; one who has applied for the certificate adds the fee receipt. Specific evidence is listed for property, a foreign director signing the company return, the 60-day rule and employment, none for self-employment; the page does not say self-employment is accepted; more may be asked.

m-571b8ec5.t: Dissolving a Cyprus company brings the transitional deemed-dividend charge forward. Under art. 3Γ(1)(β) of Law 117(I)/2002 (as replaced by Law 245(I)/2025), on dissolution all profits of the last five years, to the extent earned in tax years up to 2025 and not distributed or already deemed distributed, are deemed distributed, with 17% on the part attributable to individuals resident and domiciled in Cyprus; under the proviso to art. 4(5), once the company passes a resolution for voluntary dissolution or liquidation, the declaration and payment are due within one month of it.

m-4a7280c3.t: Since 1 January 2026 officers of a Cyprus company who bear criminal liability for its unpaid taxes are also civilly liable. Under s. 51A(3) of the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Law 4/1978, when a legal person fails or delays paying tax it withheld (income tax, defence contribution, the 2011-2013 special contribution), its executive director, board members and officers with financial-management duties also bear criminal liability; for other taxes, only if shown to have taken part fraudulently. New s. 51A(3A), added by Law 243(I)/2025 (in force 1 January 2026), makes such a person liable jointly or severally with the legal person in any civil proceedings. Read 6 October 2026.

m-460c132f.t: Cyprus lengthened the carry-forward of tax losses from five to seven years: art. 8(α) of the Income Tax (Amendment) (No. 4) Law 244(I)/2025 (Gazette No. 5070, 31 December 2025) replaced 'five' with 'seven' in the first proviso to s. 13(1) of Law 118(I)/2002, in force from 1 January 2026 (art. 25). Art. 8(β) makes group relief apply only after the claimant company has set off its own losses brought forward. The government's tax-reform page for businesses (modified 10 July 2026, read 6 October 2026) lists the 'extension of the loss carry-forward period to seven years'. Art. 8 says nothing on losses of years before 2026.

m-44d8b03e.t: On the wording of Cyprus law, the seven-year limit on carrying losses forward may not reach a small sole trader. The first proviso to s. 13(1) of Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002 applies to a person who must keep books, prepare accounts audited by an independent auditor and file a return; s. 30(1) of Law 4/1978 (as amended by Law 243(I)/2025) exempts a natural person in business with turnover up to €120,000 from preparing such accounts, and lets one up to €200,000 (assets up to €500,000 for two years running) have them reviewed instead. This is our reading of the two texts on 6 October 2026; no Tax Department guidance on it was found.

m-313a4385.t: Before the CY Login rule, the Cyprus Tax Department kept a company's Tax For All access separate from its director's: its registration FAQ (published 2 January 2025, updated 1 July 2025, read 6 October 2026) says a director of three companies must first create three different TFA accounts, one for each company, entering his own details in each but a unique e-mail per company; when creating an account or registering a company, the name and date-of-birth fields may hold the director's or secretary's details or the company's name and registration date. Since 1 July 2026 HE, AE and registered-partnership requests go only through CY Login.

m-30c55699.t: For a company, the Cyprus Tax Department's tax residence certificate page (updated 28 September 2026, read 6 October 2026) names one supporting document: the certificate of incorporation (Π1) from the Registrar of Companies. It prepares a certificate only where Cyprus has signed a double tax treaty with the other country, and charges €80 in stamps. The page does not say what a foreign company with a Cyprus branch, or one incorporated abroad but managed and controlled in Cyprus, submits instead.

m-20fb7457.t: The Cyprus Tax Department's home page (dateModified 26 February 2026, read 6 October 2026) states public service hours of 08:00-14:00; neither it nor the Department's directory of district offices (modified 7 September 2026) or contact page (modified 25 August 2026) states an appointment requirement. These are the only counter hours found for the district offices where the paper VAT application T.F. 1101 is handed in.

m-11363856.t: Moving up from sole trader or partnership to a company can keep tax losses in Cyprus: s. 13(10) of the Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002 (consolidated text read 6 October 2026) provides that where the owner of a business, 'including a partnership', converts his business into a company, any accumulated losses of the owner may be transferred to the company. The subsection sets no procedure, form or time limit.

m-ffb1708c.t: An individual requests a Cyprus tax residence certificate on form T.D.126 (2022), the only form the Tax Department's page (updated 28 September 2026) lists for individuals; by its title it is the declaration 'under the 60-day rule', and the page does not say what a 183-day resident files. It goes by e-mail or letter to the District Tax Office and costs €80 in fee stamps, paid at collection. The form asks the Cyprus TIN, social insurance number and the landlord's and employer's TIN; attachments: passport stamps or tickets, title deed or tenancy agreement, employment contract in force on 31 December. It is prepared only where a double tax treaty has been signed with the other country.

m-ff014a55.t: No decree exempting any class of individuals from filing a Cyprus personal return for tax year 2026 was found on 5 October 2026. The power exists: the third proviso to s. 5(1) of Law 4/1978 (as replaced by Law 243(I)/2025) lets the Council of Ministers exempt categories of persons and set criteria under which individuals with gross income within the zero-rate band (€22,000) need not file; the Tax Department's page restates it. For 2025 there was one (K.D.P. 52/2025, €19,500). cylaw's indexes of regulatory acts for 2025 and 2026 list none for 2026; the 2026 index (352 acts to 25 September 2026, numbers 342 and 353-371 absent) has under that Law only K.D.P. 260/2026, on the 2025 deadline.

m-f766a82d.t: An employer in Cyprus files a monthly return of income tax and contributions withheld from pay (PAYE) through Tax For All by the end of the month after the month of withholding. The Tax Department's FAQ (13 June 2025) says monthly returns are mandatory from 1 January 2025, replace the former T.F.7 self-assessments, must show every employee with his tax identification number, and that at least one monthly return must exist before the annual employer return can be reconciled. For a company first paying wages for November 2026 the Department's calendar gives 31 December 2026 (November), 31 January 2027 (December) and 31 March 2027 for the annual PAYE return for 2026.

m-ef134c5a.t: Cyprus regulates cash registers as 'fiscal electronic devices' in regulations under Law 4/1978, not in the Law itself. K.D.P. 224/2010 (Official Gazette No. 4429, 21 May 2010) is a notification under Regulation 7(6) of the 1997 regulations on invoices, receipts and records (K.D.P. 29/97); it revised the technical specifications earlier published as K.D.P. 179/1997 and K.D.P. 108/2005. Tax Department Circular 2015/21 (26 November 2015) says receipts come from printed books of lawful receipts or from a device approved by the Electromechanical Services Department with its fiscal memory activated. CyLaw's K.D.P. indexes for 2021-2026 list no later instrument on the subject (5 October 2026).

m-e7acc44b.t: CRS self-certification at account opening has a statutory basis in Cyprus beside the ministerial decrees. Annex I, Section IV.A of the Administrative Cooperation in the Field of Taxation Law 205(I)/2012, added by Law 60(I)/2016 (Official Gazette no. 4564, 25 April 2016; transposes Directive 2014/107/EU), requires a Reporting Cyprus Financial Institution, on opening a new individual account, to obtain a self-certification that lets it determine the holder's tax residence(s) and to confirm that it is reasonable in light of the information collected at opening, including AML/KYC documentation. The text stands in the CyLaw consolidation read on 5 October 2026, which runs to Law 123(I)/2026.

m-dbb8f4c7.t: For tax year 2025 the personal return duty in Cyprus still turns on €19,500: Decree K.D.P. 52/2025 (Gazette No. 5928, 21 February 2025) exempts every natural person whose gross income in 2025 does not exceed €19,500 from filing a return for 2025. The Tax Department's announcement of 18 June 2026 reads it as a duty on employees, pensioners and the self-employed above €19,500, filed through TAXISnet by 31 October 2026; the extending decree, K.D.P. 260/2026, does not cover a self-employed person obliged to prepare audited or reviewed accounts. Late filing costs €150 (s. 50A(α) of Law 4/1978, per the announcement). Returns for tax year 2026 onward are filed only through Tax For All.

m-d3a41576.t: Cyprus Law 38(I)/2026 (Official Gazette no. 5081, 27 March 2026; transposes Directive (EU) 2023/2226; deemed in force from 1 January 2026, s. 20(1)) changed the self-certification rules in Annex I of Law 205(I)/2012. Where, in exceptional cases, a reporting institution cannot obtain a self-certification for a new account in time for the reporting period in which the account was opened, it applies the due-diligence procedures for pre-existing accounts until the self-certification is obtained and validated (new Section VII.Aa). Its report must now say whether the account holder, and each reportable controlling person, provided a valid self-certification (Section I.A.1).

m-d355472b.t: Cyprus enforces card acceptance by inspection, not by a technical link. Article 32A of Law 4/1978, inserted by Law 243(I)/2025, lets the Tax Commissioner seal a business for up to ten days, after three notices, where it owes more than EUR 20,000, obstructs an audit, 'did not issue the invoices or receipts' the Law requires, or misses a set number of returns (two tax, twelve withholding or three VAT returns, counted from 1 January 2027); refusing cards is not a ground and stays under the fine of Article 50ΣΤ. The Cyprus Mail (20 July 2026), citing Tax Commissioner Sotiris Markides, reported inspections of whether businesses issue lawful receipts 'and allow customers to pay by card'.

m-cb2b0b49.t: For Cyprus's first-employment exemptions the Tax Department does not count 'gain or profit from holding an office' as remuneration from employment (Circular 4/2024, para 11(iii), on art. 8(23A); Circular 10/2022, part I, 1(β)(iii), on arts 8(21A) and 8(23A)). Read plainly, a fee paid to a founder merely as director is outside both reliefs. One bridge exists: pay as Executive Director received alongside employment remuneration in Cyprus is counted with it - under Circular 10/2022 only in the same company or one of the same consolidated group, under Circular 4/2024 in the same or another company, 'connected or not'. This matters for the €55,000 threshold of the 50% exemption.

m-c74d467a.t: Dates of the bookkeeping duties in art. 30 of Cyprus's Law 4/1978, per Tax Department Circular 2015/21 (26 November 2015): Law 135(I)/2005, in force 1 January 2006, brought the general duty to keep books and prepare accounts, the Commissioner's power of on-site audit and the period within which he may audit; Law 136(I)/2010, in force 1 July 2011, added subsections (4)-(7): inspection of business premises during working hours, books updated by the end of the fourth month after the month of the transactions, invoices issued within 30 days of the transaction, and a yearly stock count. In 2015 books were kept at least six years from the end of the tax year, wording replaced by Law 243(I)/2025.

m-b9dc79f0.t: First direct-tax dates of a Cyprus company incorporated in October 2026 (Law 4/1978 as amended from 1 January 2026): notice for the Tax Register within 60 days of incorporation - 30 November 2026 if incorporated on 1 October, 30 December if on 31 October (s. 5A(2)); its own estimate of 2026 chargeable income by 31 December 2026 (s. 24, third proviso), the provisional tax paid in one instalment by that day (s. 38(1)(γ), proviso). On 5 Oct 2026 the Tax Department's calendar shows an undated 'an extension will be given' in its 31 December 2026 provisional-tax row, but the row is titled 'for 2025' and may be a leftover. Sections 24-26 do not address a company expecting no chargeable income.

m-b3c01001.t: Cyprus's first-employment tax exemptions need no application or approval. The Tax Department's FAQ on art. 8(23A) (updated 6 August 2026) says that, as with arts 8(21A) and 8(21B), there is no application-approval procedure: an eligible taxpayer benefits through his employer's PAYE by completing form T.D.59 (given to the employer yearly), and must keep evidence - for example foreign payslips, contracts, proof of foreign social insurance, leases, a foreign tax residence certificate for the last 15 years. A tax ruling may be requested for the Department's official position. Art. 8(23A) does not cover the self-employed and is independent of non-domicile status: both may be claimed together.

m-b136b820.t: Milestone 208 of Cyprus's recovery plan - direct taxes inside the Tax Department's integrated system (ITAS) - slipped and shrank across the annexes to the Council Implementing Decision. July 2021: Q2 2024, 'direct taxes of natural and legal persons' operational in the system. June 2025: the same, moved to Q1 2026. December 2025: Q1 2026, with employers' withholding, income tax for individuals and for non-individuals and the defence contribution 'included in the ITAS'. July 2026: Q1 2026, but only employers' withholding (PAYE), defence tax and the controlled-transactions summary table, 'ready to be put into productive operation'; income tax of individuals and companies is no longer listed.

m-b0047d6b.t: Since 1 January 2026 an institution that holds electronic money for customers is a 'Depository Institution' for CRS purposes in Cyprus: Law 38(I)/2026 (Official Gazette no. 5081, 27 March 2026, deemed in force from 1 January 2026) rewrote the definition in Annex I, Section VIII of Law 205(I)/2012 to cover an entity that 'holds electronic money or central bank digital currencies for the benefit of customers'. The same Law excludes from reporting a depository account representing all the e-money held for a customer if the rolling 90-day average of its end-of-day balance did not exceed USD 10,000 on any day of the calendar year.

m-ab254eed.t: A non-domiciled shareholder stops his own Cyprus company from withholding special defence contribution on his dividends with form T.D.624/ΦΠ (2017), a declaration for exemption of a natural person from deduction of the contribution. Per the form's notes it is submitted to the organisation that pays the interest, dividends or rent, one form per source of income; the payer must let the Commissioner inspect it or hand it over on demand; the declarant tells the payer in writing within one month if he ceases to qualify. The Tax Department's domicile page (updated 11 September 2026) lists the form but says of all its forms that they go to the District Tax Office - at odds with the form's note.

m-a363cb61.t: As of 5 October 2026 the Cyprus Tax Department accepts a natural person's request for registration in the Tax Register (issue of a tax identification number, TIN) only electronically through the Tax For All (TFA) portal: the person first creates a TFA account, then chooses 'register as a new taxpayer'. The TIN is sent by e-mail when registration is completed. A person who has CY Login can use it to sign in instead of creating a separate TFA account. Applies to every individual, Cypriot or not. The page publishes no processing time.

m-9baf041f.t: What the Tax Department asks to see for an individual's tax residence certificate, per its page read 5 October 2026 - for 'foreigners': a copy of the 'Yellow Slip', passport or identity card, title deed or tenancy agreement, a recent utility bill (under six months), an employment agreement or contract, a statement of the insurance account from the Social Insurance Services, and, if any, children's school attendance certificates and a car title; Cypriots file the same without the Yellow Slip. The list names only the 'Yellow Slip' - in common usage the Union citizen's registration certificate - and no residence permit of a third-country national. The page publishes no processing time.

m-9936b4f3.t: A Cyprus resident without a domicile of origin who is about to be deemed domiciled (17 of 20 years) applies for the alternative special defence contribution regime of art. 3Δ of Law 117(I)/2002 on form T.D.631 (2026), listed on the Tax Department's domicile page (updated 11 September 2026) with Circular 02/2026 of 29 May 2026. Per the form's instructions it is signed, scanned and sent as a Tax For All message (reason 'application for extension of non-dom status') by 30 June of the first year of the five-year period, or up to two years before the year domicile would be deemed acquired; the €250,000 for the period is paid by the end of the month after the Commissioner accepts the application.

m-97df033d.t: Where the reason for a non-Cypriot's tax registration is employment in Cyprus and he holds neither a Union-citizen registration certificate nor a residence permit, the Tax Department (page read 5 October 2026) asks for one of: a letter from the employer with the terms of employment, a stamped employment contract, or a copy of the hiring notification submitted in the Ergani system with status 'Submitted'; the social insurance number must be declared in the request. For registration as a tax resident under the 60-day rule it asks for an identification document, a letter describing the reason, and a title deed or a stamped purchase or tenancy contract.

m-94610ae9.t: The first income tax return of a Cyprus company incorporated in October 2026 is for tax year 2026 and is due on 31 January 2028: s. 5(1A) of Law 4/1978 gives a person whose accounts must be audited or reviewed until 31 January of the second year after the tax year, and every company files whether or not it has income. Under the last proviso to s. 38(1)(α), for tax year 2026 onwards, the balance of tax falls due on the same 31 January 2028 - no longer on 1 August of the year after the tax year, as for tax years 2020-2025. Both dates are statutory and the return date may be extended by decree of the Council of Ministers.

m-9419e125.t: Per the Cyprus Tax Department's page on registering individuals in the Tax Register (updated 28 September 2026, read 5 Oct 2026), a foreign director who registers in order to sign the IR4 return must attach a recent certificate of the directors of the Cypriot company. The line sits among the evidence asked of EU and third-country citizens who hold neither a Union citizen's registration certificate nor a residence permit, so it describes the non-resident director; a director who holds such a document registers with it. The page does not say that every director must be registered, only what a director registering for this purpose attaches.

m-6b881eb6.t: Form T.D.59 for tax year 2026, 'Declaration for claiming tax deductions', is where a Cyprus employee claims a first-employment exemption in payroll: Part B, line 2, 'deduction for first employment'. Its note 7 offers three options - 20% of remuneration up to €8,550; 50% where the salary exceeds €100,000 (interpretative circular 2017/4); 50% where it exceeds €55,000 'according to circulars 2022/10 and 2024/04'. The employee's social insurance number is a mandatory field. As read on 5 October 2026 no line or note of the form names the 25% relief of art. 8(21B), although the Tax Department's FAQ of 6 August 2026 says that relief too is given without an application.

m-6b26480f.t: A Cyprus company registers as an employer with the Tax Department separately from the Social Insurance Services: form T.D.2001 ergod. (2025), uploaded in a Tax For All message, which needs a TFA account linked to the TIN (Department's page, updated 28 September 2026). Employers that withhold income tax or GeSY file twelve monthly returns and an annual one; those whose employees or officers (directors, secretaries) are paid without withholdings file the annual and at least one monthly return. The page also says employers outside these categories need not register - its example: no income tax to withhold and GeSY paid through the Social Insurance Services - and does not reconcile the two.

m-68daf441.t: A founder already living in Cyprus when his first employment there starts may fail the residence test of the 50% exemption. Per Tax Department Circular 4/2024 (8 July 2024), paras 13-14, the 15 consecutive years of non-residence are the tax years before the year in which the first employment in Cyprus starts; that year itself is not counted, whether or not the person was resident in it. Its example: a start in 2023 requires non-residence in every year from 2008 to 2022. One earlier year of Cyprus tax residence breaks the chain. The 20% exemption instead requires three consecutive years of employment outside Cyprus for a non-resident employer immediately before (Circular 10/2022, part II).

m-5e16570f.t: As of 5 October 2026 no rule in force, and no government announcement, was found linking cash registers or card terminals electronically to the Cyprus tax administration. Law 4/1978 (to Law 243(I)/2025) and the VAT Law 95(I)/2000 say nothing on cash registers or such a link. Cash registers are regulated one level down: under Regulations K.D.P. 29/97 and the specifications in K.D.P. 224/2010, receipts come from printed books of lawful receipts or from an approved 'fiscal electronic device' with an activated fiscal memory (Tax Department Circular 2015/21). The specifications' contents list fiscal memory, sealing and licensing, not data transmission; the 25-page scan was not read in full.

m-5c2962f3.t: A foreign employee in Cyprus without an Alien Registration Certificate (ARC) can still register in the Tax Register; every monthly withholding (PAYE) return from 2025 must carry each employee's tax number. The Tax Department's PAYE FAQ (13 June 2025, read 5 Oct 2026) accepts, with proof of employment, one of: the receipt for the ARC fee; a home-country social insurance number with evidence and a photograph; or a home-country tax number with evidence and a photograph. Its registration page for individuals (updated 28 September 2026) asks for more where a permit is only applied for: the payment receipt plus a foreign identification document, a photograph and a letter with evidence.

m-56eb2700.t: What the Cyprus Tax Department asks a non-Cypriot to upload with a Tax Register request (page read 5 October 2026). EU citizen: the Union-citizen Registration Certificate, all sides; if only applied for, the payment receipt plus point-4 documents 'as applicable'. Third-country national: the Residence Permit (kind not stated), all sides; if only applied for, the receipt plus point-4 documents. Point 4: a 'third-country' tax-number certificate, identity card or social-insurance certificate (the page's words for both groups); a recent photograph; a letter of reasons with evidence. Notes closing points 2 and 3: answer 'No' to the question on holding a Cypriot ID or Alien Registration Number.

m-4e4ac2b4.t: Non-domicile status in Cyprus is claimed by a declaration the tax office records; the form has no approval step. The Tax Department's page (updated 11 September 2026) calls it a 'request for exemption' made on form T.D.38 (2016), with questionnaires T.D.38ΕρΑ (domicile of origin) and T.D.38ΕρΒ (domicile of choice), sent to the District Tax Office. Per the form, a tax-resident individual files it with the returns section of the office holding his file 'in the first year of acquiring income from dividends / interest / rent' in which he considers himself exempt; he declares under 17 years' residence in the last 20, and one without a Cyprus domicile of origin ticks box 2 and attaches T.D.38ΕρΑ.

m-4825e6f7.t: Cyprus law gives an individual no day-count deadline for tax registration. Section 5A(1A) of the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Law 4/1978, inserted by art. 5 of Law 243(I)/2025 (in force 1 January 2026), obliges an individual to give notice for registration and obtain a TIN where he is resident in Cyprus and has reached the age of 25, or has income falling under art. 5 of the Income Tax Law; unlike s. 5A(2) for companies (60 days) it states no period. A proviso lets a person with no such income in tax years 2026 and 2027, not yet registered, give the notice until 31 December 2027. A founder who draws a salary has such income and is outside the proviso.

m-3be67e24.t: The Cyprus Tax Department gives no time for issuing a company's tax number on its registration page or in its FAQ (read 5 Oct 2026). The FAQ on the Tax Register (published 2 January 2025) says only that an e-mail gives the number once registration is completed; that numbers issued after March 2023 have eight digits plus a check character and begin with 6; that a director of three companies opens three Tax For All accounts, each with its own e-mail address; and that the name and birth-date fields may hold the director's or secretary's details or the company's name and registration date. The FAQ predates the rule that from 1 July 2026 a company's request must be made through CY Login.

m-314f2785.t: Cyprus's first CRS decree was K.D.P. 477/2015 (Official Gazette no. 4916, 31 December 2015), issued under art. 6(16) of the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Laws and in force from 1 January 2016 (para 42). Para 43 of K.D.P. 161/2016 (20 May 2016) repealed it, so the chain of CRS decrees is K.D.P. 477/2015, 161/2016, 379/2017 and 434/2020, each repealing the one before. The Tax Department's DAC2/CRS page (as served 5 October 2026) lists K.D.P. 477/2015, 161/2016 and 434/2020 under legislation but not K.D.P. 379/2017.

m-31273dd3.t: A Cyprus company with no paid employee had no PAYE filing duty for 2025: the Tax Department's FAQ on withholding returns (published 13 June 2025, read 5 Oct 2026) says companies that have no employee with emoluments need not file any of the PAYE returns for 2025 and that 'new instructions will be given' for the following years - none appears on that page. It adds that an employee with no pay in a month is left out of that month's return, while employees from whom nothing was withheld must appear in at least one monthly return so that the annual return reconciles. This bears on a new company whose director draws no salary.

m-26bcb507.t: The move of company tax registration to CY Login was announced on 9 April 2026: the Cyprus Tax Department said that from 1 July 2026 a request for registration in the Tax Register by legal persons whose Registrar number begins with HE (companies), AE (overseas companies) or Σ (partnerships) 'will be made exclusively when the connection to Tax For All is made through CY Login'. Other entities 'continue' to register through TFA without it - which implies, but does not state, that companies could do so until 30 June 2026. The step concerns only the login, no other CY Login e-service; whose profile must be used is not said. Its registration page still carried the rule on 5 October 2026.

m-249a15f1.t: Cyprus Law 123(I)/2026 (Official Gazette no. 5093, 17 July 2026) transposes Directive (EU) 2025/872 on top-up tax information returns and also widens CRS exchange: s. 3 adds to art. 7(3A) of Law 205(I)/2012 whether a valid self-certification was provided for each account holder and each reportable controlling person, the controlling persons' roles, and whether the account is pre-existing or new and whether it is joint, for taxable periods starting on 1 January 2026. The Law is deemed in force from 1 January 2026 (s. 12(1)); its s. 9 applies from 1 January 2028. It does not change the self-certification duty at account opening.

m-222fc84f.t: Cyprus's 50% exemption is anchored to the first employment in Cyprus, not to the founder's own company. Art. 8(23A) proviso (iv) of Law 118(I)/2002: 'first employment' starts when a person, after 15 consecutive tax years without any salaried services in Cyprus, begins such services for a resident or non-resident employer. Tax Department Circular 4/2024 (8 July 2024), para 10: whoever performed salaried services in Cyprus, of any duration, in the 15 tax years before is not eligible; para 11: services count when performed with physical presence in Cyprus. The Department's FAQ (updated 6 August 2026) adds that changing employer does not affect eligibility. Art. 8(21A) uses the same definition.

m-204ff392.t: Source of the pre-2026 court fine for not issuing receipts under Cyprus income-tax rules: Tax Department Circular 2015/21 of 26 November 2015 (replacing Circular 2007/16) says that under Regulations K.D.P. 29/1997 (in force from 1 July 1997, per the circular) a person who fails to issue an invoice, receipt or cash invoice, or to keep the records, commits an offence punishable on conviction by a fine of up to €1,700, up to three years' imprisonment, or both. It adds that a receipt may be issued from a pre-printed block or electronically through approved fiscal devices, and that the Commissioner may, on application, exempt an activity whose nature and size make receipts practically impossible.

m-15e535c7.t: Cyprus has a third relief beside the 20% and 50% exemptions. Law 17(I)/2026 (Gazette 6 March 2026, deemed in force 1 January 2025) added art. 8(21B) to Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002: 25% of pay from employment in Cyprus, or of an individual's business profits there, is exempt up to €25,000 a year, in the start year and the six following, each year the income exceeds €30,000. It reaches only a person who starts in 2025-2030, was not resident in the seven tax years before the start year but was resident in an earlier year, and worked full time abroad for a non-resident employer for 84 months, or 36 of the last 84 with a recognised degree. It excludes art. 8(21A) and is excluded by art. 8(23A).

m-0a140cff.t: The Cyprus Tax Department accepts the 50% and 20% first-employment exemptions for a person employed by a company he set up himself, on conditions. Circular 4/2024 (8 July 2024), para 36, repeating Circular 10/2022 (1 November 2022): the exemption 'is granted also to persons employed in companies which they themselves or persons connected with them have set up'; but where the company is dormant, or the size of its activity does not justify the remuneration, or it is not registered as an employer with the Social Insurance Services or in the tax register, or has not filed its employer returns, no salaried services are deemed to exist and neither art. 8(21A) nor art. 8(23A) relief is given.

m-051aa5a8.t: The only official text found that spoke of linking Cyprus businesses to the tax administration was a line in the annex to the Council Implementing Decision on its recovery plan, and it is gone. Reform C3.5R9 in the annex of 28 July 2021, and still as amended on 20 June 2025, said the Tax Department's new IT system would include 'connecting businesses to a server held within the Tax Department, without the use of specialised mechanisms'. The amendment of 12 December 2025 renamed the reform 'Digitalising tax collection' and cut its description to 'an IT system as a single point for taxpayer services'; the 2026 annexes keep that. Cash registers and card terminals were never named.

m-f82ca864.t: Cyprus's non-domicile regime survived the 2026 reform. Among individuals, SDC is charged only on those who are both tax resident and domiciled in Cyprus; an individual tax resident for at least 17 of the last 20 years before the tax year is deemed domiciled. New art. 3Δ of SDC Law 117(I)/2002 (added by Law 245(I)/2025, in force 1 January 2026) lets a person without a Cyprus domicile of origin who has become deemed-domiciled opt, irrevocably, for a flat SDC of €50,000 a year, paid as a single €250,000 instalment per five-year period, for up to two periods; the application is due by 30 June of the first year of the period and must be accepted by the Tax Commissioner.

m-f699f4e6.t: Since 5 June 2026 Cyprus financial institutions must ask extra questions of a new account holder or controlling person who declares tax residence in a jurisdiction offering a potentially high-risk citizenship- or residence-by-investment scheme (Tax Department announcement of that date): whether the right of residence was obtained under such a scheme; whether the person holds residence rights elsewhere; whether the person spent more than 90 days in another jurisdiction in the previous year; and where an income-tax return was filed for that year. The list is 'indicative and not exhaustive'. Existing customers who declared such a residence are to be reviewed within six months.

m-f62d8abc.t: The Tax Department of Cyprus (headed by the Tax Commissioner) administers income tax, special defence contribution, capital gains tax and VAT, and receives payments and platform data: CESOP records from payment service providers, DAC7 reports from platform operators and, for reporting year 2026 onwards (first filing in 2027), DAC8 reports. It is the competent authority for the card-acceptance duty of art. 30A of Law 4/1978 (K.D.P. 259/2021 para 5), with fines up to €6,000, and under art. 59(1)(θ) of AML Law 188(I)/2007 it supervises art dealers and intermediaries for transactions of €10,000 or more. Status on 4 October 2026.

m-ee2d6a34.t: Outline (income side), a list not a computation — Cyprus Ltd selling online to EU consumers through a payment facilitator, as of 4 October 2026: corporate income tax 15% from 1 January 2026 (12.5% before); losses carried seven years; provisional tax estimate before 31 July, instalments dated 31 July and 31 December by the Tax Department (Law 4/1978 art. 24); return by 31 January of the second following year where accounts are audited (art. 5(1A)); payroll: social insurance 8.8% + 8.8% up to €5,742 a month, GeSY 2.65% + 2.90%, employer funds 1.2%, 0.5% and 2%; dividends to a resident-domiciled owner: SDC 5% (17% on pre-2026 profits) and GeSY 2.65%; no stamp duty on documents signed from 2026.

m-e7eb3eae.t: Cyprus corporate income tax rate: 12.5% before, 15% from 1 January 2026. The change was made by art. 24(b) of the Income Tax (Amendment) (No. 4) Law 244(I)/2025, which replaced '12,5%' with '15%' in paragraph 2 of the Second Schedule to the Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002. Status on 4 October 2026: in force; the consolidated text on cylaw.org reads 15% and the Tax Department's reform presentation (March 2026) says companies are taxed at 15% from 1/1/2026.

m-d159ccc8.t: The FATCA decree in force in Cyprus on 4 October 2026 is K.D.P. 433/2020 (Official Gazette no. 5360, 18 September 2020), giving effect to the Cyprus-United States intergovernmental agreement signed on 2 December 2014. The chain of decrees is K.D.P. 281/2015, K.D.P. 223/2016 (22 July 2016), K.D.P. 133/2018 (18 May 2018) and K.D.P. 433/2020; the CyLaw K.D.P. lists for 2021-2026 contain no later one, and the Tax Department's FATCA page (published 22 January 2026) lists K.D.P. 433/2020 first. That page also records, on 24 February 2025, an extension of the temporary relief for foreign financial institutions from reporting US taxpayer identification numbers.

m-c88e350d.t: Cyprus stamp duty was abolished: the Stamp Duty (Repealing) Law 239(I)/2025 repeals the Stamp Duty Laws on 1 January 2026. The Tax Department's announcement of 7 January 2026 states that a document drawn up and signed, even by one party, after 01/01/2026 is not subject to stamp duty, while documents drawn up and signed by at least one party up to 31/12/2025 remain subject to it; from 1 April 2026 such documents are submitted through the TaxForAll portal before stamping at a district office (Department's guide of March 2026). On 4 October 2026 a contract drawn up and signed in 2026 (for example a merchant or lease agreement) carries no stamp duty.

m-c4f48d27.t: SDC on interest and rent after the 2026 reform. Interest received by a resident-and-domiciled individual bears 17% under new art. 3B of SDC Law 117(I)/2002 (3% for interest on government savings certificates and bonds and on corporate bonds listed on a recognised stock exchange). SDC on rental income is abolished from 1 January 2026: Law 245(I)/2025 deleted the rent-related definitions and the Tax Department's March 2026 presentation lists 'abolition from 1/1/2026 of SDC on rental income'. The GeSY contribution on such income (Law 89(I)/2001, art. 19) is a separate charge.

m-ae01b05d.t: Income-tax sanctions in Cyprus for not issuing invoices and receipts: Law 243(I)/2025 (in force 1 January 2026) added art. 50(4) to Law 4/1978, making breach of the invoicing and receipts regulations issued under art. 30(1) a criminal offence with a fine of up to €5,000, up to three years' imprisonment, or both; before, the Tax Department's Circular 2015/21 and leaflet of June 2017 gave the court fine as up to €1,700 or three years, under Regulations K.D.P. 29/1997. Art. 50B, there since Law 97(I)/2017 and untouched by the reform, lets the Tax Commissioner fine up to €20,000 for a breach of the Law or its regulations, decrees or notifications, after five working days for representations.

m-ab08ed85.t: Tax self-certification at account opening in Cyprus rests on ministerial decrees under art. 6 of the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Laws, and the first decrees are no longer in force. CRS: the decree in force is K.D.P. 434/2020 (Gazette no. 5360, 18 September 2020), which repealed K.D.P. 379/2017 (17 November 2017), which had repealed K.D.P. 161/2016 (20 May 2016), which had repealed the first decree, K.D.P. 477/2015. FATCA (agreement with the United States of 2 December 2014): K.D.P. 281/2015 (28 August 2015) was followed by a 2016 decree, then K.D.P. 133/2018 (18 May 2018), repealed by K.D.P. 433/2020 (Gazette no. 5360, 18 September 2020). Bank of Cyprus' entity self-certification form collects FATCA status and CRS tax residence, including controlling persons. Read 4 October 2026.

m-a7b0d632.t: Cyprus capital gains tax after the 2026 reform: the rate stays 20% of the gain on a disposal of property - immovable property in Cyprus and shares of companies holding it (arts 2 and 4 of Law 52/1980).
