m-9218df29.t: Procedure at the Business Facilitation Unit as of 5 Oct 2026: the company applies only through the Business Support Center's online service, logged in with its own identified CY Login profile (the upgraded service has taken applications since 30 June 2026). Annex I asks for copies of: the beneficial-owner search certificate from the Registrar of Companies, the memorandum and articles, a title deed or a lease of at least 12 months for business premises separate from any residence, the latest audited accounts where applicable, and proof of the €200,000 investment. Registration is completed in 'no more than ten (10) business days' from due submission; no fee is stated.

m-86cdea76.t: A third-country national holding a visitor's permit in Cyprus (the temporary residence permit colloquially called the 'pink slip', a name absent from the Department's pages read 5 Oct 2026) is barred from economic activity by Regulation 14 of the Aliens and Immigration Regulations: the permit is issued for holidays, touring or exploring the possibility of settling (14(1)), and its holder must not seek or accept employment, paid or unpaid, or engage in or carry on any business, trade or profession in the Republic without the prior written permission of the Immigration Officer, the Regulations' 'Τμηματάρχης' (14(3)). If, without that prior permission, the holder accepts employment, the permit ceases at once and is deemed cancelled; if he engages in or carries on a business, the Immigration Officer may revoke it at once (14(4)).

m-84039127.t: A third-country national already in Cyprus on a visitor's permit has a published in-country route to a permit as employee of a company of foreign interests: the Migration Department's document list for those companies (dated 21.3.2024, read 5 Oct 2026) has a block 'TEMPORARY RESIDENCE PERMIT (CHANGE OF STATUS FROM VISITOR)' with ten items: passport, CV with qualifications or two years' experience, a contract of at least two years, the employer's return-costs declaration, criminal record certificate, medical tests done in Cyprus, proof of housing, health cover, employer's liability insurance, and a 'Letter explaining the reasons for submitting a change of status request'.

m-748561b9.t: Two dated conditions of the Cyprus strategy for companies of foreign interests fall due at the turn of 2026-2027. First, every registered company commits to 30% Cypriot or EU staff within five years - counted, per the Strategy text, from the date the company joined the scheme. The Migration Department's page (read 5 Oct 2026) gives one date: 'after 2.1.2027, the ratio for new hires will be checked', and a company outside the 70:30 ratio is assessed on its merits by administrative decision. Second, holders of Key Personnel permits on a gross monthly salary of €2,000 or more may renew with the same employer without a pay rise only 'until 31.12.2026'; the threshold is otherwise €2,500.

m-6ed6b066.t: A family member of an EU Blue Card holder in Cyprus may run a business, which the card holder may not. Art. 18ΤΣΤ(6) of the Aliens and Immigration Law (Cap. 105, as replaced by Law 111(I)/2024) gives family members access to any employment 'as well as to self-employment' under Cyprus law, subject only to the public-authority restrictions of art. 18ΤΓ(5), and art. 18ΤΣΤ(5) bars any waiting period; the Migration Department's page (read 5 Oct 2026) puts it as 'free access to the labour market, including self-employment'. The holder's own access under art. 18ΤΓ(1) is to highly qualified employment only; the article as consolidated on CyLaw has no provision for self-employed activity alongside.

m-62a32679.t: Residence documents a non-Cypriot holds in Cyprus as of 5 Oct 2026, per the Migration Department: a citizen of the EU, EEA or Switzerland holds a registration certificate (after MEU1) or a permanent residence certificate (after MEU3); a photograph is taken, and fingerprints are not taken from EU citizens. A third-country national holds a residence permit in card form carrying photograph, two fingerprints and signature, taken at the Department in Nicosia or at the district unit of the Police Aliens and Immigration Service. The card of an immigration permit expires after ten years although the right is unlimited; a long-term resident's first permit is valid for five years.

m-6113b351.t: For registering a working citizen of another EU or EEA state, Law 7(I)/2007 asks for less than the Migration Department's list. Art. 10(4)(α) requires, with the application and the €20 fee, a valid identity card or passport and the employer's confirmation of engagement or a certificate of employment, or proof of self-employment; art. 10(4)(β) requires of a person living on own resources proof of income or deposits and of comprehensive sickness insurance. The Department's list (read 5 Oct 2026) adds a Social Insurance registration certificate and contribution statement, four months of paid contributions for the self-employed, and a title deed or stamped rental contract with a utility bill.

m-60e4b020.t: The Cyprus Startup Visa was revised with effect from 1 January 2025, per two firms' summaries, not an official text: Deloitte Cyprus dates the Council of Ministers approval to 18 December 2024, Patrikios Legal (2 January 2025) dates the announcement to 19 December 2024. Both report the residence right going from two years to three, the applicants' minimum shareholding from 50% to 25% and the permitted share of foreign staff from 30% to 50%; Deloitte adds renewals of two years instead of one and validity until December 2026. The decision itself was not seen; the official guide dated December 2024 carries the new terms (three years, 25%, 50%) without naming it.

m-5a515003.t: Where a non-Cypriot's registration numbers are asked for in Cyprus, from forms read on 5 Oct 2026. The Social Insurance Services' form YKA 1-008 (registration of an employed or self-employed person) has three identifier fields - identity card number, alien registration number, passport number - and a box filled in only by EU and EEA citizens. The EU citizen's form MEU1 in turn asks, for the 'worker' ground, the employer's registration number, the applicant's Social Insurance number and the Services' registration certificate, so Social Insurance registration comes before the registration certificate on that ground. The police district units ask for the ARC number in every appointment request.

m-5287cd14.t: Where Cyprus immigration applications are filed, per the Migration Department's service instructions (posted 19 December 2025, read 5 Oct 2026). Persons living outside Nicosia district are served by the district police Aliens and Immigration Unit, by appointment. Eleven categories are examined only at the central offices in Nicosia, among them immigration permits, long-term resident status, companies of foreign interests, the EU Blue Card, digital nomads and the Startup Visa. There an appointment is needed only for immigration permits, long-term resident status and students; other applications, biometrics and collection are first-come, first-served, 08:00-14:30 (last entry 14:00).

m-4ffe9b78.t: From 1 September 2026 an application for a Cyprus immigration permit in categories A to F must also carry medical documents, per the Migration Department's announcement of 25 June 2026: original blood test results 'conducted abroad' showing that the applicant and dependants do not suffer from hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV or syphilis, and an original chest X-ray for tuberculosis from the country of origin or last lawful residence, duly certified or legalised. They are not required again where the applicant already holds a temporary residence permit in the Republic for which the tests were filed and remain on file. The rule is carried by an announcement, not by the Regulations.

m-4ecddef3.t: As of 5 Oct 2026 a citizen of the EU, the EEA or Switzerland files the registration application on form MEU1 (file MEU1B_20260309) at the Migration Department's headquarters in Nicosia if living in Nicosia district, and elsewhere at the district unit of the Police Aliens and Immigration Service (Limassol, Larnaca, Paphos, Famagusta), which give appointments by e-mail. The applicant attends in person for a photograph. The page says a decision comes 'within one month at the latest' on a complete application, and that the certificate is sent by post and has no expiry date; the form says it is handed over where the application was filed. Art. 10(2) of Law 7(I)/2007 says 'immediately'.

m-47417d27.t: Long-term resident status gives a third-country national in Cyprus equal treatment with citizens in access to employment and self-employed activity, except activities involving public authority or reserved by law to Cypriot or EU citizens (Cap. 105, art. 18ΙΖ(1)(α)). The Immigration Control Committee grants it after five years of legal, continuous residence (art. 18Η(1)) subject to stable resources, health insurance and Greek at level A2 (art. 18Θ(1)); students and holders of a formally limited permit are excluded (art. 18Ζ(2)). As of 5 Oct 2026 form MLT3 is filed only at the Migration Department in Nicosia by appointment; fee €30; examination 6 to 12 months; first permit five years.

m-3f9f0988.t: A citizen of another EU or EEA state who has resided legally in Cyprus for a continuous period of five years has the right of permanent residence (Law 7(I)/2007, art. 14(1)); continuity is not affected by absences of up to six months a year in total (art. 14(3)) and the right is lost only by absence exceeding two consecutive years (art. 14(4)). A permanent residence certificate is issued on application for a €20 fee (art. 17(1)). As of 5 Oct 2026 the form is MEU3 (EU citizens' file MEU3B-EUROPEAN_20260309) and the Department's list asks for the MEU1 certificate, monthly Social Insurance contribution statements and tax returns for the last five years, and five years of utility bills.

m-36f88f46.t: Under Law 7(I)/2007 a citizen of another EU or EEA state may stay in Cyprus for up to three months with no condition other than a valid identity card or passport (art. 8(1)). Beyond three months the right of residence exists if he or she is an employed or self-employed worker in the Republic, or has sufficient resources and comprehensive sickness insurance cover in the Republic, or is enrolled as a student with such insurance and a declaration of sufficient resources, or is a family member accompanying or joining such a citizen (art. 9(1)(α)-(δ)). The authority may not fix an amount that it regards as sufficient resources and must take the person's own situation into account (art. 10(5)).

m-360e267c.t: The CyLaw consolidated text of the Cyprus Aliens and Immigration Law (Cap. 105) is one amendment behind on 5 Oct 2026: its amendment history ends at Law 149(I)/2024, while Law 4(I)/2025 (Official Gazette No. 5026 of 14 February 2025) amends 49 of its sections and repeals Annex III. Most changes replace 'Minister' or 'Minister of Interior' with the Deputy Minister of Migration and International Protection or the Council of Ministers; the power to fix single-permit fees by decree (art. 18ΥΕ(1Α)) passes from the Minister of Interior to the Council of Ministers. In the long-term-resident part only arts 18ΣΤ and 18Η(1Α)(β) change; arts 18Η(1), 18Θ, 18Ι and 18ΙΖ are not touched.

m-32d60f73.t: Apart from the Minister's discretion under Regulation 6(2), Cyprus grants an immigration permit (permanent residence) to a third-country national only in one of six categories of Regulation 5 of the Aliens and Immigration Regulations: A-D are self-employment (agriculture; mining; a trade or business; a profession or science), E non-temporary employment creating no undue competition, F a secured annual income. The Immigration Control Committee reports; the Minister - now the Deputy Minister of Migration (Law 23(I)/2024, art. 18(1)) - may grant. As of 5 Oct 2026 form MIP2 is filed only in Nicosia, by appointment; fee €500 per application plus €70 for an Alien Registration Certificate.

m-3132a2c1.t: On 6 July 2026 the Cyprus Migration Department launched online renewal of residence permits through a verified CY Login profile. It covers renewals only, 'not initial applications', for five categories: remunerated employment, domestic employment, employees of companies of foreign interests, family reunification with long-term residents or with those employees, and long-term residents; in the employment categories only with the same employer. Windows per the Department (read 5 Oct 2026): 60 to 30 days before expiry for employment and domestic work, 90 to 30 days for the others. Signature and biometrics still need a visit; family members of Cypriot or EU citizens are excluded.

m-2dcbe55e.t: Support staff in a Cyprus company of foreign interests are capped: under the government's Strategy (update of 5 February 2024, action 2) third-country nationals on a gross monthly salary below €2,500 may be employed only if they do not exceed 30% of all support staff and hold an employment contract certified by the competent authority; their pay follows the general legislation. The same text says that to obtain permits for third-country staff a company must produce certificates of registration with the Registrar of Companies and with the Tax Department. The Migration Department's page (read 5 Oct 2026) mentions for support staff only the labour-market test and sealed contract, not the cap.

m-2d370a77.t: Cyprus transposed the recast EU Blue Card Directive (EU) 2021/1883 by amending the Aliens and Immigration Law (Cap. 105, arts 18ΣΒ-18ΥΒ): per the Migration Department, Law 111(I)/2024 was published on 1 August 2024. Decrees of the Minister of Labour of 19 December 2024 limit the card to three sectors - ICT, pharmaceuticals for research, and maritime excluding captains and crew (K.D.P. 456/2024; quota zero elsewhere) - and set the minimum gross annual salary at €43,632 (K.D.P. 457/2024). Fees decree K.D.P. 200/2025 took effect on 7 July 2025: €110 with entry permit, €95 issue or renewal, €40 for mobility. It is a permit for employment under an employer, not for self-employment.

m-27775d33.t: What registering a company of foreign interests in Cyprus required in December 2022 against October 2026 (two versions of the Business Facilitation Unit's page). Archived 6 December 2022: application by e-mail with an 11-item annex (company certificates, a director's affidavit on ownership, the beneficial owners' passports, tax clearance and others), and the €200,000 deposit or investment was asked of the beneficial owner in the two shareholding cases only ('In both cases above'). Page modified 23 September 2026: online only, a 5-item annex built on the beneficial-owner register search certificate, and the investment criterion 'applicable in all the cases'.

m-274f56d1.t: Category F of the Cyprus immigration permit (third-country nationals living on their own income) does not settle what its holder may do in a company. Regulation 5(στ) requires only the Immigration Control Committee's recommendation that the person has at his full and free disposal a secured annual income of the amount in the First Schedule: 5,600 for the applicant and 2,700 for the spouse and each dependant (Cyprus pounds, Schedule of 26.7.2002). The Migration Department's page (read 5 Oct 2026) gives at least €9,568 plus €4,613 per dependant, from abroad, for a living 'without having to engage in any business, trade or profession in the Republic' - not worded as a ban.

m-234662a8.t: What a holder of the Cyprus investor immigration permit (Regulation 6(2) policy, 4th revision in force 2 May 2023) may do in a company: applicant and spouse confirm that they do not intend to undertake any form of employment in the Republic, 'with the exception of their employment as Directors in a Company in which they have chosen to invest under this policy' (para 3.3). Where the investment is not in a company's share capital they 'are permitted to be shareholders in companies registered in Cyprus', dividends are no obstacle, and in such companies they 'may also hold the position of an unpaid Director' (para 3.4). A statement of non-employment is filed with the application.

m-21ef109f.t: A citizen of another EU or EEA state who stays in Cyprus for more than three months must register within four months of the date of arrival (Law 7(I)/2007, art. 10(1)). Failure to register is an offence punishable by a fine not exceeding €2,500 (art. 10(3)). The application carries a fee of €20 fixed in the Law itself (art. 10(4)); the registration certificate states only the registered person's name, address and date of registration (art. 10(2)).

m-17aeb3d7.t: On 3 March 2026 the Cyprus Migration Department ended, 'with immediate effect', the transitional arrangement introduced by its announcement of 29 August 2023 under which an application for an investor immigration permit under Regulation 6(2) could still be filed on the criteria of the Third Revision (24 March 2021). From that date all new applications are 'examined exclusively in accordance with the applicable criteria in force, at the time of submission, irrespective of the date of filing of the sale agreement to the Department of Lands and Surveys' - that is, on the 4th revision in force since 2 May 2023.

m-14af2c06.t: Migration Department list for form MEU1 where a citizen of another EU or EEA state registers as employed or self-employed (read 5 Oct 2026): passport or identity card; Part III of the form signed and stamped by the employer; a Social Insurance registration certificate and a statement of contributions naming the last employer and salary; for the self-employed a certificate of contributions paid for the last four months; a title deed, or a stamped rental contract with certified signatures, rent receipts and a utility bill. One registering on sufficient resources shows the same identity and address papers, income, bank statements for the last quarter and health insurance or GHS registration.

m-1219cfb3.t: Residence in Cyprus of citizens of other EU and EEA states is governed by Law 7(I)/2007, since amending Law 193(I)/2020 titled the Right of Union Citizens and Certain United Kingdom Nationals and their Family Members to Move and Reside Freely within the Republic Law (CyLaw text amended through Law 96(I)/2023; no later amendment listed on 5 Oct 2026); it harmonises with Directive 2004/38/EC. Art. 2 defines 'Union citizen' as a national of an EU member state other than Cyprus or of a state party to the EEA; the text does not mention Switzerland, while the Migration Department's registration page (read 5 Oct 2026) applies the same procedure to 'citizens of the E.U., E.E.A. and Switzerland'.

m-08ae7fb2.t: Startup Visa at the Migration Department, as of 5 Oct 2026: after the Notification of Initial Approval an applicant abroad applies within six months (consulate or Department), one legally in Cyprus within one month in Nicosia; examination takes three weeks. A person in Cyprus 'with a visitor status' must first ask the Department in writing to change status (reviewed within five weeks). Fees: €120 entry and temporary residence permit, €130 issue or renewal, €70 first registration. The Department's page puts the right to economic activity at two years, renewable for at least one; the December 2024 guide, also on its forms page, says three years, renewable for at least two more.

m-075f971c.t: Permit procedure for an employee of a company of foreign interests, as of 5 Oct 2026: applications are filed only at the Migration Department's headquarters in Nicosia (form BCS, file MBCS4_20260309); biometrics may be given at the district police immigration unit. Fees (K.D.P. 284/2022, in force 18 July 2022): €70 for an entry and residence permit, €80 for issue or renewal, each valid up to three years; first registration in the Aliens' Register adds €70. The Department's page publishes an examination time of one month; its form and Cap. 105 art. 18ΥΖ(1) set four months. Renewal with the same employer may be filed online 90 to 30 days before expiry through CY Login (since 6 July 2026).

m-073c06f1.t: A third-country national already living in Cyprus under another status may apply for the Digital Nomad permit without leaving: the Migration Department's page (read 5 Oct 2026) says a person who 'legally resides in Cyprus under a different status ... has the right to submit the relevant application' at the Department in Nicosia; others apply within three months of arrival. The first permit is valid for one year and a renewal for at most two; family members get permits for the same period 'without the right to be employed' or to perform any economic activity in Cyprus. A holder who stays more than 183 days in a tax year is, per the page, a Cyprus tax resident if not tax resident elsewhere.

m-06385f93.t: A second duration on Cyprus's business portal concerns an EU citizen's own registration: its page 'Social Insurance Registration and Contributions' (modified 12 August 2024, read 5 Oct 2026) says an EU citizen may look for work for four months before applying for a Registration Certificate at the Migration Department (Nicosia residents) or the district immigration offices, and that the certificate, 'if approved is issued immediately', on an identity card or passport, the employer's confirmation or a certificate of registration as self-employed with the Social Insurance Services, and a €20 fee. The page still names form MEU1A; it is the portal's statement, not the Migration Department's.

m-dce394ab.t: Providers' own texts read 4-6 October 2026; no sign-up tested. (iii) A newly formed company: Bank of Cyprus takes an online application, completed at a branch; Eurobank's account pages give no checklist, only a meeting, while its Basic Terms list what a legal person must produce; Alpha prices packages only for 'corporate current accounts' and publishes no checklist; Revolut Business, Viva and myPOS onboard online. A non-citizen resident: Alpha's online opening is for EU citizens only; Eurobank's app needs a Cypriot biometric ID while its branches accept an Alien Registration Certificate; Wise asks a passport or national ID and country of residence; Viva verifies identity by video.

m-cd071ca3.t: Bank of Cyprus's online 'Business Sight Account' (page read 6 October 2026) is for companies only: its FAQ says it is 'available to all companies registered in Cyprus, including private companies, public companies and partnerships' that subscribe to 1bank, all directors must approve online, and an application may be rejected if the company 'does not have the legal form of a private company, public company or cooperative'. The two lists disagree (partnerships against cooperatives); neither covers a natural person trading in his own name.

m-c0c38627.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus publishes no eligibility list or document checklist for a business account on its business pages (read 6 October 2026). Its 'myAlpha Business' transaction packages, €5 (Core) or €8 (Smart) a month under terms in force from 1 August 2025, are 'addressed exclusively to Small Businesses' served by its Retail Banking Business Area, defined as 'companies approved for servicing' by that area, and are 'only offered in combination with corporate current accounts in euro'. The terms do not say whether a sole trader or a business name counts as such a business.

m-a6774c4d.t: Whether a Cyprus self-employed person may take card payments into a personal account, per texts read 4-6 October 2026: the law, the decree as amended and Directive 20/2021 set no account rule; JCC credits 'existing current accounts' at any local bank, under the name in the bank's system; SumUp accepts a personal account in the profile holder's name; Stripe tests the name, Shopify the account type (euro, SEPA, not savings or money-transfer services); myPOS, Viva and Revolut Pro credit their own account in his name, and myPOS bars using its service 'for your personal purposes that are not related to your business'. Eurobank says its personal Current Account suits the self-employed.

m-8d34a8f6.t: Wise's article on verifying an EEA sole trader (updated July 2026, read 6 October 2026) has a Cyprus entry with two forms. A self-employed person trading in his own name gives his tax identification or VAT number and, if Wise cannot find him in a registry, uploads a Tax Register certificate or confirmation, a VAT registration certificate or a Tax For All confirmation. One trading under a business name gives its 'EE' number and the business-name certificate or a copy of the application. The owner shows a passport, national ID or similar (no driving licence) and gives his country of residence and full address; an uploaded proof of the business must be valid or issued within 6 months.

m-713a3391.t: Providers' own texts read 4-6 October 2026, no sign-up tested. (i) A self-employed person trading in his own name: Bank of Cyprus's business onboarding covers only a company, a business name and a building committee, and no Bank of Cyprus page read names a route for him; Eurobank says its personal Current Account suits self-employed persons; Wise has a Cyprus 'personal name' sole-trader route on a tax or VAT number; Revolut offered Pro to unregistered freelancers (2025 snapshot); Viva's form asks a registry or VAT number; myPOS listed sole traders (2025 snapshot). (ii) A business name: Bank of Cyprus publishes a checklist and Wise takes the EE number; Eurobank and Alpha publish nothing.

m-70cba4f6.t: Eurobank Limited (Cyprus; Hellenic Bank until its change of name effective 2 September 2025, per GLEIF) lists 'Self employed persons' among those its personal Current Account suits (undated page read 6 October 2026). Opening needs documents confirming identity, income, contact details and 'Professional activity details', by meeting, at a branch or in its mobile app. Its Business Current Account page names no eligible legal form and no documents and offers only 'Book a virtual or physical meeting at your preferred branch or contact us.' No Eurobank page names a business name as an account holder; for a company the documents are set in its published Basic Terms, not on its account pages.

m-62fb9dcf.t: myPOS's Cyprus site (undated, read 6 October 2026) offers a 'free myPOS business account' with no set-up or monthly service fees, opened in its mobile app: the applicant completes an online identification, the myPOS team reviews and verifies the information, then the account is set up. The account is provided by myPOS Ltd, an e-money institution authorised by the Central Bank of Ireland (licence C475122). The page names no eligible legal forms; myPOS's help article listing sole traders, self-employed individuals, private limited companies and partnerships could be read only in 2025 web-archive copies, the live help centre returning a bot challenge.

m-49897731.t: Revolut's Cyprus site described 'Revolut Pro' as 'a simplified business account available within the personal Revolut mobile app' for 'freelancers, sole traders, and side-hustlers', usable 'if you're not registered in your local business registry (depending on regional requirements)', with no extra subscription fee; card acceptance cost €0.20 + 1% online for domestic personal cards, €0.20 + 2.8% for international and commercial cards, and 1.5% on its card reader. It said Revolut Business is for 'legal entities, partnerships, and certain self-employed people registered in their local business registry' (web-archive snapshot of 8 October 2025, the latest; live page HTTP 403 on 6 October 2026).

m-33f167ee.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus's online-products page (read 6 October 2026) lists one online account opening, 'Alpha Easy 2 Open', an Alpha 100 personal deposit account for an individual over 18 who is 'a European citizen and a permanent resident in Cyprus', with an identity card or passport, proof of permanent residence address in his name not older than 6 months and proof of income not older than 3 months. A relationship officer calls and the documents are signed at a branch or another agreed place; the bank estimates 1-2 business days. The page names no online route for a Cyprus resident who is not an EU citizen.

m-18a33e86.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus's legal-entity 'Customer Profile' form (AB190E, edition 09/2014; PDF created 9 September 2024, read 6 October 2026) shows what it collects from a company: the entity type from a list of legal persons (limited company, partnerships, trusts, foundations and others, plus 'Other'; no sole-trader or business-name entry), registration, VAT and tax numbers, any supervisory licence, links to politically exposed persons, activities and group, two years' financial figures where the bank deems them necessary (or a tax return), and whether shareholders are the beneficial owners. Documents are attached 'according to the Bank's requirements', which it does not list.

m-17342187.t: myPOS's help article 'Is my business eligible for a myPOS account?' (not country-specific), as archived on 14 October 2025 (latest copy; the live help centre answered HTTP 403 on 6 October 2026), admits 'Legal businesses registered and operating in the EU', EEA, UK and Switzerland, adds that 'Businesses can be owned or directed by nationals from other countries as well', and lists sole traders, self-employed individuals, freelancers, private limited liability companies, public companies and partnerships. It excludes, among others, FX speculators, weapons and arms dealers, non-regulated charities and companies with bearer shares.

m-051c9275.t: Viva.com's help article on account registration (not country-specific; last updated 1 October 2026, read 6 October 2026) asks a new merchant for first and last name, company name, 'Business Registry Number or VAT Number', e-mail, phone, website if any, country and estimated annual processing revenue; in most cases Viva 'automatically collects the required information from trusted sources', identity is verified by video, and the IBAN is created once verification is complete. Its Cyprus beneficial-owner article (last updated 30 January 2025) says the declaration must be signed by the company's legal representative (director).

m-fff95a45.t: FBME deposit-guarantee payout: on 9 April 2016 the Management Committee of the Deposit Guarantee and Resolution of Credit and Other Institutions Scheme announced the activation of the scheme for FBME Bank Ltd - Cyprus Branch. Depositors could submit the standard statement of particulars from Monday 11 April 2016 at the Central Bank of Cyprus; compensation was promised within seven working days of an accepted statement, up to EUR 100,000 per depositor, by credit transfer in euro to an account in the EEA, other currencies being converted at the ECB reference rate of 8 April 2016. No announcement gives the date of the first payment; payouts could start no earlier than 11 April 2016.

m-ea81e1d6.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus's General Terms take interest rates out of the two months' notice for a business that is not a micro-enterprise: 'you agree that we can vary the interest rate with which your account is credited and/or debited by an announcement in the daily press or written notice and that any such variation will apply from the date specified in the said notice or announcement' (para 7.9.3) - so worded in the 6th Edition (in force 01/03/2020, archived), the 10th (in force 05/10/2025) and the 11th (2026). None of the three editions has a clause on negative credit interest or a liquidity fee (text search, 5 October 2026); para 7.9.1 treats a reference rate that falls below zero as zero.

m-cd2ff002.t: What the 11th Edition of Alpha Bank Cyprus's General Terms (AB205E, 'Effective from a date not earlier than 21 September 2026') changes against the 10th ('In force from 05/10/2025'): para 7.2, which said only that a revised Charges Catalogue 'will be available at all our branches and on our Website at least 60 days before it comes into effect', now promises 'at least two (2) months' prior notice' of fee changes with a free exit; the preamble makes the Additional Terms, Charges Catalogue included, prevail over the General Terms; para 25 lets the customer as well as the bank sue outside Cyprus. Neither Alpha terms page read on 4-5 October 2026 says the 11th Edition has taken effect.

m-c5daa6b4.t: As read on 5 Oct 2026, neither Bank of Cyprus nor Eurobank Limited publishes a way to finish opening a company's account without a branch visit, and Alpha Bank Cyprus publishes no company route (its online opening is for individuals). Bank of Cyprus, for a company registered in Cyprus: online form with uploaded documents, 'Bank officer will contact you within 3 working days', then a branch visit with all originals. Eurobank's Business Current Account page offers only 'Book a Meeting', and that page says online meetings 'are for consultation purposes only'; it states no time. Bank of Cyprus lets international clients apply through a local professional intermediary instead of visiting.

m-b90ad264.t: Revolut's Business Terms for Cyprus no longer name a court. The en-CY versions archived on 29 January 2021 and 29 September 2022 said 'Any legal action between you and us will be decided in the courts of the Republic of Lithuania'. The version applying from 28 September 2026 (read 5 October 2026) keeps the choice of Lithuanian law (section 31) but has no jurisdiction clause; its complaints section says the customer has 'the right to apply to any competent court'. When the clause was dropped was not traced: Revolut's page lists versions back to 19 August 2024, which were not opened.

m-6188fe65.t: Eurobank Cyprus Ltd charged companies negative interest on euro deposits from 1 March to 30 Sept 2022. Its announcement dated 30 December 2021 set -0.50% a year on all euro accounts with credit balances held by legal entities from 01/03/2022, calculated daily on current, notice and overdraft accounts, debited monthly, with the first EUR 100,000 exempt and fixed deposits priced before the announcement excluded. Its announcement dated 22 September 2022 ended it: 'As of 01/10/2022, the negative interest rates on EUR denominated deposits held by legal entities will be terminated', after ECB rate rises. Both read in Internet Archive snapshots of eurobank.com.cy (1 October, 10 December 2022).

m-53f0bc55.t: In the data embedded in Wise's Cyprus business pricing page (read 5 October 2026), Cyprus and Malta are the only two of the 30 EEA countries whose business status is 'TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE'; the other 28 are 'AVAILABLE'. Worldwide 32 of the 250 listed jurisdictions carry that flag for business - among them the British Virgin Islands, Cayman Islands, Bermuda, Jersey, Guernsey, Isle of Man, Mauritius, Seychelles, the United Arab Emirates and Israel - against 76 'AVAILABLE' and 142 'UNAVAILABLE'. Wise states no reason on the page; the grouping is an observation from the data, not a statement by Wise.

m-533e8a92.t: FBME payout after activation. On 11 April 2016, the first day for claims, the Management Committee of the Cyprus deposit guarantee scheme announced that a strike declared that day at FBME Bank Ltd - Cyprus Branch and 'the lack of cooperation by FBME' kept the special administrator from verifying depositors at the bank; depositors were told to come to the Central Bank of Cyprus, and the Committee warned of 'a possible delay in the payout procedure'. On 14 June 2016 it announced that verification at FBME's premises would begin on 15 June 2016. The scheme's page states that the submission of new statements of particulars 'was completed on 11 April 2018'. No date of first payment is published.

m-3a7c681b.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus's Charges Catalogue for International Clients (valid from 6 April 2026, read 5 October 2026) charges a client it no longer accepts: item 4.12 'Not accepted client fee' is EUR 175 for individuals and EUR 350 for organisations 'per month, for clients with terminated accounts that have credit balances'. Client accounts carry a 'Review Fee on Client Accounts' of 0.5%, minimum EUR 500, on the declared or actual total credit turnover, quarterly (item 4.3). On transfers, a 'Transaction Investigation' costs 1%, minimum EUR 50 per transaction, and a credit transfer 'where enhanced due diligence is required' EUR 20 up to EUR 10,000 and EUR 40 above (Category C, items 4.9-4.10).

m-20115cc8.t: Eurobank Limited's fee table for international clients changed on 3 November 2025, replacing the Hellenic Bank edition 'effective from 01/04/2025' (listed as valid until 02/11/2025). Account opening went from 'Personal Accounts: min €150, Corporate Accounts: min €250' to a single 'Assessment of new business relationship Minimum €200'; the review fee from 'Physical persons: min €150, Legal entities: min €400' to EUR 100 for individuals and a minimum of EUR 500 for legal entities. The row 'Payments with beneficiary country Russia or Belarus: €100' is new: the April 2025 edition has no country-specific charge. The transaction due-diligence fee of 0.75%, minimum EUR 50, is in both editions.

m-fc66548e.t: For a business name registered in Cyprus, Bank of Cyprus's 'Business Name Account' list (PDF created 30 October 2025, read 2026-10-04) asks for the certificate of registration of the business name from the Registrar of Companies and, where the name belongs to a physical person, the owner's identification documents and proof of permanent address - a utility bill from the last 6 months; mobile phone bills are not accepted. Where the name belongs to a legal entity it asks for a board decision of the owning company certified by its secretary and the identification and address proofs of its directors, secretary, shareholders and signatories.

m-fc5b48bc.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus publishes a customer-data-review Q&A listing documents that 'may be requested' from a legal entity during the review process, 'not limited to': founding document and articles of association, certificates of registered office, of directors and secretary, and of registered shareholders (private companies), name-change and trade-name certificates, an operating licence for regulated companies, a group ownership structure; proof of identity, address and financial information for directors, shareholders, signatories and controllers; and audited financial statements not older than two years or, failing those, management accounts or the latest tax returns. It is a review list.

m-f92f3f41.t: How the three large Cyprus banks use Law 31(I)/2018 against a company that is not a micro-enterprise (terms published on 4 October 2026). Notice of changes to terms and fees: Bank of Cyprus none; Eurobank none (ex-Hellenic terms) or two months (ex-Eurobank Cyprus terms); Alpha two months, interest rates excepted. Termination by the bank: Bank of Cyprus immediate; Eurobank 'without notice'; Alpha 15 days, at once on AML grounds. Time to dispute a payment: Bank of Cyprus 2 months; Eurobank 60 days, 7 via online banking, or 2 weeks (ex-Eurobank Cyprus terms); Alpha 2 months. All three disclaim the burden of proving authentication. Courts: Cyprus, exclusive only under the ex-Hellenic terms.

m-f7f1d9da.t: Eurobank Limited's 'International Business Centres & Shipping - Table of Commissions and Charges' (effective 03.11.2025, read 4 Oct 2026) prices customers of those centres separately: 'Assessment of new business relationship Minimum €200', with no enhanced-due-diligence condition; account maintenance for legal entities EUR 150 per quarter per customer; a separate row for accounts without transactions for 12 consecutive months, EUR 100 per quarter per customer; customer or account reviews minimum EUR 500 per customer; changes in a company's structure or signatories minimum EUR 100; overdue closing of terminated accounts EUR 200 quarterly; closing all accounts of a legal entity EUR 100-500.

m-f4855fc1.t: Revolut: Cyprus Mail (18 February 2021) reports that on 17 February 2021 Revolut announced 'its opening as a bank in Cyprus' - it began using its European specialised banking licence there, so that Cyprus customers who upgrade to Revolut Bank hold deposits protected by a deposit guarantee scheme; the company then claimed more than 160,000 customers in Cyprus. Trade press (FStech) dates the launch in ten markets including Cyprus to 4 March 2021. Revolut's own release was not found (its site refuses automated access). This is cross-border use of a licence issued in another member state: no Revolut entity is in the Central Bank of Cyprus register of credit institutions checked on 2026-10-04.

m-f1bd123f.t: On 4 October 2026 the Central Bank of Cyprus' Register of Credit Institutions operating in Cyprus lists four locally authorised institutions (Ancoria Bank Limited, Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd, Cyprus Development Bank Public Company Limited, Housing Finance Corporation), three subsidiaries of EU banks (Alpha Bank Cyprus Ltd, Eurobank Limited, National Bank of Greece (Cyprus) Limited), one subsidiary of a non-EU bank (Societe Generale Bank-Cyprus Limited), three branches of EU banks and four branches of non-EU banks. AstroBank and Eurobank Cyprus Ltd no longer appear; Eurobank Limited is shown with 'previous name: Hellenic Bank Public Company Limited'.

m-f14e6070.t: Eurobank Limited (Cyprus) publishes no document checklist on its business account-opening pages (read 4 October 2026): the Business Current Account page offers only 'Book a Meeting'; the International Current Account page asks for an 'International Customer Questionnaire', a meeting and documents on identity, income and activity. A list for legal persons appears only in its KYC-update FAQ: corporate certificates, memorandum and articles, board resolution, ownership structure, IDs of signatories and owners, audited accounts. Its 'Customer Information Form (Entity)' collects registration and VAT numbers, line of business, source of funds, expected turnover and related persons' roles.

m-eddb9e59.t: Bank of Cyprus' list for a 'Limited Company Account' in the version linked from its online onboarding form (limited-company.pdf, PDF created 30 October 2025, read 4 October 2026) asks for: memorandum and articles certified by the Registrar of Companies; certificates of incorporation, registered office, directors and secretary, and shareholders; the registration receipt for the Beneficial Owners Register; trust deeds where shareholders are nominees; audited or unaudited management financial statements for up to 2 years 'where available', or VAT payments for the last 12 months; a utility bill for the address of the main economic activities; a directors' resolution to open the account; and identification plus proof of permanent address for directors, secretary, shareholders and signatories.

m-ed72066e.t: On 4 October 2026 Bank of Cyprus served two versions of its 'Limited Company Account' checklist at once. The file limited-company.pdf (PDF created 30 October 2025, linked from the online onboarding form) lists five Registrar of Companies documents - memorandum and articles, and certificates of incorporation, registered office, directors and secretary, and shareholders - among the documents to submit. The file company-onboarding-en.pdf (PDF created 22 June 2026, linked from the 'Legal Entities onboarding' page) moves the same five to 'Supplementary Documents (that may be requested)', whose 'submission is not required at this stage'. The dates are PDF metadata; the bank states no version or change date.

m-ebc1b3af.t: Bank of Cyprus serves international clients through twelve International Business Units in Nicosia, Limassol, Larnaca and Pafos. Its account-opening page (read 4 October 2026) says an applicant must visit a Unit in person or apply through a local professional intermediary. The company questionnaire (form edition 01.2017) lists 17 enclosures; beyond the corporate certificates these include a certificate of good standing or incumbency for foreign companies over two years old, all board minutes leading to the current status, a group structure chart, CVs of beneficial owners, bank references not older than 6 months, and financial statements or management accounts for companies over 1 year old.

m-e722b00f.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus publishes its customer-acceptance categories in an AML/CFT policy statement dated January 2020, still linked as 'KYC Statement' on 4 October 2026. 'Unacceptable customers' include shell banks, shell companies, unauthorised gambling and betting companies, customers with regular betting activity and unauthorised providers of financial services. 'High-risk customers' under enhanced due diligence include offshore companies and special purpose vehicles, complex business structures, payment and e-money service companies, companies whose main purpose is lending within a group, and 'clients of international activities where the final beneficiary is under 27 years of age'.

m-de5ed287.t: Eurobank Limited (Cyprus) keeps two inherited contract sets in force, as published on 4 October 2026. Its terms page lists, under 'Hellenic Bank', the 'Basic Terms & Conditions of Use of Hellenic Bank Services' - form OP(CD)123 - 5/2025, valid from 1 May 2025 for new accounts and 1 July 2025 for accounts opened earlier, 57 pages, beside edition 1/2024 'until 30/04/2025' - and, under 'Eurobank Cyprus', the 'General Terms governing the relationship between Customer - Bank' of Eurobank Cyprus Ltd (form A 1.6 E, 68 pages). It says that, after a communication of 29 May 2025 on the merger, 'the terms and conditions that you had agreed upon with each bank will continue to remain in effect'.

m-ddf3a8e8.t: Bank of Cyprus's flat maintenance fee on companies' current accounts first appears in the earliest legal-entities table in its archive, footer 'Version 01 01/10/2016' (PDF created 31 August 2016, listed 3 Nov 2016): EUR 100 a quarter per customer for current accounts without an overdraft, EUR 3 to EUR 500 with one; 'Version 01 01/11/2016' repeats both. The earlier combined table for 'personal and commercial accounts' (effective 01/02/2015, amended 18/01/2016) has a quarterly maintenance fee only for overdraft accounts (EUR 4 to EUR 250), a 'Service Charge for Current A/c' of EUR 2.50 to EUR 34 for enterprises, and a 'Maintenance fee for IBU customers €200 Annually' for legal entities only.

m-d6abbbeb.t: Revolut's two texts on who may open a Revolut Business account in Cyprus disagree. The eligibility FAQ on its Cyprus (en-CY) business page, read 2026-10-04, says the company must be fully incorporated and active, registered in an eligible country, and 'can't function as a charity, operate in the public sector, act as a cooperative, or be registered as a sole trader'; the Business Terms on the same site (applying from 28 September 2026) say accounts 'can only be opened by companies or sole traders'; eligible legal forms are listed at sign-up. Plans cost €10 (Basic), €35 (Grow) and €125 (Scale) a month; Enterprise is custom. Documents asked: identity verification, certificate of incorporation, proof of business activity, proof of operating address, a list of directors and shareholders above 25%. Revolut says it aims to review within 24 hours.

m-d6778d08.t: Hellenic Bank's Basic Terms before and after the PSD2 transposition, from two archived editions: OP(CD)123 - 1/2017 (62 pages) defines the 'Payment Services Law' as Law 128(I)/2009, caps a consumer's or very small business's loss from a lost or stolen instrument at EUR 150 (para 4.9.2), gives other businesses one month's notice of amendments (4.6.2) and makes termination free only after 12 months (4.12.1); OP(CD)123 - 3/2020 (55 pages) cites the 2018 Law, cuts the cap to EUR 50 (4.8.2), drops the notice period for other businesses (4.5.1) and makes termination free after 6 months (4.10.5). Unchanged: other businesses must dispute a payment within 60 days, or 7 days via web banking.

m-cf5bb427.t: Governing law, courts, dormant accounts and set-off in Bank of Cyprus's published terms (read 4 October 2026): the Supplementary Agreement (September 2025, para 22), the 1bank terms and the cards terms are governed by Cyprus law with jurisdiction of the courts of the Republic of Cyprus, non-exclusively - either party may sue in any other country whose courts have jurisdiction. The Supplementary Agreement has no set-off clause and mentions dormancy only as a fee event (para 4.1); set-off appears in the cards terms for card obligations. The fee table of May 2026 charges a dormant notice or savings account EUR 5 a quarter once inactive for 400 days (13 months) with a balance under EUR 200.

m-ca8e5eb5.t: Eurobank Limited's Basic Terms (OP(CD)123 - 5/2025) are one document covering the whole relationship: general provisions, accounts, an embedded 'Agreement for Payment Services' (section 4) that prevails over the rest and over any special terms, online banking (section 5), cards (section 6), transactions and set-off (7), the bounced-cheques register and dispute resolution. The customer also signs 'Account opening documents' (para 3.1.1), which are not published. Fees are those in the Table of Commissions and Charges 'which can be found on the Bank's official website', and the bank may impose or modify charges 'at its sole and absolute discretion', after notice (para 1.13.1).

m-c3bf3a12.t: Revolut's Business Terms on its Cyprus (en-CY) site (version applying from 28 September 2026, read 4 October 2026) are an agreement between 'the company or sole trader' holding the account and Revolut Bank UAB, and say accounts 'can only be opened by companies or sole traders' registered with their local business register. The same site's eligibility FAQ says a business cannot 'be registered as a sole trader': the two texts disagree, and the legal forms accepted for Cyprus are shown only at sign-up. The page's data bind this document to Cyprus alone; Malta has a separate, near-identical one. The acquiring terms also cover 'Revolut Pro' accounts for freelancers and sole traders.

m-c13e5e3f.t: Bank of Cyprus' online 'Legal Entities Onboarding' form (read 4 October 2026) covers three applicant types only: a company or a business name registered in Cyprus and a building management committee. It asks for the business activities and their location, number of employees, annual sales, expected annual credit and debit turnover, types of transactions, frequent payers and payees, and countries of origin and destination of funds; a FATCA/CRS self-certification and supporting documents are uploaded. An officer contacts the applicant 'within 3 business days', then a branch meeting completes the opening. International clients use a separate channel, the International Business Units.

m-bf2a9afd.t: Eurobank Limited (Cyprus) publishes two routes for a first personal account (read 4 October 2026). Mobile app: age 18 or over, a Cypriot biometric ID, an account for personal income and expenses, proof of address in the applicant's name dated within 6 months; dual citizens must visit a branch. Branch: the web FAQ lists European identity card or passport, Alien Registration Certificate, proof of address and, for employees, employment contract, work permit and social-insurance certificate; the bank's one-page PDF gives the identity documents as alternatives ('or') and adds a payslip. No initial deposit; once approved, opening takes 'as little as one hour, to a maximum of five business days'.

m-be82c630.t: The Revolut entity named in the en-CY Business Terms changed twice, as archive snapshots show. On 2 April and 6 June 2020 the party is Revolut Ltd, a UK e-money institution (FCA reference 900562, company no. 08804411), under the laws and courts of England and Wales. On 29 January 2021 it is Revolut Payments UAB (company no. 304940980, e-money licence no. 42), under Lithuanian law and courts. The snapshot of 29 September 2022 shows a version 'to apply from 17 October 2022' with Revolut Bank UAB (company no. 304580906), licensed by the Bank of Lithuania and the ECB - the party still named on 4 October 2026. Which entity the terms in force just before 17 October 2022 named was not seen.

m-bd91bac2.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus's Charges Catalogue for individuals and small companies, valid from 6 April 2026, charges small organisations €12 per month per current account without a limit (individuals €3), €0.25 per accounting entry on deposit accounts with exclusions for ATM, e-banking and card transactions, and a 'Business Relationship Assessment / Review Fee' of minimum €100 per customer where enhanced due diligence is required — collected in advance, not refunded if the request is rejected, and charged again at every annual review of the relationship.

m-bd56c899.t: The notice on Eurobank Limited's terms page about 'the circulation of the revised Basic Terms and Conditions of Use of Eurobank Limited (with previous name Hellenic bank Public Company Limited)', effective 'two months after their availability/ publication', is a standing text, not the announcement of an edition later than 5/2025: the same paragraph, naming 'Hellenic Bank Services', stood on hellenicbank.com on 1 November 2024 (Internet Archive). On 4 October 2026 the page's document list, in English and in Greek, ends with 'Basic T&C (from 01/05/2025)' (OP(CD)123 - 5/2025) for ex-Hellenic customers and the undated 'General T&C' (A 1.6 E) for ex-Eurobank Cyprus customers.

m-bae63db9.t: Bank of Cyprus onboards individuals remotely through its mobile app (read 4 October 2026): the applicant scans an ID card or passport and confirms identity with 'a live selfie', accepts the terms, creates a passcode and enters financial details. A person without an original passport or identity card cannot open an account through the app; only an individual permanently resident in Cyprus with no existing relationship with the bank may then apply by form, uploading the documents electronically and attending a branch in person with the originals to activate the account. The bank states that it reserves the right to reject any application.

m-ba55b778.t: Bank of Cyprus's account-opening page for international clients (read 4 October 2026) states three limits: the bank 'reserves its legal right to decline an application/business relationship for legal, regulatory or any other reason, at any time, without the need/obligation to justify its decision to decline'; it 'may require additional documentation or information depending on the case'; and its 'products and services are not available to customers in certain countries', exclusions 'reviewed and updated on a regular basis'. The page publishes no list of them. A web-based account-opening system, the 'IBU Gateway', is 'offered exclusively to Business Professionals of the Bank'.

m-b51688f1.t: Cyprus's capital controls (first decree K.D.P. 98/2013, Gazette of 27 March 2013) ended by expiry, not by a repealing act: the last two Minister of Finance decrees - the 35th decree on transactions (K.D.P. 85/2015) and the 28th decree on foreign banks (K.D.P. 86/2015), both in Gazette No. 4857 of 13 March 2015 - were in force for 21 days from 16 March 2015, i.e. through Sunday 5 April 2015, and were not renewed; Monday 6 April 2015 was the first day without restrictions. By then the 35th decree limited only cashless transfers out of Cyprus (free up to €1,000,000 a month per person per institution) and cash carried abroad above €10,000 per trip, not domestic transfers.

m-b40d7290.t: Bank of Cyprus's carve-out for larger businesses predates PSD2. An edition of its 'Supplementary Agreement governing the relationship between the Bank of Cyprus ... and its Customers' (form GEN 001-01-1822E, 01/2011, under Payment Services Law 128(I)/2009; Internet Archive snapshot of 1 June 2011) already provided that, for a customer neither a consumer nor a micro-enterprise, 'the two month notice period shall not apply' to amendments (para 20), that the bank may terminate 'with immediate effect' (22.8) and may charge for termination 'even after the expiry of the 12 month period' (22.2). Consumers and micro-enterprises got at least 60 days' notice of adverse changes, 30 of neutral ones.

m-b2d3a6ae.t: How the AstroBank transfer reached customers' contracts. Alpha Bank Cyprus's FAQ says the legal transfer 'was completed on 31st October'. The ex-AstroBank 'Basic Terms and Conditions governing the relationship between Customer and AstroBank Public Company Limited' (PBC1665EN - 11/2025, file last modified 31 October 2025) carry a final-page notice that every reference to AstroBank shall 'be deemed as references to Alpha Bank Cyprus Ltd (Reg. no. 923)'. Alpha's page for ex-AstroBank customers lists that text as the 'Effective version as of November 2025' and the 11th Edition of Alpha's own General Terms as the revised version 'with an effective date no earlier than 21 September 2026'.

m-b176d0fe.t: Changes in Bank of Cyprus's framework agreement between the April 2018 (2nd) and April 2023 (3rd) editions, per both texts: para 3.1, which in 2018 allowed amendments 'to reflect market conditions ... or for any other reason', became a list newly naming 'liquidity costs incurred by the Bank' and 'changes to the cost of funding'; para 4.1 gained fees 'including where the Account is dormant'; para 19.4, which in 2018 allowed termination where the customer 'refuses to provide important information requested by the Bank in the process of updating his file', was recast into lettered grounds 'with immediate effect', with an express money-laundering ground and a KYC ground.

m-b0214e76.t: Wise's EEA sole-trader guide lists Cyprus ('Αυτοεργοδοτούμενος / Ατομική Επιχείρηση'), takes the tax identification or VAT number as registration number and the tax- or VAT-register certificate as proof of existence, and requires a passport or national ID, not a driving licence. But on 2026-10-04 the data embedded in Wise's Cyprus business pricing page marked business accounts for Cyprus 'TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE' and priced no business product (the Greek page shows a €60 set-up fee), so whether Wise now opens accounts for Cyprus businesses is not established. Wise Europe SA, a payment institution authorised by the National Bank of Belgium, has been passported into Cyprus since 03/09/2021.

m-af1abacb.t: Hellenic Bank's right to drop a business customer without notice predates the 2018 payment-services law: its Basic Terms OP(CD)123 - 1/2017 (archived 13 July 2017) gave a consumer or very small business two months' notice and added that 'where the customer is not a consumer or very small business or where it is imposed/allowed/not prohibited under any law to terminate this Agreement with less or no notice the Bank may do so' (para 4.12.1(a)). The edition 3/2020 says 'the Bank may terminate the Payment Services Agreement without notice' (para 4.10.2), as does the edition 5/2025 in force on 4 October 2026. What such customers lost after PSD2 was the one month's notice of amendments.

m-a758fb4c.t: Bank of Cyprus' Table of Commissions and Charges for 'International Business Units Customers' (edition June 2026, listed as in effect on 4 October 2026) charges nothing for 'Opening of new account' as such, but an account-opening application fee of EUR 300 for legal entities incorporated outside the EEA and 'third equivalent countries' and EUR 500 for persons or entities requiring enhanced due diligence (new customers only). Legal entities pay a monthly maintenance fee of EUR 50 (active, EEA-incorporated), EUR 75 (active, non-EEA), EUR 100 or EUR 125 (dormant), and a file review fee of EUR 500 to EUR 2,000, or from EUR 500 where enhanced due diligence applies.

m-a5d0217d.t: Eurobank Limited (Cyprus) prices international clients on a separate 'International Business Centres & Shipping - Table of Commissions and Charges', effective from 3 November 2025 and still served on 4 October 2026: assessment of a new business relationship, minimum EUR 200; account maintenance EUR 150 per quarter per customer for legal entities and EUR 40 for individuals (EUR 100 and EUR 20 after 12 months without transactions); customer or account review, minimum EUR 500 per customer for legal entities and EUR 100 for individuals; a change in a company's structure or signatories, minimum EUR 100; a client account in the name of third persons, minimum EUR 250 per account per year.

m-a1b7c511.t: Business customers' liability and forum under Eurobank Limited's Basic Terms (OP(CD)123 - 5/2025): a customer that is neither a consumer nor a 'Very Small Business' must dispute an unauthorised or wrongly executed payment within 60 days, or 7 days for an account accessible through Online Banking, instead of 13 months (para 4.8.1(a)); use of a payment instrument 'in itself, constitutes proof' of consent and the bank need not prove authentication (4.8.4); the EUR 50 cap is granted only to consumers and Very Small Businesses (4.8.2). The terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Cyprus and its courts have exclusive jurisdiction (11.1.4).

m-a0949156.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus's General Terms kept the core business clauses from the 6th Edition (in force 01/03/2020, archived) to the 10th (October 2025) and the 11th (2026): two months' notice of amendments to every customer, termination on 'at least 15 days notice' for businesses that are not micro-enterprises, a 2-month dispute limit and exclusion of arts 72(1) and 74. Changes seen: by the 10th Edition immediate termination gained a limb for relationships whose risk 'cannot be effectively managed', and dormancy (2020: 24 months without movement) also needs no other active account and an overdue KYC update; the 11th rewrites the fee-change clause (7.2) and lets the customer too sue abroad (25).

m-9e1cccd6.t: Ending the relationship at Bank of Cyprus (Supplementary Agreement, September 2025, para 19): the customer may terminate in writing at any time; a business that is not a micro-enterprise may be charged even after six months. The bank may close accounts without reason on two months' notice (19.3), at once on listed grounds (19.4), and, 'subject to the provisions of any applicable law', at once where the customer is neither a consumer nor a micro-enterprise (19.7). Grounds include money laundering through an account or the bank's reasonable belief of it (c), 'compliance reasons in accordance with the regulatory framework' (i), and refusal or failure to meet KYC and due-diligence requests (j).

m-9cac20d1.t: Bank of Cyprus charged companies for holding euro deposits in the negative-rate years. Its legal-entities fee table of February 2021 carries a 'Liquidity Fee' of 0.50% a year, charged monthly on monthly average euro balances, with EUR 100,000 per customer exempt; by letter of 15 December 2021, 'as a result of the negative interest rates in Euro', the exempt amount was cut to EUR 50,000 from 15 February 2022, fixed deposits being first charged after their first renewal from that date. In an undated announcement the bank said it would cease applying the fee to legal entities' euro deposits from 1 December 2022; the row is in the August 2022 edition and absent from the December 2022 edition.

m-9c2ee1c0.t: Bank of Cyprus's Table of Commissions and Charges for legal entities dated May 2026 (in effect on 2026-10-04) sets the maintenance fee for current accounts without an overdraft at €6 per quarter per account for a small business and €100 per customer for small-medium and large businesses. The €100 row does not restate the period: 'Quarterly charge:' is printed only on the €6 row, in the English and Greek versions. An additional account of the same category costs €100 to open; a 'file update / review fee' is €100 for small to medium legal entities and €250-€750 for corporate group companies requiring enhanced due diligence. No line prices the opening of a company's first ordinary account.

m-99a508a2.t: In Central Bank of Cyprus monetary statistics a company is a 'resident of Cyprus' by registration, not by presence. The Bank's statistics chronology (September 2026 edition) records that under the 'Definition of the Term "resident of Cyprus" for Statistical Purposes Directive of 2008', in force from 1 July 2008, enterprises incorporated or registered in Cyprus are residents 'irrespective of whether or not they maintain a physical presence in Cyprus', and that companies with none, 'known as "brass plates"', moved from non-resident to resident. By inference, deposits of a foreign-owned Cyprus-registered company count as domestic, so the non-resident share understates foreign-owned money.

m-99255639.t: Unauthorised payments where the customer is a business other than a micro-enterprise, Bank of Cyprus Supplementary Agreement (September 2025, 5th Edition): the customer must notify an unauthorised, unexecuted or wrongly executed payment within two months of the debit or credit, not thirteen (para 8.8.1); 'the Bank shall not bear such burden of proof' that the payment was authenticated and correctly recorded (8.8.2); the bank bears no liability under para 8.8.8 for non-execution or defective execution; and it 'may, but shall not be obligated' to give the information the Payment Services Law requires for consumers (6.8). The EUR 50 cap for a lost or stolen instrument is in para 8.8.4.

m-95c3bb0c.t: Central Bank of Cyprus Monetary and Financial Statistics, Table 1 (deposits of non-MFIs with MFIs in Cyprus other than the Central Bank, outstanding amounts): the share held by non-residents of Cyprus (other euro area plus rest of the world) was 38.3% at December 2012 (EUR 26.8bn of 70.2bn), 29.8% in 2013, 30.0% in 2014, 28.5% in 2015, 25.3% in 2016, 23.5% in 2017, 21.4% in 2018, 19.5% in 2019, 17.5% in 2020, 17.8% in 2021, 16.0% in 2022, 14.9% in 2023, 14.2% in 2024, 12.8% in 2025 and 11.9% at August 2026 (EUR 7.0bn of 59.3bn). Rest-of-the-world residents alone: 30.7% in 2012, 14.6% in 2018, 8.1% at August 2026.

m-941b0801.t: Dormant accounts and set-off at Alpha Bank Cyprus (General Terms AB205E, 11th Edition, Section II): a deposit account may be classified dormant after twenty-four months without movement, and only if the customer has no other active account and, 'due to your own fault', the update of customer information required by the Central Bank's AML Directive ('Directive R.A.A. 120/2025') has not been made (para 5.1); no transaction is possible until reactivation at a branch (5.2-5.3); a dormant account with EUR 200 or less may be closed six months after the bank's letter (5.8). The bank 'may, without notice, appropriate or set-off' any account against the customer's obligations (11.2).

m-9013b60d.t: Bank of Cyprus publishes a checklist for opening the first business account of a limited company registered in Cyprus ('Limited Company Account', PDF created 22 June 2026, read 2026-10-04): a directors' resolution on opening the account and its signatories; identification and proof of permanent address for directors, secretary, shareholders and signatories; the Beneficial Owners Register registration receipt; trust deeds where nominees hold shares; financial statements for up to 2 years, or VAT payments for the last 12 months; and a utility bill for the place of main activity. Registrar certificates and the memorandum and articles are only supplementary documents that may be requested later.

m-8d61b287.t: Hellenic Bank put negative rates on companies' euro deposits from 3 March 2020: an announcement (file dated 21 January 2020) set -0.60% on euro credit balances of 'non-households customers' - on current and overdraft accounts only above EUR 100,000, on savings and notice accounts on the whole balance; customers could close accounts free until 28 February 2020 and were otherwise deemed to accept. The Basic Terms of 1/2017 have no such clause; the edition 3/2020 (file created 30 December 2019) and the editions 1/2024 and 5/2025 authorise the bank 'to apply zero or negative interest' to interest-bearing accounts of non-consumer holders (para 1.8.1); editions between were not seen.

m-8cf699dc.t: Unauthorised payments for a business that is not a micro-enterprise, Alpha Bank Cyprus General Terms (AB205E, para 20, same in the 10th Edition in force from 5 October 2025 and in the 11th): the bank is 'not obliged to prove' authentication and excludes articles 72(1) and 74 of the Law (20.1.3, 20.2.5); the customer must notify within 2 months instead of 13 (20.2.1); the EUR 50 loss-sharing rules apply only to consumers and micro-enterprises - others accept 'that any Payment Transaction which is recorded in your Account is authorised'. Cyprus law governs; its courts are non-exclusive: the 10th Edition reserves only the bank's right to sue elsewhere, the 11th both parties' (para 25).

m-83b6bfbb.t: Editions of Bank of Cyprus's payment-account framework agreement: a PSD1-era edition (form GEN 001-01-1822E, 01/2011, citing Law 128(I)/2009; Internet Archive snapshot of 1 June 2011); April 2018 (2nd Edition, 26 pages); April 2023 (3rd Edition), announced by a customer letter of 21 February 2023 with effect from 30 April 2023; July 2024 (4th Edition), adding instant credit transfers (its letter prints the effective date as '01/07/20204'); September 2025 (5th Edition, 32 pages), adding the Verification of Payee service with effect from 9 October 2025. The 2023 letter gave 68 days' notice and told customers that not terminating before 30 April 2023 would be deemed acceptance.

m-829e74c2.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus publishes itemised account-opening requirements only for personal documents (read 4 October 2026). 'Alpha Easy 2 Open' is for individuals over 18, European citizens permanently resident in Cyprus, with identity card or passport, proof of address not older than 6 months and proof of income not older than 3 months; the application is online, a meeting with a bank officer is needed to sign, estimated time 1-2 business days, opening free. The ex-AstroBank International Banking page asks for ID or passport, proof of address, bank reference, CV and a due-diligence questionnaire. No company-account checklist was found on /en/business, /en/international or the ex-AstroBank pages.

m-81df878e.t: Eurobank Limited (Cyprus; formerly Hellenic Bank), in its Table of Commissions and Charges effective 16 September 2026, lists an 'assessment of new business relationship' fee of €50 for individuals, 'applied when enhanced due diligence is required', and 'Legal Entities: Minimum €200' in a separate cell that does not repeat the condition - ambiguous in the English and Greek versions alike. A customer review costs legal entities €50. Account maintenance for current accounts without a limit is €9 for small businesses and €15 for small-medium and large businesses, per account; these rows sit under the 'Monthly Fee' column heading of the overdraft block and do not restate the period.

m-81d3a0fb.t: Hellenic Bank ended its negative rates on companies' euro deposits on 3 October 2022, according to the Cyprus Mail of 14 September 2022: the bank 'on Tuesday announced its decision to terminate negative interest rates on non-household Euro accounts, with effect from October 3, 2022', after which 'the interest rate on all non-household current, savings and notice accounts will be set at zero'. The negative rate had been announced at -0.60% from 3 March 2020; its level in between was not seen. The bank's own announcement was not found; the clause allowing zero or negative interest on non-consumer accounts remains in the Basic Terms in force on 4 October 2026 (OP(CD)123 - 5/2025, para 1.8.1).

m-7fdc66a0.t: Bank of Cyprus raised the quarterly maintenance fee on companies' current accounts with an overdraft twice in just over a year. In the editions from 8 February 2017 to March 2020 the bands were EUR 3 (limit up to 3,000), 5, 35, 200 and 500 (over 1 million); from 1 February 2021 they were EUR 6, 10, 50, 200 and 500; from 15 February 2022 EUR 12, 20, 75, 250 (100,000-500,000), 300 and 500, with a new EUR 100 fee for opening an additional account of the same category and new maintenance fees for notice (EUR 2) and trading (EUR 5) accounts. The May 2026 edition still shows the 2022 bands. Customers were told by letters of 30 November 2020 and 15 December 2021, each two months ahead.

m-7c8ff071.t: At Bank of Cyprus the fee table is part of the contract by reference: para 1.2 of the Supplementary Agreement (September 2025, 5th Edition) lists 'each applicable Table of Commissions and Charges' among the documents it is read with, and para 4.1 entitles the bank to charge account maintenance fees '(including where the Account is dormant)', transaction commissions and other charges 'in accordance with the Bank's Table of Commissions and Charges which is made available to the Customer at the time of opening the Payment Account'. Para 4.3 lets the bank amend the table under the amendment clause, 'without limitation, the increase of commissions and charges or the introduction of new ones'.

m-768a8087.t: Changes and termination under the ex-Hellenic Bank Basic Terms published by Eurobank Limited (OP(CD)123 - 5/2025, still in Hellenic Bank's name; latest edition listed on 4 October 2026): the bank may amend them at any time by website posting, letter, Bank Mail or 'any other way which the Bank considers appropriate' (para 1.2.1). A consumer or 'Very Small Business' (micro-enterprise of Recommendation 2003/361/EC) gets two months' notice of payment-services changes; para 4.5 'will not apply' to others. The bank may close any account on two months' written notice (3.2.1) but, for a customer that is neither, 'may terminate the Payment Services Agreement without notice' (4.10.2).

m-74890ed4.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus's Charges Catalogue 'International Clients', valid from 6.4.2026 (read 4 October 2026), prices account opening outright: 'Opening Account Fee - Individuals: Minimum €250; Organizations: Minimum €500', plus an 'Expedite Account Opening Fee €1.000'. For organisations it adds an account maintenance fee of EUR 60 monthly per customer, a dormant fee of EUR 50 per month per dormant account on top of it, a low-activity fee of EUR 150 per customer per quarter, and EUR 200 per account for closure. A note says the bank may apply 'commonly agreed charges' for assessing account-opening applications where enhanced due diligence is required.

m-73c75f17.t: Bank of Cyprus's published contract set for a payment account, as served on 4 October 2026: the 'Supplementary Agreement governing the relationship between the Bank of Cyprus Public Company Limited and its Customers with respect to Payment Accounts', September 2025 (5th Edition), 32 pages, 'an integral part' of the account-opening terms, read 'without limitation' with the agreement for current accounts with limit (branches only), the Cards terms (form 001-007-0043, 19/06/2026) and Prepaid Cards terms, the 1bank terms (form 001-01-2004A, September 2021) and 1bank Operating Guidelines, 'each applicable Table of Commissions and Charges', and the fax/'Message' authority and indemnity.

m-6eb2fb6d.t: FBME payout, per the scheme's announcements and Central Bank of Cyprus annual reports: on 11 April 2016 a strike at FBME and 'the lack of cooperation by FBME' stopped verification at the bank's premises, and depositors were sent to the Central Bank; on 14 June 2016 the scheme announced that verification at FBME's premises would begin on 15 June. In 2016, 770 depositors were compensated with about EUR 40 million; by end-2017 some 1,140 with about EUR 62 million; the payout was completed in November 2018 with 1,481 depositors and about EUR 83 million. The 2016 report calls 9 April 2016 the scheme's first activation. Claims ran until 11 April 2018 (the activation notice had said 9 April 2018).

m-68260c14.t: Eurobank S.A. announced on 29 August 2025 that it had all regulatory approvals to merge its Cyprus subsidiaries Hellenic Bank Public Company Limited and Eurobank Cyprus Ltd. Its 2025 annual report (approved 5 March 2026) states that, effective 1 September 2025, all assets and liabilities of Eurobank Cyprus were transferred to Hellenic Bank under the Transfer of Banking Business and Collateral Law of 1997; Hellenic Bank was then renamed Eurobank Limited and Eurobank Cyprus Ltd became ERB Cyprus Holdings Ltd, dissolved when the merger was completed on 3 December 2025. GLEIF dates the name change to 2 September 2025. On 4 October 2026 the CBC register lists only Eurobank Limited.

m-5e7a23ef.t: Bank of Cyprus publishes an informative bulletin on documents that 'may be requested' at onboarding or data update under Law 188(I)/2007 and the Central Bank's AML directive; it calls the list non-exhaustive. For legal entities: corporate certificates from the Registrar of Companies, memorandum and articles of association, documents verifying the identity of authorised signatories, registered shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners, proof of the head-office address up to 6 months old, a description of activities with supporting documents, proof of income including group structure and recent audited financial statements or management accounts, expected account activity, and tax residency.

m-56efe016.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus's account contract is one document plus 'Additional Terms', as published on 4 October 2026: the General Terms and Conditions (form AB205E) say the agreement 'consists of these General Terms' and the Additional Terms - the Charges Catalogue, the applicable interest rates and any special product terms. Section I with Sections IV-IX is 'a separate framework contract for the provision of payment services'. Only the 11th Edition ('Effective from a date not earlier than 21 September 2026') adds that the Additional Terms 'form an integral part' and prevail if inconsistent; the 10th ('In force from 5 October 2025') says that only of special product terms.

m-54b1904e.t: AML, dormancy and set-off in the ex-Hellenic Basic Terms of Eurobank Limited (OP(CD)123 - 5/2025, read 4 Oct 2026): a customer who fails or refuses to supply data requested to update identification or about transactions has the relationship terminated and accounts closed (para 1.3.4(b)). Para 3.1.2, on reliance on third parties for identification, activates the account only after a meeting (online allowed), else the bank 'must terminate the customer relationship'. An account without transactions for over 12 consecutive months is dormant only if the holder has no other active account, and is blocked until customer data are updated (3.8). The bank may set off any customer claim (7.1.7).

m-4b7d1253.t: How Bank of Cyprus's termination-for-cause clause acquired its compliance grounds, in three dated editions of its account agreement. The 01/2011 edition (para 22.4; Internet Archive, 1 June 2011) listed death, bankruptcy, dissolution, repeated breach, suspicion or risk of fraud, suspicious transactions and inability to settle - nothing on compliance or due diligence. The April 2018 edition (para 19.4) added 'for compliance reasons', refusal 'to provide important information requested by the Bank in the process of updating his file' and failure to meet its 'Customer Acceptance Policy' criteria. The April 2023 edition recast these as grounds (c), (i), (j): money laundering, compliance, KYC.
