m-467eab9d.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus changed its company account maintenance fee between two editions of its legal-entities catalogue: 'Valid from: 7.5.2025' - current accounts without limit, 'Small Organizations: €60' and 'SME Organizations and Corporate: €100', quarterly per account; 'Valid from: 19.1.2026' (renamed 'Corporate and Small Medium Companies') - EUR 80 quarterly per account for all, with small companies priced in the separate 'Individuals and Small Companies' catalogue. The 2026 edition also adds the Business Relationship Assessment Fee with its EUR 200 three-working-day option and a EUR 200 account closure fee; neither row was found in the 7.5.2025 edition.

m-448569cb.t: How Bank of Cyprus may change terms and fees (Supplementary Agreement, September 2025, para 3): it posts changes on its website or in the press (3.2); a consumer or micro-enterprise is also informed on a durable medium two months before an amendment takes effect, may close the affected accounts in that period without charge, and is deemed to accept if silent; 'where the Customer is neither a Consumer nor a Micro-enterprise, the amendment shall enter into force without prior notice' (3.3) - including fee increases and new fees (3.4). Changes in the customer's favour need no notice (3.5). A micro-enterprise: fewer than ten employees and turnover or balance sheet total not above EUR 2 million.

m-441545a6.t: For customers taken over from Eurobank Cyprus Ltd, Eurobank Limited still publishes that bank's General Terms (form A 1.6 E; read 4 October 2026). A customer that is not a consumer or microenterprise 'is fully and exhaustively liable' for damage from unauthorised use of a lost or stolen payment instrument (clause 2.13), must notify within 2 weeks instead of 13 months (2.15.3) and bears the burden of proving a payment unauthorised (2.16.1.1); the bank terminates 'with shorter or without notice' (2.25.1), but amendments need two months' notice to every customer (2.24.1). All accounts form 'a single indivisible account' for set-off (1.15). Cyprus law governs; the bank may sue abroad (1.25.1).

m-42b3033a.t: Eurobank Limited (Cyprus) publishes a customer-review FAQ listing documents that 'may be requested' from a legal person in the data-updating process, 'not limited to': certificates of incorporation, of registered office, of directors and secretary, and of registered shareholders (private companies), memorandum and articles; a board resolution on opening the account certified by the company secretary; any trust deed between nominee shareholders and beneficial owners; the ownership structure certified by the beneficial owner; identity documents of signatories, shareholders and beneficial owners; and recent audited financial statements or, absent those for two years, management accounts.

m-42a9cae7.t: Eurobank Limited's fee table for International Business Centres customers (effective 3 November 2025, in effect on 4 October 2026): on 'OUR' terms, 'Payments with beneficiary country Russia or Belarus' cost EUR 100, against EUR 15 to EUR 40 by amount for other payments; a 'Transaction Investigation (Due diligence on transactions. When extensive compliance checks need to be performed)' costs '0.75%, Minimum €50' (base not stated). The bank's International Current Account page says an applicant first completes an International Customer Questionnaire and then books 'a virtual or physical meeting' with an International Business Centre; neither names excluded countries.

m-3ea40ea2.t: Company account fees at Hellenic Bank and its successor, by edition. Valid from 16/09/2019: current and trading accounts, legal persons EUR 5-30 a month plus EUR 0.15 per accounting entry; an opening fee (EUR 100 per account) only for provident funds. Effective 02/01/2023: SME accounts (Retail Division) EUR 9.00 and corporate accounts EUR 15.00 per month; opening free under normal processing and, where enhanced due diligence is required, 'Corporate accounts: Min €100'. Eurobank Limited's table published 3 September 2025 with effect from 03.11.2025 and the edition effective 16.09.2026: EUR 9 and EUR 15 (period not restated) and 'Legal Entities: Minimum €200' to assess a new relationship.

m-3dcacbe8.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus's maintenance fee on a corporate or SME current account without limit more than tripled from 2019 to 2026. Catalogue editions dated 05/08/2019 and 03/08/2020 (archived) charge 'Organizations: €25 per account, quarterly'; the edition valid from 7.5.2025 charges small organisations EUR 60 and SME and corporate customers EUR 100 a quarter; the edition valid from 19.1.2026 EUR 80, with small companies at EUR 12 a month under a separate catalogue. For international-sector organisations the 2019 and 2020 editions set EUR 150 per quarter per customer and a EUR 300 assessment fee; the 6.4.2026 edition EUR 60 a month and an opening fee of at least EUR 500.

m-370e162d.t: Starting condition for the 2015–2026 timeline (Central Bank of Cyprus clarification of 30 March 2013, after the Eurogroup agreement of 25 March 2013): Laiki Bank's insured deposits up to €100,000 were transferred to Bank of Cyprus as of 26 March 2013; other Laiki deposits above €100,000 stayed in the 'bad' bank. At Bank of Cyprus the bail-in base was a customer's deposits above €100,000 net of the customer's loans there on 26 March 2013: 37.5% of that difference was converted into Class A shares, 22.5% frozen for possible conversion and 40% temporarily frozen for liquidity. These percentages were announced on 30 March 2013; the final conversion rate, fixed on 30 July 2013, was 47.5%.

m-35c00db0.t: Alpha Bank S.A. announced on 3 November 2025 that its indirect wholly owned subsidiary Alpha Bank Cyprus Ltd, with other group entities, had completed the acquisition of substantially all of AstroBank's assets and liabilities and of its personnel (agreement announced 24 June 2025) - a transfer of business, not a merger of the companies. Alpha Bank's FY2025 results release dates the acquisition to October 2025; GLEIF records it as effective 31 October 2025 and shows ASTROBANK PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED (HE 189515) inactive with a retired LEI and Alpha Bank Cyprus Ltd (HE 923) as successor. On 4 October 2026 astrobank.com redirects to alphabank.com.cy, which has an 'Ex-ASTROBANK' section.

m-35126e32.t: Anti-money-laundering termination at Alpha Bank Cyprus (General Terms AB205E, 11th Edition, para 23.1; same text in the 10th): the bank may terminate the framework contract and close any account 'with immediate effect' if it reasonably believes that keeping the account may breach any law, put its reputation at risk or expose it to legal or regulatory process, 'or if you do not comply with our requests which arise from the regulatory framework in relation to the prevention of money laundering and the financing of terrorism', or if on its risk assessment the risk of the relationship 'is particularly high and cannot be effectively managed'. No notice period is attached to these grounds.

m-2e35f7d2.t: For an individual, Bank of Cyprus's international 'New Account Questionnaire - Personal' (form edition 01.2017, linked from the account-opening page on 4 October 2026) asks for three enclosures: a legible certified true copy of the passport(s) with photograph, signature and expiry date; a bank reference not older than 6 months; and proof of residential address, e.g. utility bill, not older than 6 months. Neither this form nor the company questionnaire of the same edition mentions an apostille, legalisation or translation: the company form asks for a certificate of good standing or incumbency 'for foreign companies over two years old' and is silent on how foreign documents are authenticated.

m-2d832d53.t: Bank of Cyprus's EUR 100 maintenance fee for a company's current account without an overdraft is a quarterly charge per customer: its archive of prior editions prints '€100 Quarterly charge (per customer)' in the legal-entities tables of 01/10/2016, 01/11/2016, 08/02/2017, March 2018, March 2020 and February 2021. The June 2021 edition split the row into EUR 6 per account for a small business and EUR 100 per customer for small-medium and large businesses, both under one heading 'Quarterly charge:' (unchanged in July, August and December 2021). The May 2026 edition, in effect on 4 October 2026, keeps EUR 6 and EUR 100 but prints the heading on the EUR 6 row only.

m-261ac230.t: In Bank of Cyprus' fee table for International Business Units customers (edition June 2026, read 4 October 2026) the surcharges for 'legal entities incorporated outside EEA & Third Equivalent countries' turn on the bank's own list of twelve 'third equivalent countries': Australia, Brazil, Canada, Hong Kong, India, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Singapore, Switzerland, South Africa and the United States. A legal entity incorporated in the EEA or in one of the twelve pays no EUR 300 application fee and EUR 50 a month for an active account; one incorporated elsewhere pays EUR 300 and EUR 75 a month. This is the bank's price list, not a regulatory classification.

m-1deb8d2f.t: Bank of Cyprus bail-in, final rate: on 30 July 2013 the Central Bank of Cyprus, as Resolution Authority, converted an additional 10% of the bailed-in eligible deposits (the 'Excess Amount' under the bail-in decree) into equity, raising the total converted to 47.5%, and declared that as of 30 July 2013 the bank was no longer under resolution (Bank of Cyprus announcement of 31 July 2013). After the conversion bailed-in depositors held around 81% of the bank's share capital and legacy Laiki Bank around 18%.

m-1b8e62b4.t: Wise Business for Cyprus, re-read 4 October 2026: the data embedded in Wise's Cyprus business pricing page still marks Cyprus 'PERSONAL: AVAILABLE, BUSINESS: TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE' - the same status as Malta, while Greece, Lithuania and Ireland are 'AVAILABLE' for business - and all twelve product flags for a Cyprus business (send, card, balance, bank details, payments and others) are false. The contract that would apply is Wise's EEA Business Customer Agreement, last updated 7 August 2026: 'a contract between your Business' and Wise Europe SA, a Belgian company (no. 0713.629.988) authorised by the National Bank of Belgium, for business clients with their seat or registration in the EEA.

m-17df382b.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus's Charges Catalogue 'Corporate and Small Medium Companies', valid from 6.4.2026 (read 4 October 2026): current accounts without limit EUR 80 quarterly, per account; execution fee EUR 0.25 per accounting entry; dormant fee EUR 30 a year per dormant account, on top of the maintenance fee; account closure fee EUR 200; and a Business Relationship Assessment Fee of 'Minimum €100' per customer, 'where enhanced due diligence is required', paid in advance and not refunded if the request is rejected - with, 'to expedite the account opening process', an 'additional charge €200, for processing the request within 3 working days'. The edition valid from 19.1.2026 carries the same rows.

m-140cb701.t: As of 4 October 2026 the customer-facing KYC pages of Bank of Cyprus and Eurobank Limited still cite the repealed CBC directive. Bank of Cyprus' informative bulletin on customer data review refers to 'the 5th Central Bank of Cyprus Directive'; Eurobank Limited's 'Customer Review - KYC' page and FAQ cite 'Section 4.5 (paragraphs 82-86)' and quote paragraph 86 on terminating the relationship and closing all accounts of a customer who fails to supply update data within a reasonable time. That numbering belongs to the February 2019 Fifth Edition, repealed on 2 June 2025; updating of customer data is now governed by para 25 of the Directive of 2025.

m-10f4ce31.t: Alpha Bank Cyprus has a separate Charges Catalogue for 'International Clients' (valid from 6 April 2026, served 4 October 2026). Opening an account costs a minimum of EUR 250 for individuals and EUR 500 for organisations, and an 'Expedite Account Opening Fee' is EUR 1,000; where enhanced due diligence is required the bank may add 'commonly agreed charges'. Maintenance is EUR 20 a month per customer for individuals and EUR 60 for organisations, plus EUR 15 or EUR 50 a month for each dormant account and a low-activity fee of EUR 50 or EUR 150 per quarter; a review or profile update costs a minimum of EUR 150 or EUR 500; closing an account EUR 100 or EUR 200.

m-0a0065a3.t: What Eurobank Limited's Basic Terms (OP(CD)123 - 5/2025) require to open a company account: 'the original or certified copies of the documents used to register the legal person' and proof of its representatives' authority (para 1.3.1(a)(ii)); the certificate of registered office as proof of address (1.3.2); the ultimate beneficial owners and, 'where necessary', their share percentages (1.3.3); signed account-opening documents (3.1.1). Para 3.1.2, on reliance on third parties for identification, has the bank hold 'the meeting' before any transaction; it 'may be held over the internet (e.g. Teams)'. For a cheque account the bank checks the bounced-cheque register and takes references (3.1.4).

m-070bb700.t: Revolut's Business Terms for Cyprus (applying from 28 September 2026, read 4 October 2026) prohibit: dating, escort, adult entertainment; cannabinoids; weapons; trade in antiques, precious metals, stones or art; auction houses and pawnbrokers; counterfeits; chemicals; video-game arcades; debt collection; binary options or gambling; certain financial services; consular services; holding client funds; crowdfunding; streaming; and anything else 'outside our risk appetite'. Charities, political and religious bodies, trusts, SPVs and non-profits may be refused. Closure is generally on 60 days' notice, 30 days for a 'Large Corporation' (ten or more staff, or turnover or balance sheet over €2m).

m-039e07e3.t: Changes and termination under Alpha Bank Cyprus's General Terms (AB205E; same text in the 10th Edition, in force from 5 October 2025, and the 11th): the bank may amend the General Terms and the Additional Terms - which include the Charges Catalogue - on at least two months' notice to every customer (para 22); but for a customer that is not a consumer or micro-enterprise it may vary interest rates by press announcement or written notice from the date stated there (7.9.3). It may end the framework contract on two months' written notice to a consumer or micro-enterprise and on 'at least 15 days notice' to any other customer (23.2.5), or a single payment service on 7 days' notice (23.3.4).

m-fdf9daf1.t: Cyprus firms read on 6 October 2026 disagree on whether a founder can make the HE1 declaration himself. Harris Koufettas & Associates LLC (FAQ of 20 August 2026) says it 'may be sworn either by that advocate or by a person named in the articles as a director or secretary', and calls the cheapest lawful route paying an advocate for the memorandum and articles and filing HE1-HE3 oneself for €165. EasyCorporate (guide of 13 March 2026) says 'Only licensed lawyers in Cyprus are allowed to sign' HE1; Savva Cyprus that a direct filing by an individual 'will result in the paperwork being rejected'; George K. Konstantinou LLC that the online filing is handled by the lawyer.

m-f97d36ee.t: Cyprus law has provided since Law 151(I)/2023 (Gazette 19 December 2023) for forming a company 'entirely by electronic means': s. 366E of the Companies Law has the Registrar issue binding directives on online formation that must cover, among other things, 'the role of the practising advocate ... subject to the Advocates Law', and s. 366ΣΤ has him post template memoranda and articles. As read on 6 October 2026, the Registrar's page on incorporation still asks, 'regardless of the type of company', for form HE1 'signed and sworn before the court by the entrusted lawyer' on the e-filing route, and cylaw's indexes of regulatory acts for 2023-2026 list no directive on online formation.

m-f528b00d.t: The Cyprus Registrar's own texts set an order inside company formation. Form HE1 (served 6 October 2026) asks for the 'number of the application for name approval', and his review criteria (page published 28 February 2019, served 6 October 2026) require HE1 and the memorandum to show the company name 'as approved', so both follow the name approval. The memorandum's date must be the date HE1 is submitted to the Department or earlier, and the articles must bear the same date and the name and signature of the lawyer who drew them up, so the signed documents exist by the filing. No text read orders the swearing of HE1 against the signing of the memorandum and articles.

m-e469b2ca.t: Customs form C.1000 (file of 26 August 2019, read 6 October 2026) asks a legal person to attach copies of all its Registrar certificates (incorporation, office of establishment, directors) and the signer's ID or passport, plus its VAT registration certificate 'if any'; a natural person attaches ID or passport and, if any, the business-name and VAT certificates. After approval the Department of Customs and Excise gives one number for both the Customs Registry and the EORI database. A company therefore files it after incorporation; VAT registration is not a precondition.

m-dae8b929.t: For the barest company the Cyprus Registrar of Companies offers a ready memorandum: its page 'Types of Memorandum of Association' (read 6 October 2026) provides 'a model memorandum of association' that 'can be adopted' by a private company with shares that 'will conduct business as a general commercial company' (a Greek Word file dated 20 September 2018). The model lets the company carry on 'any work, business or profession'; it bars financial services unless the law allows them and any required CySEC or other licence is held, and bars taking on obligations to the public by deposits, securities or other borrowing; it states that 'the liability of the members is limited'.

m-c535c945.t: A founder may be his own Cyprus company's secretary without a licence only within two limits. Cap. 113 s. 171(1) requires a secretary and bars a sole director from being also secretary, except in a private company with a single member. Law 196(I)/2012 s. 4(3)(β) (cylaw text amended to Law 69(I)/2025, read 6 October 2026) frees a natural person resident in Cyprus from the administrative-services licence to act as secretary where the company is at least 50% owned by him, his spouse or relatives to the fourth degree - 25% where the shareholders are Cyprus-resident individuals - or is his sole employer, if the service is not advertised or offered to others.

m-c522b421.t: Of the Cyprus Registrar's review-criteria pages (2019, read 6 October 2026), only the one for company registration names a lawyer's stamp: form HE1 must carry 'lawyer stamp duty, as determined by the Bar Association', the name of the lawyer or law firm 'sworn in court' and a signature, and a missing stamp is listed first among the 'most common reasons for rejection'. The criteria for HE2, HE4 and the private company's annual return HE32 ask for an officer's signature (HE2 and HE4 also a secretary's declaration), those for the business-name form EE1 the owner's signature; none names a stamp. Forms HE2, HE4, HE32 and EE1 have no stamp field; the EE1 page states €80, plus €40 to accelerate.

m-a74ae8de.t: The Cyprus Registrar's FAQ on its redesigned statutory forms, attached to its announcement of 27 January 2021, says that as each new form takes effect the advocate's sworn declaration is replaced by an advocate's statutory declaration built into the form, company registration (HE1) included; that each new form carries a solemn declaration by the person the law makes responsible for signing, a law office without that capacity appearing only in the contact details; and that the third bundle of forms will come with the new information system, three years after its development contract is signed. HE1 was in neither bundle brought into force in 2021.

m-9cd5e99d.t: No Cyprus Registrar announcement from September 2003 to 30 September 2026 (read 6 October 2026) deals with advocates' stamps on self-filed forms or says a director may make the HE1 declaration. The one text on that declaration, the FAQ attached to the announcement of 27 January 2021, says the advocate's sworn declaration will give way to an advocate's statutory declaration inside each redesigned form, HE1 included. Secretary certification of HE2, HE4 and HE57 was required from 1 March 2013, dropped for electronic filing on 6 February 2014 and required again for it from 2 October 2019. The incorporation page still asks for HE1 'signed and sworn before the court by the entrusted lawyer'.

m-963d02df.t: The Cyprus Registrar of Companies announced on 23 September 2026 that 'due to scheduled maintenance works relating to CY Login' its e-filing system, e-search system and beneficial owners system would be unavailable from 17:00 on Friday 25 September to 18:00 on Saturday 26 September 2026. The announcement does not say how each system uses CY Login.

m-8f996e5c.t: A company struck off the Cyprus register under s. 327 of the Companies Law, Cap. 113 - as in the unpaid-levy round starting in December 2026 - is dissolved on publication of the strike-off notice, but any liability of its directors, officers and members continues (s. 327(5) proviso). The company, a member, a creditor or a person harmed by its acts before the strike-off may apply to the court to restore it within twenty years of publication of the strike-off; the court may restore it if it was carrying on business or if restoration is just, and may order payment of the fees owed to the Registrar and of his costs (s. 327(7)). Cylaw consolidated text read 6 October 2026.

m-859556df.t: The World Bank's expert answers for Cyprus in B-READY 2025 (workbook of 23 December 2025; reference point 1 September 2024) say the law does not let entrepreneurs register a limited liability company by themselves on a simple standard form without mandatory third-party intermediaries (question 19: 'No') but lets them update company statutory information themselves (question 21: 'Yes'). They report no paid-in minimum capital, no foreign-ownership caps, no screening of foreign entrepreneurs different from domestic ones and no nationality rules for management or board. The screening answer predates Law 194(I)/2025, in force since 2 April 2026, which requires approval of some non-EU investments.

m-62975a16.t: Registrar guidance (read 6 October 2026) names no lawyer for routine changes: a change of directors or secretary (form HE4) and notice of a share transfer in a private company (HE57) are filed within 14 days, online or by hand or post, €20 each plus €20 if accelerated; late notice may cost up to €250. Changing the objects differs: the memorandum is amended by special resolution approved by the Court on an application, and filed within 15 days of the time set in the court order unless it directs otherwise (€100). The Advocates Law makes appearing in court for another and drafting or amending a memorandum, or a resolution on a company's organisation, practice open only to licensed advocates.

m-544e5344.t: Neither the Companies Law (Cap. 113) nor the Registrar's forms and review criteria read on 6 October 2026 set a qualification for the witness of a new company's signatures. Cap. 113 requires the memorandum and the articles to be signed by each subscriber 'in the presence of at least one witness' who attests the signature (ss. 5, 11(β)). The Registrar's Annex 'A' for online incorporation (file of 22 January 2014, no fee) has the witness declare that the shareholders, the witness of their signatures, the drafting advocate and the officer on HE2, HE3 and HE5 signed before him, and asks only his name, signature and date; the review criteria ask his name, address and signature.

m-49fd9f7c.t: No Cyprus text read on 6 October 2026 says in terms whose CY Login a company must use to register in the Tax Register; since 1 July 2026 HE, AE and registered-partnership requests are accepted only through a CY Login connection. The texts point to the company's own legal-entity profile (an inference): CY Login has a separate profile type for companies, identified only in person; the Tax Department's 'TFA - CY Login' guide (updated 29 September 2026) has a taxpayer without a TIN start registration 'through his CY Login account' and a legal person log in 'with the personal CY Login credentials of the Legal Person'. The registration page asks the ID of the officer who submits.

m-3dc0bd2b.t: CY Login's help (read 6 October 2026) lets an organisation profile add users and assistants and assign them e-services; by default its policy is that users and assistants may reach all applications. Only if the organisation switches to 'do not allow' must it name, per application, the users or assistants who may enter; if it names none, only the organisation's 'main profile', the one that created it, has access. The help publishes no list of the government e-services an organisation profile reaches; it says only that state systems will be linked to the profile 'gradually'.

m-2faaec18.t: Cyprus's Companies (Amending) Regulations 2018 (K.D.P. 368/2018, Gazette of 18 December 2018) prescribe a new form HE1 whose compliance declaration is made only by 'a practising advocate' entrusted with the formation, who gives his Bar register number; a separate declaration is signed by a proposed director and/or secretary 'authorised to submit this form' for the subscribers. New forms apply only once the Registrar brings them into force by Gazette notice (reg. 4(2)); the notices made, K.D.P. 34/2021, 484/2021 and 495/2021, do not cover HE1, and cylaw's indexes to 18 September 2026 show no later one, so the old HE1 still applies.

m-2e74e649.t: The Cyprus Registrar of Companies' guidance on online incorporation (read 6 October 2026) lets any registered e-filing user submit it ('If you are a registered user, you may proceed'), naming no lawyer-only condition for the submitter. The online file must carry form HE1 'signed and sworn before the court by the entrusted lawyer', the memorandum and articles signed in Greek, and a witness's solemn declaration that the shareholders signed the memorandum and articles, and the officer signed forms HE2, HE3 or HE5, before the witness, and that the drafting advocate's signature was set before him. Fee €165 (€235 without share capital), +€100 accelerated, by credit card.

m-0f293598.t: CY Login, through which companies registered with the Cyprus Registrar must now request tax registration, has a separate company profile: its help pages (read 6 October 2026) offer at sign-up a profile 'For Citizens' or 'For Companies and Organisations'; an organisation profile can add users and assistants and limit which government e-services each reaches. A Registrar-registered company's profile is identified only at an identification centre, on form CYL/1 by an officer, who may name another person to hand it in, or on CYL/3 by a provider with the officer's CYL/2.

m-0f20feda.t: Who may make a new Cyprus company's declaration of compliance differs between law and the Registrar's forms. Cap. 113 s. 17(2) (cylaw, read 6 October 2026) allows the practising advocate who undertook the formation 'or a person named in the articles as director or secretary', and s. 37A(4) lets it be filed electronically, a false one carrying a false oath's liability. The Registrar's form HE1 (PDF of 28 January 2003, served 6 October 2026) is worded only for 'the Advocate entrusted with the formation', sworn before a District Court registrar, and his incorporation page asks on both routes for HE1 'signed and sworn before the court by the entrusted lawyer'.

m-0f00ff06.t: Of the 58 pages in the Cyprus Registrar's 'Tips & Notes' (read 6 October 2026), only the business-name (EE1) criteria mention immigration. The criteria for registering a company (HE1-HE3 and memorandum, page of 28 February 2019) ask, for an individual director or secretary, an identity or passport number, country of origin, date of birth and profession, and, for individual shareholders, address, identity number, nationality and profession; those for changing directors and secretary (HE4, 25 February 2019), registering a partnership (Σ1, 25 April 2019) and name approval (6 March 2019) ask for no immigration permission either.

m-fe087bbc.t: CY Login, Cyprus's government single sign-on, identifies a natural person's profile in three ways (help page read 5 October 2026): through the e-banking of commercial banks, the bank passing identity number, telephone and e-mail to CY Login; by video call with Citizen Service Centre officers, only 'for persons with a Cypriot identity card'; or in person at an Identification Centre by appointment, with form CYL5-NP and one original document - a Cypriot identity card, a residence permit showing the alien registration number (ARC) and photograph, or an EU citizen's registration certificate showing the registration number and photograph. A passport alone is not on the list.

m-ef3498e6.t: As of 5 Oct 2026 the Cyprus Registrar of Companies' e-filing system is entered through an account on the government gateway: its page 'Obtain access to e-filing' says a user must first register on the gateway 'gov.cy' (the links lead to CY Login) and can then submit, among others, the name-approval application, the registration of a company and requests for certified copies. Filing for an already registered entity needs its 'authorisation code', obtained free by e-mailing an application form to the Department; the entity may give the code to a registered user or register as a user itself. The page names no nationality or residence condition and does not say the profile must be verified.

m-e602e0b7.t: EU citizens have a second way into Cyprus's government sign-on besides an identified profile. The Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy announced on 17 March 2025 that 'Sign in with eIDAS' is offered to European citizens within CY Login, Cyprus having set up its national eIDAS node; on 5 October 2026 the CY Login site serves a 'Sign in with eIDAS' page asking the type of person (natural or legal) and the citizen's country. Neither text says which services - Tax For All, the beneficial-owner system, Ergani - accept such a login, and the option does not reach third-country nationals.

m-c98387d4.t: A company's own CY Login profile can be verified only in person at an identification centre (Citizen Service Centres, post-office citizen centres, district offices of the Ministry of Commerce, the Registrar), per the CY Login help page read 5 Oct 2026: an officer files form CYL/1, or a service provider files CYL/3 with the officer's authorisation CYL/2. Form CYL/1 (v3, March 2022) lets the officer state an identity-card number, an Alien Registration Number (ARC) or a passport number, but the page asks for the 'civil identity card' of whoever presents the papers and names no other document for a non-Cypriot. No processing time is published: applicants are told to ask the centre.

m-9e544a78.t: A company's own CY Login profile can be identified only by an on-site visit to an identification centre (Citizen Service Centres, post-office citizen centres, district offices of the Ministry of Commerce, the Registrar of Companies), per the CY Login help page read 5 October 2026. An officer signs form CYL/1 (v3), giving an 'identity number / alien registration number (ARC) / passport number', his capacity and the 16-digit profile number; he hands it in himself or authorises on the form a person, named with an identity number, to do so. A service provider uses CYL/3 with an authorisation CYL/2 signed by an officer. The page asks for the 'civil identity' of whoever presents the documents.

m-5f7d17c3.t: The Cyprus Registrar of Companies' public 'Results of Name Examination' service, read on Monday 5 Oct 2026, states that it holds name applications submitted between 01/03/2016 and 02/10/2026, that it returns only names submitted through the Department's cash register, and - twice - that 'The decision for the name is valid for 6 months'. A search requires the order date, the order number and the applicant number. The service shows neither a date of decision nor the date up to which applications have been examined, so it gives no measure of the time taken; the Registrar's guidance page says only that name approval results 'are available via e-services'.

m-57d74a19.t: Where requirements for a new Cyprus company point at each other (5 Oct 2026): the employer form lists a VAT certificate and a first VAT return, while VAT registration asks for proof of activity and employers must register before the first hire; Bank of Cyprus asks for the owner-register receipt and a utility bill for the place of activity before any account exists; JCC asks, 'as applicable', for an IBAN certificate plus tax and VAT numbers; the Registrar calls its certificates optional, yet the tax register, social insurance and the tourism licence ask for them; a non-Cypriot director can verify a personal CY Login profile but, on the Registrar's guidance, not use it for the owner register.

m-4c904a06.t: Cyprus's national electronic identity (eID) is closed to non-citizens as of 5 October 2026, and by statute: art. 65A(4) of the Civil Registry Law 141(I)/2002 makes issue subject to a check that the person 'has Cypriot citizenship', is 18, holds a biometric identity card in force and has no other eID in force; it is valid three years (art. 65A(7)). The official eID site (modified 7 September 2026) repeats this, names JCC Payment Systems as the only approved provider 'at this stage' and requires identification in person at a Citizen Service Centre. A non-Cypriot resident needs a CY Login profile identified otherwise; for EU citizens CY Login also offers 'Sign in with eIDAS'.

m-2643f5a2.t: The Cyprus Registrar of Companies identifies founders on the incorporation papers by document number, not by immigration status: its published review criteria (read 5 Oct 2026) require, for an individual director or secretary on form HE3, 'identity or passport number, country of origin, date of birth and profession', and for each shareholder in the memorandum the full address, identity number, nationality and profession. No residence permit, registration certificate or Cyprus address of the person is asked for; only the registered office must be in Cyprus, written in Greek. The same wording serves a citizen of another EU state and a third-country national.

m-04591b6d.t: Reading the Cyprus texts together for a founder paid a salary by his own private company (inference, 5 October 2026): the Social Insurance Law counts a shareholder's work in his private company as employment, so the company applies to the Social Insurance Services at least one day before he starts, gets an employer number, opens an Ergani account and notifies his hiring a day ahead; it files employer returns with the Tax Department through Tax For All (subject to that page's carve-out); he gives it form T.D.59 each year. His personal TIN needs only his registration certificate or residence permit; without one, the Tax Department asks proof of the employment and his social insurance number.

m-f7a9132b.t: For company formation Cyprus law sets the Registrar a time limit only on the online route: s. 366Ε(5) of the Companies Law (Cap. 113), inserted by Law 151(I)/2023 (Gazette No. 4974, 19.12.2023, transposing Directive (EU) 2019/1151; no commencement clause), says electronic formation is completed within 5 working days where the company is formed exclusively by natural persons using the Registrar's templates (s. 366ΣΤ), and within 10 working days otherwise, counted from the later of completing all formalities and paying the registration fee; if not, the Registrar tells the applicant why. The same Law gives 10 working days for online registration of an overseas company's branch (s. 366Η(6)).

m-ee49c83c.t: Advocates' Pension Fund stamp on the memorandum filed to register a Cyprus limited liability company (Table Part III item 9 of the Advocates' Pension Fund (Fees) Regulations, set by K.D.P. 605/2007 from 1 January 2008 and not amended by 4 Oct 2026), by share capital: up to €2,000 - €40; €2,000-30,000 - €50; €30,000-60,000 - €60; €60,000-100,000 - €70; €100,000-200,000 - €80; €200,000-300,000 - €90; €300,000-600,000 - €100; €600,000-1,000,000 - €120; €1,000,000-2,000,000 - €140; above €2,000,000 - €140 plus €10 per €2,000,000; company without share capital (by guarantee) - €18. The stamp scales with capital; for the usual €1,000 company it is €40.

m-e9e5b111.t: Section 102 of the Companies Law (Cap. 113) requires every company, from the day its certificate of incorporation is issued, to maintain a registered office in the Republic of Cyprus to which notices may be addressed; notice of its location is filed together with the memorandum (form HE2) and any change must be notified within 14 days. The Registrar's guidance adds that the registered office 'must not be a mailbox' and is where the company's registers are kept, and that the address is published in the electronic register.

m-e8ebde35.t: Under the Companies Law (Cap. 113) a private company must have at least one director (s. 170) and every company must have a secretary; a sole director may not also be the secretary, except in a single-member private limited company (s. 171(1)). Sections 170-172 as consolidated on cylaw on 4 Oct 2026 contain no residence, nationality or licensing requirement for a director or secretary of a private company; the Registrar's guidance adds only that directors and the secretary must be at least 18 years old.

m-e8be691e.t: As of 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar of Companies charges €20 per certified copy or certificate, €40 for a certified copy of the memorandum and articles when a copy is supplied with the application (€50 when it is not), and €20 more per document for the accelerated procedure. In the Schedule to the fee regulations K.D.P. 31/2013 these are items 5(β), 5(γ) and 8(α) as enacted (4(β), 4(γ), 7(α) since K.D.P. 364/2018). The set of five documents offered on incorporation for €120 or €130, plus €100 accelerated, is the sum of these items: 4 x €20 + €40 = €120; 4 x €20 + €50 = €130; 5 x €20 = €100.

m-ddffc683.t: The Cyprus Tax Department states that from 1 July 2026 a legal person registered with the Registrar of Companies (registration prefix HE, AE or Σ) can submit its request for registration in the Tax Register only when logged into the Tax For All (TFA) portal through CY Login; requests filed otherwise are rejected. A company incorporated at the Registrar attaches its certificate of incorporation and the certificates of registered office address, of directors and secretary and of shareholders, plus an identification document of the officer who submits the request.

m-d6996527.t: On 30 September 2026 the Registrar of Companies announced that in December 2026 it will begin striking off, under section 327(2A)(b) of the Companies Law, companies that have not paid the annual levy due for any of the years 2012-2023: they will be published in the Official Gazette for three months and then removed from the register unless cause to the contrary is shown. The abolition of the levy from 2024 therefore does not extinguish arrears for earlier years.

m-d68c343e.t: Go-live of the Cyprus Registrar of Companies' new electronic system slipped from the first half of 2025 to the first quarter of 2027 over five official statements. Registrar, 12 October 2022: contract signed 11 October 2022 with NET-U Consultants Limited, budget €14 million (€6.6 million from the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility), 'expected to be completed in the 1st half of 2025'. Minister's review, 17 January 2023: full digital service 2025. One-year review, 22 April 2024: end 2025 or early 2026. Action Plan 2025 (November 2024): November 2022 - December 2026. Registrar, 19 June 2026: 'expected within the first quarter of 2027'. K.D.P. 282/2025's certificates will be issued through it.

m-d1b8ade3.t: A legal person may be director or secretary of a Cyprus company. The Companies Law (Cap. 113) assumes it: s. 192(2)(β) and (3)(β) prescribe what the register of directors and secretaries records for a director or secretary that is a legal person (corporate name and registered office; for a director, registered or principal office), and s. 172 only forbids two combinations - a corporate secretary whose sole director is the company's sole director, and a corporate sole director whose sole director is the company's secretary - neither applying to a single-member private company. The Law sets no qualification for the secretary of a private company.

m-cce79ae9.t: Capital duty on Cyprus company registrations was abolished by regulation, not by the Companies Law: K.D.P. 364/2018 (Official Gazette No. 5128, 18.12.2018, no commencement clause) deleted it from the fee schedule and renumbered schedule items 4-11 as 3-10. The Companies (Amending) (No. 3) Law, Law 149(I)/2018 (Official Gazette No. 4678, 21.12.2018), does not mention capital duty; it deleted from s. 5 the rule that the memorandum be stamped as an agreement and, by art. 41 (in force on the 15th day after publication, s. 51(4)), renumbered the fee-making power from s. 387(1)(δ) to s. 387(1)(γ). Citations of fee items or of s. 387(1)(δ) made before 2019 therefore use the old numbering.

m-cb034478.t: As of 4 Oct 2026 the cylaw consolidated text of the Cyprus Companies Law (Cap. 113) is not a safe guide to what is in force. It already prints amendments of Law 2(I)/2026 that take effect only on 1 January of the year after the small-entity reporting standard is published (e.g. s. 142(1)(α1)), without marking them. It also still prints s. 120(3) - an administrative fine of up to CY£5,000 for not filing the annual return - although Law 149(I)/2018 art. 26(a) ordered its deletion one year after that Law's commencement and the Registrar's 'Late Filing' page says the fine (given as €8,543) is abolished 'as at 18/12/2020'. Status claims read from the consolidation need the amending Gazette text.

m-be7680fa.t: The €49 'Bar Association stamp on HE1 for €1,000 share capital' quoted by two Cyprus formation providers in July 2026 does not match the published scale: the Advocates' Pension Fund (Fees) Regulations give €40 for a company with share capital up to €2,000 (K.D.P. 605/2007, Table Part III item 9(α)), and no single item of Part III is €49. The €9 difference equals the flat stamp for several other Registrar filings, but neither provider explains its figure and no Bar circular setting €49 was found on 4 Oct 2026 (Bar Association guide for new advocates, October 2025; Pension Fund website apf.com.cy; cylaw index).

m-adc0e2ad.t: A natural person may trade in Cyprus without forming a company. Under s. 50(b) of the Partnerships and Business Names Law (Cap. 116) he must register a business name with the Registrar of Companies if he has a place of business in Cyprus and trades under a name that is not his true surname without any addition other than his true first names or initials; s. 52(1) sets the deadline at one month from commencing business. As of 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar charges €80 for registration (form EE1 or e-filing) plus €40 accelerated; its comparison table sets 'unlimited liability of the owner of a business name' against 'limited liability of company members' and €165 to register a company.

m-aaa58158.t: No change to the Cyprus Registrar of Companies' fee schedule in 2019-2026 was found on 4 Oct 2026: the Registrar's legislation page for the Companies (Fees and Rights) Regulations offers the 2013 regulations (K.D.P. 31/2013) and the amending regulations of 2017 (K.D.P. 431/2017) and 2018 (K.D.P. 364/2018) only, and cylaw's yearly indexes of regulatory acts for 2019-2026 (2026 covered to 25.9.2026) list no regulations with that title. The 2022-2026 changes to what a company costs came through primary laws instead: the €150 cap on the annual-return late charge (2022, general from 2024), abolition of the €350 levy (2024) and repeal of stamp duty (2026).

m-a7c91d0e.t: As of 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar of Companies states that a private limited company must have at least one member and not more than fifty and that private companies have no minimum share capital, while a public company needs at least seven members and a minimum capital of €25,629. In the Companies Law (Cap. 113) these are s. 3(1) (seven persons, or one for a private company), s. 29(1)(β) (fifty members, not counting current and former employees) and s. 4A(1), which sets a minimum only for public companies and still reads '15.000 λίρες' (Cyprus pounds) in the cylaw text (= €25,629 at 0.585274). The memorandum must state the nominal capital with which the company registers.

m-a4027e25.t: No provision of the Cyprus Companies Law (Cap. 113) obliges a company to engage a licensed accountant for bookkeeping: s. 141(1) puts the duty to keep accounting books on the directors, and s. 141(4) accepts as a defence that a competent and reliable person was charged with it (cylaw consolidated text, read 4 Oct 2026). Licensed professionals enter elsewhere: the yearly audit or review needs a statutory auditor (s. 152A), and under s. 29 of Law 4/1978, as replaced by Law 243(I)/2025 from 1 January 2026, the tax authority may disregard accounts not prepared and certified by a statutory auditor and tax computations not prepared and certified by a holder of an ICPAC practising certificate.

m-a0b2d408.t: E-filing does not remove the advocates' stamp in Cyprus, by the text of the regulations: K.D.P. 227/2022 (Gazette No. 5710, 17.6.2022) added a proviso to reg. 4 of the Advocates' Pension Fund (Fees) Regulations that where a filing is made electronically the fees payable under the Regulations are paid by electronic means, the internet or any other way the Bar Council sets, and a new reg. 2A that 'stamps are affixed' includes such payment. K.D.P. 220/2017 (reg. 10) had already made e-filed trade-mark documents pay the fee to the Pension Fund through its website after filing. Neither act names company forms; how the stamp is collected on an e-filed incorporation was not established.

m-99f3407c.t: As of 4 Oct 2026 several English guidance pages of the Registrar of Companies still describe the repealed €350 annual levy as a current obligation ('Annual fee', 'After Incorporation', 'Choosing the right type of Business Entity'); the last also gives company taxation as 12.5%, while the Income Tax Law as consolidated on cylaw sets corporate tax at 15%. The Registrar's own notice of 21 March 2024 and Law 25(I)/2024 show the levy was abolished from 2024, so these pages are stale; they are not evidence that the levy survives.

m-991ebf3e.t: As of 4 Oct 2026 the company-registration stamp scale of K.D.P. 605/2007 stands unchanged. The later acts under the Advocates' Pension Fund (Fees) Regulations leave Part III items 8-14 alone: K.D.P. 306/2008 (stamp design and denominations), 220/2017 (court items; Part III trade-mark items 3-7 payment column, ship items 15-23), 409/2017 (ship items 15-23), 227/2022 (electronic payment counts as affixing stamps) and 280/2023 (civil-procedure items, Part III ship-arrest items 24-31, new Part IV). Cylaw's index lists nothing later to 25 Sep 2026. Seven 2020-2021 Gazette dates in the margins of the 2022 and 2023 acts are the dates of seven Advocates (Amending) Laws, not of fee regulations.

m-95070876.t: K.D.P. 282/2025, 'the Companies Order of 2025' (made by the Minister of Energy, Commerce and Industry under s. 387Α of the Companies Law on 4 September 2025, Official Gazette No. 5969, 19.9.2025), replaces the table of contents of the Schedule to the Companies Regulations - listing HE1 as 'Formation of a company' and no HE3 - deletes certificate forms HE50, HE58 and HE69 and adds the new certificates and certificates of entries. Under its para. 3 it enters into force on a date fixed by a notification of the Registrar in the Gazette, which may set different dates for different provisions. As of 4 Oct 2026 no such notification appears in cylaw's index (to 25.9.2026) or on the Registrar's site.

m-94a03752.t: How the Cyprus Registrar's company fees changed in 2013: under the Companies (Fees and Duties) Regulations of 2006 (K.D.P. 422/2006), as converted to euro on the Registrar's list (file created 22 October 2008, archived 17 June 2009 and unchanged in a capture of 24 January 2013), registration of a company with share capital cost €102.52 (CY£60) plus 0.6% subscription tax on nominal capital, without share capital €170.86, a statutory declaration €34.17, any other document €17.09 and an annual return €17.09. K.D.P. 31/2013 (1 February 2013) repealed those regulations, raised the five amounts to €105, €175, €40, €20 and €20 and kept the 0.6% duty, which K.D.P. 364/2018 then removed.

m-88c2dc54.t: As of 4 Oct 2026 the Cyprus Registrar of Companies' e-filing system (access via the gov.cy gateway) offers name reservation, incorporation, register updates, annual return filing, certified copies, charges and strike-off applications. Electronic-only: the annual return of a private company with share capital (form HE32I, since 2014) and beneficial-owner filings. Paper-only: annual returns of public companies and of companies without share capital, and the Income Tax Information Report under Law 138(I)/2024 (cashier, €20). From 1 January 2026 personal cheques are not accepted. A notice of 19 June 2026 says the Department's new electronic system is 'expected within the first quarter of 2027'.

m-8652340b.t: Under s. 120(4) of the Companies Law (Cap. 113) as consolidated on cylaw on 4 Oct 2026, a company that delivers its annual return late is charged €50 plus €1 for each day the breach continues, capped at €150 per breach; the Registrar attributes the cap to Law 18(I)/2024 (Gazette 5 March 2024) and applies it to returns with a reference date in 2021 or later. The Registrar's page 'Annual Return Filing Fee' still shows the earlier scale (€50, then €1 a day for six months and €2 a day after, up to €500), which is the wording inserted by Law 149(I)/2018; the filing fee itself is €20, plus €20 when filed late.

m-85bd85a5.t: Statutory history of the Cyprus annual-return late charge: Law 149(I)/2018 (Official Gazette No. 4678, 21.12.2018), art. 26(b), inserted s. 120(4) of the Companies Law - €50, then €1 a day for six months and €2 a day thereafter, capped at €500. Its start was deferred by Laws 163(I)/2019, 38(I)/2020 and 192(I)/2020 (to 1 April 2021) and fixed at 1 June 2021 by Law 43(I)/2021 (Gazette No. 4826, 7.4.2021). Law 87(I)/2022 (Gazette No. 4897, 24.6.2022) capped the charge at €150 for returns dated in 2021 and 2022, until 31 December 2024, with refund of any excess already paid; Law 18(I)/2024 (5.3.2024) removed the €2 tier and made €150 the cap for all returns.

m-811689b1.t: The 'lawyer's stamp' the Cyprus Registrar of Companies checks on form HE1 is the advocates' stamp (δικηγορόσημο) of the Advocates' Pension Fund (Fees) Regulations 1966-2023, made under s. 27 of the Advocates Law (Cap. 2). Part III of the Table, 'Filings of documents with the Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver and the Ship Registry', as replaced by K.D.P. 605/2007 from 1 January 2008, sets an amount per filing, paid by affixing stamps of equal value to the document filed. The match is by description, not citation: the Table names the memorandum, not HE1; the Registrar's Greek examiner guide (2015) asks for stamps on HE1 'proportional to the capital, as set by the Bar Association'.

m-7eabbed0.t: The €350 annual company levy, introduced as section 391 of the Companies Law by Law 117(I)/2011 (Official Gazette No. 4292, 31.8.2011) and payable by 30 June each year, was abolished by the Companies (Amendment) (No. 2) Law 2024, Law 25(I)/2024 (Official Gazette No. 4986, 15.3.2024). Law 25(I)/2024 deletes section 391, is deemed to have entered into force on 1 January 2024, and keeps the obligations arising from section 391 alive for the years 2011 to 2023. The Registrar announced on 21 March 2024 that levies already paid for 2024 would be refunded.

m-7ccaffbe.t: Law 18(I)/2024 (Official Gazette No. 4984, 5.3.2024) amended s. 120(4) of the Cyprus Companies Law (Cap. 113): a company that delivers its annual return late is charged €50 plus €1 for each day the breach continues, capped at €150 per breach. Before it, s. 120(4) (inserted by Law 149(I)/2018, in force 1 June 2021 under Law 43(I)/2021) charged €50, €1 a day for the first six months and €2 a day thereafter, capped at €500; Law 87(I)/2022 had already capped returns dated 2021-2022 at €150 until 31.12.2024. The 2024 Law covers the annual return only. As of 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar's 'Annual Return Filing Fee' page still shows the €500 scheme.

m-785185e0.t: Under section 11(5) of the Advocates Law (Cap. 2) drafting the memorandum or articles of association of a company of any form is the exclusive work of a practising advocate, who must certify on the documents that he drafted them; a memorandum or articles drafted in breach is void, and drafting them without being a practising advocate is an offence. The Registrar of Companies restates the rule: only lawyers practising in the Republic of Cyprus can draft the memorandum and articles. In force as of 4 Oct 2026 per the cylaw consolidated text.

m-7748cd78.t: As of 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar of Companies charges €10 for each proposed company name submitted for approval, plus €20 per name for the accelerated procedure; an approved name stays reserved for six months, within which the incorporation application must be filed. In the Companies (Fees and Rights) Regulations 2013 (K.D.P. 31/2013) the €10 is item 5(ε) and the €20 surcharge item 8(α) of Part I of the Schedule as enacted, renumbered 4(ε) and 7(α) by K.D.P. 364/2018 (18.12.2018). No later amendment of these regulations appears in the cylaw index of regulatory acts for 2019 to 25 Sep 2026.

m-76e3611a.t: Before its repeal on 1 January 2026 the Cyprus Stamp Duty Law (19/1963) charged nothing specific on forming a company: its First Schedule, as last consolidated on cylaw (35 items, amendments to Law 221(I)/2025), names no memorandum, articles, share capital or incorporation; only partnership deeds are named (item 20). Generic items remained: a written affidavit or formal declaration €4 (item 2), an agreement without a stated sum €35 (item 3B), an attested document not otherwise covered €2 (item 32). The memorandum had to be stamped 'as an agreement' until Law 149(I)/2018 deleted that from s. 5 of the Companies Law. What the Registrar actually collected in 2019-2025 was not established.

m-762c6b44.t: The seven 2020-2021 Gazette dates listed in the margins of the Cyprus Advocates' Pension Fund (Fees) (Amending) Regulations of 2022 and 2023 (K.D.P. 227/2022, 280/2023) are not amendments of those regulations: they are the publication dates of the seven Advocates (Amending) Laws of 2020-2021 - Laws 6(I)/2020 (31.1.2020), 41(I)/2020 (30.4.2020), 83(I)/2020 (17.7.2020), 139(I)/2020 (9.10.2020), 200(I)/2020 (22.12.2020), 8(I)/2021 (12.2.2021) and 145(I)/2021 (5.11.2021) - none of which deals with stamps or the fee Table. The same margin omits the two amending regulations of 2017, so it is not a reliable list of amendments.

m-71dfe528.t: Section 17(2) of the Companies Law (Cap. 113) requires a statutory declaration of compliance with the registration requirements, made by a practising advocate engaged in the formation of the company or by a person named in the articles as director or secretary. In practice only the advocate route exists: form HE1 as published by the Registrar on 4 Oct 2026 contains only an advocate's oath sworn before a District Court registrar, and the Registrar's review criteria require the lawyer's name, the court seal and a stamp 'as determined by the Bar Association', whose absence is the first listed reason for rejection. The new HE1 prescribed by K.D.P. 368/2018 also carries an advocate's declaration.

m-6859bbb6.t: As of 4 Oct 2026 the Cyprus Advocates Law (Cap. 2, cylaw text through Law 17(I)/2024) contains no minimum-fee provision: s. 24(1)(ια) lets the Bar Council regulate only how disputes over fees in out-of-court matters are resolved, 'subject to the principles of free and healthy competition'. Law 38(I)/2022 (Gazette No. 4882, 30.3.2022) deleted s. 17(9); the House Legal Affairs Committee report of 15 March 2022 on that bill says the deleted rule made it a disciplinary offence to charge less than the minimum set by regulations, and cites the bill's memorandum that it was without object after the 2018 fee-dispute regulations. Those regulations were not read; the negative covers the statute only.

m-680588ca.t: On 4 September 2026 the Cyprus Registrar of Companies announced that, following reminder letters sent to companies on 9 February 2026 about overdue annual returns and the corresponding financial statements, their filing is extended until 31 December 2026; after that date the strike-off procedure under s. 327 of the Companies Law will continue for companies that have not complied. This is a separate track from the strike-off for unpaid annual levy announced on 30 September 2026. Statement about what happens after 31.12.2026: re-check then.

m-64597746.t: The only official duration found for the Cyprus Registrar's company registration is a ministerial claim, not a service standard: the Minister of Energy, Commerce and Industry's review of 2020-2023 (presentation dated 17 January 2023) lists, under modernisation of the Department of Registrar of Companies, 'registration of a company within 48 hours for applications via the internet'. The slide gives no method, period or sample and does not say whether this is the standard or the accelerated procedure, or whether name approval is included.

m-62934eb5.t: The Companies (Fees and Rights) (Amending) Regulations 2018 (K.D.P. 364/2018, Official Gazette No. 5128, 18.12.2018) deleted the words 'plus capital duty of 0.6% on the nominal capital' from the company-registration fee and deleted the item that charged capital duty on increases of share capital. Since that amendment the Registrar's fee for registering a company with share capital no longer depends on the amount of its authorised capital.

m-57c0bfc0.t: The Companies (Fees and Rights) Regulations 2013 (K.D.P. 31/2013, Official Gazette No. 4623, 1.2.2013), made by the Council of Ministers under s. 387(1)(δ) of the Companies Law (para. (γ) since Law 149(I)/2018), set the Registrar's fees: €105 to register a company with share capital (as enacted 'plus capital duty of 0.6% on the nominal capital', deleted by K.D.P. 364/2018), €175 without share capital, €20 for an annual return (€40 late), €10 for a name application, €160 for filing a translation of the memorandum or articles, €100 extra for expedited registration. No amendment after K.D.P. 364/2018 appears in the cylaw index of regulatory acts to 25 Sep 2026.

m-57389070.t: As of 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar of Companies issues, optionally on incorporation, a set of certificates (shareholders; directors and secretary; registered office address; certified copies of the memorandum and articles and of the certificate of incorporation) for €120 when a certified copy of the memorandum and articles is supplied, or €130 when it is not, plus €100 for the accelerated process. Certificates issued electronically carry an authenticity code that can be verified online for 90 days from issue.

m-3c91f1f1.t: As of 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar of Companies charges €165 in total to register a company with share capital (€235 without share capital), covering forms HE1, HE2 and HE3; the accelerated procedure adds €100, a file of translations of the memorandum and articles €160, and form HE5 for a public company €20. The total exceeds the registration items of the fee regulations K.D.P. 31/2013 (€105 with share capital, €175 without) by €60 in both cases; the Registrar does not itemise that €60, which equals three forms at the €20 it charges for other statutory forms (an inference, not a published split). Online filings are paid by credit card.

m-3ac4a418.t: The Companies (Amending) Regulations 2018 (K.D.P. 368/2018, Official Gazette No. 5128, 18.12.2018) prescribe a new set of company forms in which HE1 is a single 'Incorporation of a company' form (registered office, secretary, directors, capital, members, advocate's declaration) and no form HE3 exists; under reg. 4(2) the new forms take effect only by notification of the Registrar in the Gazette. The notifications found in the cylaw index to 25 Sep 2026 (K.D.P. 34/2021, 484/2021, 495/2021) cover other forms, not HE1, and on 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar's site still supplies the old HE1, HE2 and HE3. K.D.P. 282/2025 (19.9.2025), which updates the list of forms, also awaits a commencement notice.

m-308e3733.t: Who may not be a director of a Cyprus company (Companies Law, Cap. 113, read 4 Oct 2026): an undischarged bankrupt, without leave of the bankruptcy court (s. 179, an offence); a person whom a court - after conviction for an offence tied to promoting, forming or managing a company, or a finding in a winding-up of fraud or breach of duty as an officer - has barred, save with its leave, from being a director or taking part in management for up to five years (s. 180). Since Law 151(I)/2023 (19.12.2023) the Registrar may also reject the appointment of a person disqualified in another EU Member State, and the Registrar or anyone with a legitimate interest may ask the court to end it (s. 180Α).

m-2f54ec75.t: The advocates' stamp is by statute a cost of the lawyer, not of the client: under s. 28 of the Cyprus Advocates Law (Cap. 2) all fees imposed under s. 27(1) are paid into the Advocates' Pension Fund, and s. 29(1) forbids an advocate to charge to or collect from any client any amount he paid as a contribution to the Fund or as fees under s. 27(1); breach is conduct incompatible with the profession and exposes him to disciplinary prosecution (s. 29(2)). Read on 4 Oct 2026 in the cylaw consolidated text, which runs to Law 17(I)/2024. Formation providers nevertheless list a 'Bar Association stamp' as a separate cost to the client (vendor pages of July 2026).

m-2df9cabb.t: A consolidated fee table of the Cyprus Registrar of Companies exists for the regulations as they stand after their last amendment: a three-page Greek table titled 'The Companies (Fees and Rights) Regulations of 2013 to 2018' (PDF created 20 December 2018, two days after K.D.P. 364/2018), published on the Department's former website and archived on 11 July 2019. It shows item 1 at €105 with no capital duty, item 2 at €175, filing items 3(α)-(ο) including statutory declaration €40 and any other document €20, name application €10 (4(ε)), acceleration €20 per service (7(α)) and €100 for company registration (7(β)). No such table was found on the current site on 4 Oct 2026.

m-289b1e04.t: The Cyprus Registrar's €165 total for registering a company exceeds the €105 registration item of its fee schedule by €60, and as of 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar publishes only the total. The schedule (K.D.P. 31/2013, Part I, item 3 after the renumbering by K.D.P. 364/2018) has two filing items that can build it: 3(θ) 'statutory declaration' €40 and 3(ι) 'any document required by the Law ... for which no other provision is made' €20. Two splits give €165: 105 + 40 (HE1 as statutory declaration) + 20, or 105 + 3 x 20 (HE1, HE2, HE3). The Registrar charges €20 more for form HE5 of a public company and €20 for HE2 or HE4 filed alone, which fits the per-form reading without proving it.

m-222b678c.t: As of 4 Oct 2026 the Cyprus Registrar of Companies publishes no service charter and no statistics on examination times. Places read: its guidance pages on name approval and incorporation (fees only); its Statistics section (262 entries, monthly counts only, no durations); its Publications section (12 entries); the gov.cy service page 'Approval of company name' (no processing-time field); the government business portal; the Ministry's action plans for 2023-24 and 2025. Providers' figures disagree and cite no source: name approval 'three to five working days' (Expanship) or 'about two weeks' (Savva) standard, one to four working days accelerated.

m-2183ed9f.t: Workload behind the Cyprus Registrar's examination times, from the 'Companies Section Statistics' block of its home page (read 4 Oct 2026): 14,444 new company registrations in 2024, 406,648 e-filing submissions, 320,335 certified copies issued, 128,562 annual returns filed and 152,669 updates of company particulars; total registered companies 203,545 (2021), 192,469 (2022), 198,863 (2023) and 196,090 (2024). The page does not say how the totals are counted or on which day of the year.

m-2097501c.t: Besides the annual return, the Cyprus Companies Law (Cap. 113, cylaw consolidated text read 4 Oct 2026) attaches a late-filing charge of €50 plus €1 for each day the breach continues, capped at €250 per breach, to five other filings: the return of allotments (s. 51), the notice of the registered office or its change (s. 102), the notification of a transfer of shares in a private company (s. 113A), the return of changes in directors or secretary (s. 192(10)) and changes notified by an overseas company (s. 349). The charges were introduced by Law 149(I)/2018 (arts. 11, 20, 23, 28, 36); Law 18(I)/2024, which cut the annual-return cap to €150, did not change them.

m-203f419a.t: As of 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar of Companies (DRCIP) lists for incorporating a company by hand/post: form HE1 (statutory declaration signed and sworn before the court by the entrusted lawyer), HE2 (registered office), HE3 (first directors and secretary) and the memorandum and articles signed in Greek; a public company adds HE5. Where applicable it also asks for the consent or pre-approval of the competent authority for restricted words or a regulated nature of business, and a certified translation if a translation file is wanted. The e-filing list names HE1, the memorandum and articles and a solemn declaration of the witness of signatures. Filing follows approval of the name.

m-1d7ee013.t: Section 5A(2) of the Assessment and Collection of Taxes Law (Law 4/1978), in the wording inserted by Law 243(I)/2025 with effect from 1 January 2026, obliges a company to give notice for registration in the Tax Register and to obtain a tax identification number within 60 days of its incorporation or registration in Cyprus. Changes to registered details must be notified to the Tax Commissioner within 60 days as well (s. 5A(3)).

m-1ccf847e.t: The Stamp Duty (Repealing) Law 2025, Law 239(I)/2025 (Official Gazette No. 5070, 31.12.2025), repealed the Stamp Duty Laws with effect from 1 January 2026; the Registrar of Companies announced on 19 January 2026 that documents submitted to the Department need no stamp duty as of 01/01/2026. This concerns State stamp duty only: on 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar's review criteria for form HE1 still require the lawyer's stamp 'as determined by the Bar Association', a separate Bar charge that the repeal does not mention. The rule that a company's memorandum be stamped as an agreement had already been deleted from s. 5 of the Companies Law by Law 149(I)/2018.

m-1bb1d32c.t: Which of the new Cyprus company forms of K.D.P. 368/2018 are in effect, by the Registrar's Gazette notifications under its reg. 4(2): K.D.P. 34/2021 (22.1.2021) brought in forms HE11, HE17, HE18, HE19, HE25, HE66 and KE1 from 12 February 2021; K.D.P. 484/2021 (26.11.2021) forms HE8, HE9, HE15, HE20, HE60, HE61, HE63, HE67, AE4-AE9 (AE7 in three variants), AE11, AE14 and KE2 from 6 December 2021; K.D.P. 495/2021 (3.12.2021) form HE64 from 6 December 2021. None names the new single incorporation form HE1, nor HE2, HE4 or HE32, and cylaw's index lists no further notification under reg. 4(2) up to 25 September 2026.

m-1a8ff721.t: Every Cyprus company with share capital must make an annual return once per calendar year (Companies Law s. 118) up to its reference date and deliver it to the Registrar within 28 days of the date it is made up (s. 120(1)); the first reference date is the day after 18 months from incorporation. Since 2014 a private company's return (form HE32I) can be filed only through the e-filing system, accompanied by the financial statements for the previous financial year. As of 4 Oct 2026 the Registrar's filing fee is €20, plus €20 for the accelerated procedure.

m-1618106f.t: Prices for keeping a Cyprus company, as published by three providers in July 2026 (read 4 Oct 2026) - vendors' own figures, not official fees: registered office €300-€600 a year and company secretary €700-€1,000 (Savva Cyprus); registered office plus secretary €500-€1,200 (Zeno). Nominee individual director: €2,000-€3,500 (Savva), €1,500-€3,000 (Zeno), 'up to €1,000' (Expanship); nominee corporate director: €1,000-€1,800 (Savva), 'roughly €400' (Expanship). Like for like, the highest figure is 3.5 times the lowest for an individual nominee and 4.5 times for a corporate one. No publisher describes a method or sample, and none mentions that these are regulated administrative services.

m-1420ff09.t: Prices for forming a Cyprus private company, as published by four providers and read 4 Oct 2026 - vendors' figures on different bases, not official fees and not a market survey: Zeno (3 July 2026) 'market range €950-€2,500' for professional fees, its own fixed fee €950, government fees extra; Savva Cyprus (14 July 2026) €1,500-€4,000 professional fee, government fees extra; Expanship (1 July 2026) €1,500-€4,000 including government filing fees; Christophi & Associates LLC (undated) €1,300 plus VAT including registrar fees and a registered office for 12 months. Savva and Expanship add a €49 Bar Association stamp on form HE1 for €1,000 share capital. No publisher explains its range.

m-0126dcb1.t: Part III of the Table of the Cyprus Advocates' Pension Fund (Fees) Regulations (K.D.P. 605/2007, in force 1 January 2008, these items not amended by 4 Oct 2026) lists flat advocates' stamps for other Registrar filings: application to register a business name €9; memorandum of a general or limited partnership €26 regardless of capital; memorandum of a public company €171; overseas ('off-shore') branch €86; annual return (HE32) €9; notification of change of registered office (HE2) €9; notification of change of directors and secretary (HE4) €9. The first HE2 and form HE3 filed on incorporation are not listed as separate items.

m-e824626c.t: Cyprus VAT attaches to the person, whatever the rung. Under VAT Law 95(I)/2000 a taxable person is 'every person who is registered or required to be registered' (s. 6(1)); 'legal person' includes a partnership, whether or not constituted under any law (s. 2). Persons carrying on business in partnership may be registered in the firm's name, and until the Commissioner is told of a change, a partner who has left is treated as still a partner, in particular for liability for VAT on the firm's supplies (s. 34(1)-(2)). Read in the consolidated text on 6 October 2026.

m-da02a927.t: As of 6 October 2026 the Cyprus Tax Department's VAT registration page (updated 3 August 2026) still has form T.F. 1101 filed 'in printed form' at the district offices, with, for a natural person, a copy of 'the identity card (both sides)' and evidence of economic activity or of the duty or right to register, such as invoices issued, agreements or correspondence; it links 'District Offices' to the contact page. The Department's directory says all requests and questions on indirect taxation must be submitted 'exclusively' through a Tax For All message, and it gives the district VAT offices no e-mail address, unlike the district direct-tax offices.

m-cf0ac646.t: Two actions for partial annulment of the ViDA Directive (EU) 2025/516 were brought before the General Court in June 2025: T-394/25 Nomad Stays v Council (17 June 2025) and T-393/25 Pro.Loca.Tur. v Council (18 June 2025). Both ask for annulment of Article 3(1), which inserts the deemed-supplier rule for platforms facilitating short-term accommodation rental (new art. 28a(1) of the VAT Directive), of Article 3(3)(a), which treats short-term rentals as having a similar function to the hotel sector, and of a provision of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/518. Article 3 applies from 1 July 2028; Article 2 (1 January 2027) is not challenged. No judgment was listed on EUR-Lex on 6 October 2026.

m-b7543b86.t: A Cyprus online shop that uses the EU One Stop Shop registers on the Cyprus Tax Department's OSS portal: per the Cyprus page of the European Commission's OSS portal (read 6 October 2026), registration is made electronically at tax-oss.mof.gov.cy, where a new taxable person first creates an account ('Sign Up') and confirms it by e-mail; OSS returns are filed there too. The page does not mention Tax For All. A refused applicant may ask for adjustment by e-mail, appeal to the Tax Commissioner within 60 days and go to the Administrative Court within 75 days. The page's €85 late-registration and €100 late-return penalties are listed for Cyprus as Member State of consumption.

m-b4c52f52.t: Filing VAT and VIES returns for someone else in Cyprus's Tax For All portal needs a listing as 'representative', not a professional licence, on the Tax Department's own texts read 6 October 2026. A would-be representative creates a TFA account and submits form TFA 04, which asks for the applicant's own VAT registration number, name, user name and contacts, signed in one of six capacities (self-employed, partner, director, secretary, administrator or trustee, authorised officer) with an ID copy, plus a Registrar certificate of directors for a company; it asks for no ICPAC, Bar or other qualification. The taxpayer appoints the representative by form TFA 03, online or on the VAT form TD 1101.

m-8e8bac98.t: A seller established in Cyprus that uses the EU One Stop Shop (Union scheme) is identified there by the VAT number Cyprus has already given it. Article 369d of VAT Directive 2006/112/EC (consolidated version of 14 April 2025, read 6 October 2026) says the Member State of identification 'shall use the individual VAT identification number already allocated to the taxable person in respect of his obligations under the internal system'. On that wording, Cyprus VAT registration comes before OSS use; the Commission's Cyprus OSS page does not say so itself.

m-6fa0b144.t: When an online seller's use of the EU One Stop Shop (Union scheme) starts is set by EU law: under art. 57d(1) of Council Implementing Regulation (EU) No 282/2011, inserted by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/2026, the scheme applies from the first day of the calendar quarter following the trader's notice to the Member State of identification, or, where the first covered supply comes earlier, from the date of that supply provided the trader informs that State no later than the tenth day of the following month. Art. 57e: the trader is identified in the scheme by his ordinary VAT number.

m-6d43b6bb.t: An online shop's registration in the EU One Stop Shop (union scheme) comes after its Cyprus VAT registration: under art. 369d of VAT Directive 2006/112/EC (in force; consolidated text of 14 April 2025 read 6 October 2026) the Member State of identification uses 'the individual VAT identification number already allocated' to the trader under the domestic system. The scheme is one Member States 'shall permit' traders to use (art. 369b), not a duty; it becomes relevant once intra-EU distance sales to consumers exceed €10,000 in a calendar year, or the seller opts to tax them at destination, when they are taxed in the customer's Member State (art. 59c).

m-4cbd810a.t: Splitting one business among two or more persons to stay under the Cyprus VAT threshold can be overridden. Under para. 2 of Part I of the First Schedule to VAT Law 95(I)/2000 (consolidated text read 6 October 2026) the Commissioner may direct that the persons named be treated as a single taxable person liable to register, from the date of the direction or a later date it sets. He may name a person only if satisfied that the person makes taxable supplies in activities that properly belong to one business carried on with others, that the whole would be liable to register, and that avoiding registration is the main reason or one of the main reasons for the arrangement.

m-28ab36da.t: The second counter for a Cyprus VAT application, the Point of Single Contact (PSC Cyprus) of the Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, gives its office as 5-6 Kinira Street, 1102 Nicosia, open Monday to Friday 7:00-14:30, telephone +357 22409318, e-mail businessincyprus@meci.gov.cy (contact page modified 17 March 2026, read 6 October 2026). The business portal's tax page (modified 15 September 2026) says form T.D. 1101 'can be submitted by hand at the closest District Tax Department Office ... or by hand or post at the PSC Cyprus'. No appointment requirement is stated.

m-24597444.t: Cyprus law times compulsory VAT registration from the trigger, not from incorporation. Under the First Schedule, Part I, of VAT Law 95(I)/2000 (cylaw text read 6 October 2026) a person established in Cyprus whose taxable supplies in the year to a month's end exceeded the threshold must notify the Commissioner within thirty days from the end of that month and is registered from the end of the next month or an agreed earlier date (paras 1(1)(α), 5), unless the Commissioner accepts that the coming year will stay below the lower limit (para 1(3)); one expecting to exceed it in the next thirty days notifies before they end and is registered from their start (paras 1(1)(β), 6).

m-b491de8d.t: As of 5 Oct 2026 VAT registration in Cyprus is still not an online service: the Tax Department's page says the request is filed on form T.F. 1101 'in printed form' at the District Offices, and states no processing time. The government business portal (page modified 15 September 2026) adds a second counter - the form may be handed in at the nearest District Tax Office 'or by hand or post at the PSC Cyprus', the Point of Single Contact of the Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry - and asks for a copy of a document proving taxable activity in Cyprus, such as a contract or an invoice. Neither page says how long the VAT number takes.

m-a88826fe.t: The Cyprus Tax Department's VAT Leaflet 3 'Registration in the VAT Register' (November 2001, still linked from its VAT registration page on 5 Oct 2026) says what an intending trader must show: a business that has started but makes no taxable supplies yet may register if it intends to make them, and must send written evidence, which 'may include' details of arrangements made, copies of proposed contracts, building permits, details of purchases made for the business, or patent applications; without it the examination 'may be delayed'. On timing it says only that the registration number and certificate come once the examination is completed. It is guidance of 2001, naming the old form VAT 101.

m-809f1ba8.t: The euro figure of the Cyprus VAT registration threshold stands in the statute in one place only. Law 104(I)/2025 (Gazette No. 5043, 25 June 2025; deemed in force from 1 January 2025) added Section 2 to Part IA of the First Schedule of VAT Law 95(I)/2000; its point 5(1)(α) exempts a small enterprise established in another Member State from registering when its yearly turnover in Cyprus, counted from the time it would become liable under Part I, Section 1, para 1(1), 'does not exceed fifteen thousand six hundred euro (€15.600)'.
