Art. 5(2) lists 'a place of management', a branch and an office as permanent establishments; art. 10(1) makes dividends paid to a resident of the other state taxable only there.

m-3a93291f.t: Under s. 2 of Cyprus's Cap. 109 (CyLaw text read 6 October 2026; last amendment listed 161(I)/2011), an 'alien' is any non-citizen of the Republic and includes a company controlled by aliens and a foreign company, but not EU or EEA citizens, nor a legal person formed under another EU Member State's law with its seat, central administration or principal place of business in the EEA. A body is 'controlled by aliens', for acquiring immovable property, where aliens make up half or more of its directors, or hold half or more of its votes (directly or through others voting for them) or shares, or constitutional powers to have it run as they wish, or half or more of its controlling interest.

m-38849e47.t: What the Cyprus Tax Department asks before certifying a company as tax resident: form T.D.98 (2015), the only company form on its tax residence certificate page (updated 28 September 2026). It asks whether the company is incorporated in Cyprus and tax resident only there; whether most board meetings are held in Cyprus, the board takes the key management and commercial decisions, its minutes are kept in Cyprus and the majority of the board are Cyprus tax residents; whether shareholders meet in Cyprus; and whether seal, books and records are kept there. A director signs that management and control are exercised in Cyprus. The certificate costs €80 in stamps.

m-2e508bc4.t: Time limits in Cyprus's foreign-investment screening Law 194(I)/2025 (s. 5): within 20 working days of a complete application the Ministry of Finance decides whether the investment will be screened and tells the investor within 5 working days; if it screens, it decides within 65 working days whether the investment may harm security or public order. Both clocks stop while requested information is outstanding, and approval exists only once the investor has it in writing. Failure to notify carries an administrative fine of €5,000 to €50,000 (s. 12(1)(α)), and an un-notified notifiable investment may be examined for five years after completion (s. 3(8)(γ)).

m-27c4ce6f.t: What sets a branch apart, per Cap. 113 and the Registrar's pages (read 6 October 2026): registration 'does not require the creation of a new legal entity' - the foreign company itself operates in the Republic; once it has filed its documents it may hold immovable property as if incorporated under the Law (s. 348); it must show its name and country of incorporation at every place of business and on letterheads, and state that its members' liability is limited where it is (s. 351). Two Registrar overseas-company pages still ask a €350 annual fee by 30 June, while its companies' page says it was repealed from 2024 by Law 25(I)/2024, which deleted s. 391, Cap. 113's only annual-fee provision.

m-1ea65f9b.t: A foreign company trading in Cyprus through a branch is taxed as a non-resident with a permanent establishment if managed and controlled abroad; if managed and controlled in Cyprus it is resident (Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002, art. 2). Art. 5(2)(α) charges a non-resident on 'any profits or other benefits from a permanent establishment situated in the Republic'; art. 2 lists a branch and an office as permanent establishments; companies pay 15% (Second Schedule, text of 6 October 2026). Under art. 5(4) such non-residents 'may elect' the same tax treatment as residents. No charge on remitting branch profits to head office was found in that Law or the Special Defence Contribution Law 117(I)/2002.

m-1d511154.t: Per Politis (13 September 2026), CY Login, the government sign-in, is linked through the eIDAS network with 20 countries, letting European citizens use their own country's recognised eID 'on compatible Cypriot services', and the Registrar of Companies' new system is being designed with CY Login access built in. The article does not say which services are compatible; on 6 October 2026 the Registrar's e-filing access page still named only registration with the gov.cy gateway, so whether an EU founder can file with a home-country eID today is not shown.

m-1d03198b.t: The chair of the House Interior Committee, AKEL MP Aristos Damianou, said after its session of 3 September 2026 that the texts agreed before the May 2026 election covered natural persons only, and that the committee would return to the subject in October 2026, including rules for companies, on which he said there are legal difficulties (AKEL statement published 4 September 2026; Cyprus Mail reported the October plan on 3 September). As of 6 October 2026 no date for that session was found published and no report of it was found.

m-16fad0f5.t: The Cyprus Ministry of Finance's FDI screening guidance (28 July 2026, Q3.8) says whether a target is of strategic importance is judged by 'the actual activities carried out by the relevant undertaking in the Republic of Cyprus', not by the group's sector or the deal's label. Where a Cypriot entity 'performs only limited sales, marketing, administrative or support functions' and does not itself engage in activities linked to sensitive infrastructure, technologies, inputs or information, the transaction 'may not necessarily fall within' mandatory notification; access to sensitive data or services linked to critical infrastructure 'may be a relevant indication' of strategic importance.

m-117da5de.t: For a Cyprus company owned through another company, the Registrar's 'Guidance to the Final Solution of the Beneficial Ownership Register' (Version 2.1, February 2025; advisory, 'no legal value' per its disclaimer) has it declare the natural persons holding more than 25% through the chain: across successive levels the share is 'the multiplication of the ownership percentages', and direct and indirect holdings are added. If the chain reaches a company listed on a regulated market (e.g. Frankfurt; London), that entity is declared instead, with name, jurisdiction and market. A non-Cypriot owner not resident in Cyprus is identified by passport or ID card, with any second nationality.

m-0f6112fc.t: 'Foreign investor' in Cyprus's screening Law 194(I)/2025 turns on nationality or place of incorporation: a natural person who is not a national of an EU or EEA state or Switzerland, or a third-country undertaking, that makes or intends to make a foreign direct investment (s. 2). The duty also reaches an entity at least 25%-owned, beneficially owned or controlled by a foreign investor that invests in an undertaking of strategic importance (s. 3(6)); the Ministry's guidance of 28 July 2026 (Q3.6) applies this to entities incorporated in Cyprus, the EU, the EEA or Switzerland. Neither text mentions residence: on their wording a third-country national living in Cyprus is a foreign investor.

m-0c46cdaa.t: As of 6 October 2026 no Cyprus law transposing Directive (EU) 2025/25 (deadline 31 July 2027) was found: of the 2025-2026 Companies Law amendments on CyLaw, Law 28(I)/2025 cites Delegated Directive (EU) 2023/2775, Law 162(I)/2025 the sustainability-reporting directives, Laws 155(I)/2025 and 2(I)/2026 no directive; the partnerships amendment Law 156(I)/2025 cites none, and the 2026 list (to Law 128(I)/2026) has no other such law. EUR-Lex's transposition page shows 0 Cyprus measures. Meanwhile a branch of a company from another Member State files apostilled true copies of its constitution, translated into Greek if not in Greek or English (Registrar's filing page).

m-0aa296df.t: Per Nomoplatform's bill records read on 6 October 2026, the plenary vote on three members' amendments of Cap. 109 on aliens buying property (files 23.02.066.008-2025, tabled 23 January 2025; .208-2025 and .211-2025, tabled 6 November 2025) and on a companion amendment of the Immovable Property (Transfer and Mortgage) Law (.210-2025) was postponed on 6 April and again on 16 April 2026, with no later entry. They are still live: KYPE reported four members' bills on the subject (unnamed) pending before the Interior Committee on 3 September 2026. A fifth Cap. 109 bill (.059-2025, tabled 27 February 2025, on 'alien Cypriot' status for children of non-Cypriot mothers) is pending there.

m-092793dc.t: Cap. 109's definition of a 'trust for the benefit of an alien' reads differently in two texts. The Greek consolidated text on CyLaw (read 6 October 2026) includes any arrangement under which property not owned by an alien is held by or for him or is at his disposal 'in another way or under a lease not falling within' s. 3(6)(α); the Law Commissioner's English consolidation (to 1 October 2007; Wayback snapshot of 24 June 2022) says 'otherwise than under a lease not falling within' it. The English excludes leases of 33 years or less; the Greek, read literally, does not clearly do so. The English edition says only the Gazette texts are authentic; the 1972 Gazette original was not read.

m-039419a4.t: Since 25 July 2025 the Cyprus Companies Law (ss. 365ΙΑ-365ΙΒ, inserted by s. 12 of Law 155(I)/2025, in force on publication) has the Registrar issue certificates in electronic form and, on anyone's application, an English-language certificate or certified true copy, admissible in any legal proceedings as equal to the original, 'notwithstanding' s. 17 of the sworn-translators Law 45(I)/2019; electronic certificates carry a qualified electronic seal under Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 and fees are set by the Council of Ministers. Other parts of Law 155(I)/2025 start on a date the Registrar notifies in the Gazette.

m-0318bdad.t: A government bill amending the Cyprus Companies Law, approved by the Council of Ministers on 6 August 2026 and tabled in the House on 17 September 2026 (referred to the Committee on Energy, Commerce, Industry and Tourism), would let the Registrar refuse a company's registration and other requests, and strike companies off, on grounds such as national security, public order or state sovereignty, on information from a competent authority; per CyprusNews.eu its proposed s. 397 allows striking off without any reasoning being required. Per Economy Today (24 September 2026) and CyprusNews.eu (25 September 2026); bill text not read; pending, not law, on 6 October 2026.

m-000a9d3b.t: As of 6 October 2026 the Cyprus Registrar of Companies registers an overseas company's place of business on forms AE1, AE2 and AE3 for €380 (the same online and over the counter, per its fee list), plus €100 for the accelerated procedure. Its guidance asks for true copies of the constitutional documents certified by a Hague apostille (or by the competent authority where the country is not a party) and, if not in Greek or English, a Greek translation by affidavit or by a sworn translator of the Republic; its review criteria list the Greek translation without that exception and require €86 in stamps with form AE1. Neither page states a maximum age for the foreign documents.

m-fb3aec0c.t: The Pancyprian Organisation of Freelance Professional Designers, Architects and Civil Engineers (POEEM) publishes terms of engagement with fee tables (posted 15 October 2020, read 6 October 2026) that set a minimum fee of €350 per unit for a change of use of an existing building; where alterations, additions or conversions are needed, its first-category percentages of construction cost apply instead. The tables also price expert reports at €100 an hour, and its engagement form says fees exclude VAT. This is the association's own scale, not a law: the text leaves its General Assembly approval date blank, and ETEK says no statutory fee scale for private works exists.

m-f9850d72.t: Per the firm, Christophi & Associates LLC (Nicosia, HE240652) charges €1,300 plus VAT, which it calls all-inclusive, to form a standard company: Registrar fees, memorandum and articles in English, the certificate of incorporation and other certificates, and a registered office for the first 12 months (undated pages read 6 October 2026; its FAQ still lists 'the annual levy' among recurring obligations). Its calculator prices add-ons plus VAT: registered office and secretary €350 a year each, nominee director and nominee shareholder €650 a year each, bank-account assistance €500, tax and UBO registration €200 each. It gives 7-10 working days standard, 2-3 express for an extra fee.

m-f5bed742.t: A.N. Easy Corporate Ltd (HE456719), which says it is 'Licensed and Supervised by the Cyprus Bar Association', publishes VAT-inclusive prices (read 6 October 2026): company registration €1,200 standard or €1,400 expedited ('6-8 working days'), covering name application, drafting of memorandum and articles, government filing fees, 'HE1 Stamp Duty Fees', the four certificates, tax registration, UBO registration, courier and out-of-pocket costs. Sold separately, incl. VAT: registered office €65 a month, VAT registration €200, Social Insurance registration €300, bank-account opening €600, seal €20. Accounting from €145 a month and audit €1,190, both incl. VAT, for very small businesses.

m-f27f7070.t: Per the firm's own schedule (version 1.1, PDF created 18 March 2026, linked from its fees page on 6 October 2026), Fidesta Ltd, a CySEC-licensed administrative service provider, sells a 'Self-Managed Cyprus LTD' for owner-directors at €1,350 plus €133.95 VAT, €1,483.95 in all: name approval, formation, Registrar-certified memorandum and articles and four certificates, first-year registered office and secretary, seal, tax registration, filing of UBO details, English memorandum file and express incorporation. From year two it charges from €1,000 plus VAT a year; accounting and audit are excluded. Its November 2025 schedule priced the package, then without UBO filing, at €1,070 plus €80.75 VAT.

m-ecf4d154.t: Two Cyprus firms read on 6 October 2026 put the advocates' Pension Fund stamp for forming a company into the client's price at €49 for €1,000 share capital: George K. Konstantinou LLC, a law company ('HE1 stamp payable to the Cyprus Bar Association €49', page of 3 October 2026), and EasyCorporate, a Bar-registered provider whose guide (updated 13 March 2026) gives '€49 (as of January 2026)' and whose packages list 'HE1 Stamp Duty Fees'. The Fees Regulations (Part III item 9(α), unchanged by the 2017-2023 amendments) set €40 for a company with capital up to €2,000, and s. 29(1) of the Advocates Law (Cap. 2) forbids an advocate to charge a client any such fee he paid.

m-e2ed01ff.t: No ICPAC-registered firm was found on 6 October 2026 publishing a self-employed package of bookkeeping plus tax return. CYAUSE Audit Services Ltd, on ICPAC's register, prices single items on an undated page; the web-archive copies of 14 November 2025 and 12 March 2026 and the live page all show €225 for registering an individual as self-employed and 'from' €150 for a simple personal tax return (IR.1), per the firm, excluding VAT. Philippou Accounting & Tax Ltd (PLF Accounting), which says statutory audit goes through partner ICPAC-licensed auditors, lists the personal tax return as 'Fixed quote'.

m-e1e956d7.t: Limassol law firm Chambers & Co's fee schedule (modified 26 August 2026, read 6 October 2026; 'all fees are subject to 19% VAT where applicable') lists a 'corporate package' of €2,600 - name application €30, express incorporation €100, registration €2,320 (which it says covers Registrar fees, paperwork and filing, certificates, memorandum and articles, share certificates, seal, first directors and minutes) and tax code €150. Under 'Annual cost & additional services', without marking which recur, it lists secretary €500 and registered office €500 (both 'Required'), an optional natural-person nominee director €1,500, HE32 filing €350, an 'AML Compliance Fee' €400 and VAT registration €350.

m-db654c50.t: No fee scale for engineers' or architects' private work exists in Cyprus, per the Scientific and Technical Chamber (ETEK)'s undated FAQ read 6 October 2026: draft regulations on minimum services and fee scales for architecture, civil, mechanical and electrical engineering were approved by ETEK's General Council and sent to the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Works for the House, but 'for a series of reasons' have not yet been taken forward; ETEK says it is pressing to speed this up. For public works, fee scales agreed before EU accession were abolished on accession as incompatible with the acquis, which ETEK, citing its legal opinion, considers wrong and has asked to reinstate.

m-d488359a.t: Per Green Dot Cyprus's pages (read 6 October 2026), the collective system for non-packaging paper, ΔΙ.ΧΑ., whose member registration, declarations and collections Green Dot handles as exclusive agent, covers newspapers, magazines, books, office paper, school notebooks, envelopes and catalogues. Joining costs a one-off registration fee of €200 plus VAT and a yearly certificate renewal of €150 plus VAT, with an application form and a signed accession agreement (registration page modified 20 April 2026).

m-ce648433.t: The Paphos accounting firm Ioannou & Co Ltd (reg. no. 489547; page modified 19 July 2026, read 6 October 2026) prices accounting and audit together by ledger lines a year, plus 19% VAT: €1,500 for 1-50 lines up to €3,000-€3,100 for 651-800, with company tax filing and up to three dividend declarations included; with the UBO update (€50), annual return (€80) and a director's tax declaration (€70) printed yearly totals run €1,700-€3,500, or €700 for a dormant company. VIES and OSS filings are €200 a year each; payroll tax declarations €100-180. One-off: incorporation €1,000; yearly registered address €250.

m-be6d3489.t: Signatures and seals on documents in Cyprus are certified by certifying officers appointed by the Interior Minister under Law 165(I)/2012, at least one per municipal parish; a practising lawyer, estate agent or banker may not be one (s. 3(4)). The Law set €2 per signature or seal (s. 10(1)); the Minister's notice K.D.P. 48/2024 (Gazette No. 5856, 16 February 2024) replaced this with maximum fees per document: €5 for 1-2 pages, €10 for 3-10, €25 for 11-100, €40 above, plus at most €2 per extra signer or seal, and at most €10 for travel. For private documents sent abroad, such as powers of attorney, it sends further certification to the Justice Ministry or citizen service centres.

m-b99aace7.t: Per Green Dot Cyprus's own pages (read 6 October 2026), joining costs a one-off €50 plus VAT and a membership agreement that is 'one and non-negotiable'. Its 'approved fees of the System for the years 2017-2025' run per tonne from €11.80 (commercial wood) to €149.41 (other non-reusable household packaging), PET and HDPE €100.60, pesticide packaging €380. The page (modified 26 March 2025) also lists yearly fees by tonnage band - €100 for 0-1 t, €142.5 for 1-2 t, €237.5 for 2-5 t, up to €1,900 for 25-50 t - which Green Dot's 2026 'declaration with categorisation' form charges, plus VAT, to members whose last declaration falls in those bands. No 2026 per-tonne list was posted.

m-b4031458.t: Chambers & Co, a Limassol law firm stating it is regulated by the Cyprus Bar Association, publishes an hourly rate (fees page modified 28 May 2026, read 6 October 2026): €200-€500 plus VAT an hour by seniority of lawyer or partner, invoiced monthly. It also offers fixed fees paid in advance (court representation, drafting or reviewing a document), a general retainer or a deposit held in a trust account, and in some cases contingency fees, agreed in the engagement letter. Of the other firms read, Fidesta Ltd (an administrative service provider) bills non-standard work at €100-€200 an hour by staff level; Philippou Accounting & Tax says it does not bill by the hour.

m-a80eeb3e.t: Philippou Accounting & Tax Ltd (plf-accounting.com, Paphos), 'part of the Philippou Law Firm group', publishes 'from' fees excluding VAT and government costs (read 6 October 2026): an Accounting, Audit & Tax retainer from €2,048 a year - IFRS bookkeeping, statutory audit via partner ICPAC-licensed auditors or ISRE 2400 review where eligible, quarterly VAT with VIES/OSS where applicable, payroll and Social Insurance, corporate tax return; company formation from €998 one-off with tax registration, VAT registration where required, UBO filing and a bank or EMI introduction; tax relocation and non-dom set-up from €1,470. Single services: written fixed quote, no amount published.

m-a221bcf2.t: A second Cyprus law firm publishes an hourly figure: Harris Koufettas & Associates LLC's home page (modified 9 June 2026, read 6 October 2026) answers 'How much does a Cyprus lawyer cost?' with 'Cyprus fees are not centrally fixed. Hourly rates run €150–€300 depending on seniority', adding that it sends a written engagement letter with a fixed quote or a scoped hourly range before any work. The page does not say whether the range is its own rate or the market's, or whether VAT is included. The only other published rate found is Chambers & Co (chambersandco.com), €200-€500 plus VAT by its fee page of May 2026; it calls itself a law firm, but its Bar-registered entity was not identified.

m-9d08f123.t: Per the firm, George K. Konstantinou LLC, a Limassol law company (HE321623), prices forming a private company at €1,899-€2,099 in all, or €2,059-€2,259 with the memorandum and articles certified in English (page modified 3 October 2026, read 6 October 2026), for €1,000 share capital and accelerated processing. Its legal fee is €1,300-€1,500 plus 19% VAT; the rest it itemises as name approval €30, registration on HE1-HE3 €265, certificates with a certified memorandum and articles €220, an 'HE1 stamp payable to the Cyprus Bar Association' €49, courier €35, and optionally €160 for English translations. The price lists no registered office, secretary, tax or VAT registration.

m-9898d053.t: Published yearly prices for a firm-supplied director (read 6 October 2026): Fidesta Ltd €2,000 + VAT for a resident individual director in year one ('introductory rate', reviewed after) or €500 for a corporate director, plus €300 as bank signatory, which it calls mandatory with that service (schedule of 18 March 2026); Chambers & Co €1,500 + VAT for an optional natural-person nominee director; Meridian Trust €950 + VAT for resident directors from year two, 'if needed'; Florin Piciorlung's office €250 (VAT not stated); Polycarpos Philippou & Associates LLC only in its Enterprise package, from €1,850 a year + VAT from year two. Fidesta calls the resident director essential for tax residence.

m-888c1cb7.t: Per the firm, CYAUSE Audit Services Ltd's indicative yearly fee for accounting and audit, excluding VAT and 'without any commitment' (undated page read 6 October 2026), is €450 for a dormant company; under €1,500 for fewer than 50 invoices and under €1,800 for fewer than 100, both with no employees; under €3,000 for fewer than 300 invoices and 3 employees; under €5,000 for fewer than 500 and 8; above €5,000 beyond. It covers bookkeeping with VAT returns, monthly VIES, draft and audited statements and the company tax return; payroll must be agreed in advance. Corporation-tax payment (€150), HE32 filing (€75 plus disbursements) and provisional tax (€150) are extra.

m-862c1ca7.t: Per its own article (updated 3 September 2026, read 6 October 2026), the Paphos law firm Polycarpos Philippou & Associates LLC sells fixed-fee packages 'plus VAT at 19% and government fees billed at cost': Basic from €1,050 (name approval, incorporation documents and certificates, expedited registration, UBO and company tax registration, VAT, VIES and OSS registration); Standard from €2,300 (adds nominee secretary, registered office, an online corporate bank account, the AML report and annual UBO update), then from €950 a year; Enterprise from €3,900 (adds a Cyprus-resident nominee director and a local bank account), then from €1,850 a year. Accounting and audit from €2,100 plus VAT a year.

m-85526913.t: The Cyprus Architects Association's model contract for architects' services (2024 edition, read 6 October 2026) gives fee percentages of project value for private works that it calls indicative and 'in no case binding': up to €150,000, 6.70% for Category 1, which lists shops, entertainment venues and restaurants, and 7.60% for Category 2, which includes renovations or conversions of existing buildings. The percentage covers stages from preliminary services through the planning permit, the building permit, supervision and completion; additional services such as surveys of existing buildings are agreed separately.

m-82d076e7.t: Per AFIS Cyprus's own pages (read 6 October 2026), a liable company - one that imports batteries or devices with built-in batteries - joins by an application, a non-negotiable membership agreement and a one-off registration fee of €400 plus VAT. Members declare the batteries up to 2 kg they placed on the market, including those built into devices, once a year by 31 January or every quarter, and pay fees per piece set in the declaration form; AFIS says its fees are set by its board and approved by the Waste Management Advisory Committee when the system is licensed.

m-76ae3e69.t: Per WEEE Cyprus's own producer FAQ (read 6 October 2026), members declare the weight of household-type EEE placed on the market quarterly (by 10 April, 10 July, 10 October and 10 January), or yearly by 20 January where the scheme so decides, and pay its invoice within 30 days; 'As long as you have placed any quantity of E.E.E. on the market, you should complete the Declaration properly.' Its fees per tonne 'From 01/01/13- Today', excluding VAT per its declaration form, are €131.32 for small (under 50 cm) and €77.75 for large items in most categories, €77.75 for air conditioners, €217.63 for refrigerators, €229.34 for screens and TVs and €476.48 for fluorescent bulbs.

m-74e5a8cd.t: Per the firm's undated price lists (read 6 October 2026, all plus VAT), CYAUSE Audit Services Ltd charges €225 to register an individual as self-employed with Social Insurance and €225 for an objection to that office; from €150 for a simple personal tax return (IR1); €100 for a company tax number; €150-€250 for a company VAT number; €350 for OSS registration; €250 to register a company as an employer, €100 per employee; €200 for the first UBO declaration and €75 for each yearly confirmation; and €150-€210 an hour for tax or VAT advice. Monthly payroll runs €200 for fewer than 5 employees. Its pages disagree on some items: employer registration €150 on the payroll page.

m-678a1375.t: Asterisk Corporate Services (Nicosia), in its own guide (published 15 March 2026, modified 14 April 2026, read 6 October 2026), quotes no fixed formation price: a standard incorporation 'handled by a regulated professional services firm typically starts from €1,500-€2,000 plus VAT where applicable' and 'usually' includes government out-of-pocket expenses, which it puts at €500-€700. Its 'typical annual cost' table: registered office €300 (address only), secretary €300+, statutory accounting €1,000-€2,000+, statutory audit €1,200-€3,500+, tax compliance €200-€800+, in all €3,000+ a year. Fixed quotes are given only on request.

m-55fa7aed.t: Ioannou & Co Ltd's fee page (cyprustaxaccounting.com, modified 19 July 2026, read 6 October 2026) displays no nominee-director or nominee-secretary service: rows pricing them at €350 and €250 a year exist only inside an HTML comment in the page source and are not shown to visitors, so they are not prices the firm publishes. Among the one-off and recurring items it does display are incorporation €1,000, registered address €250 a year, certificate reissue €50 and change of directors or secretary €50, all plus 19% VAT.

m-545b7c9e.t: A Cyprus municipality also charges each legal person trading within its limits an annual fee (Municipalities Law 52(I)/2022, s. 56(6)) up to Sixth Schedule ceilings: a private company with up to 5 employees EUR 1,000, rising to EUR 4,000 over 30; partnerships EUR 1,000-5,000; insurance, shipping, banking and like firms and public companies EUR 10,000; legal persons whose registered office or management is with law, accounting or audit firms or administrative-service providers EUR 4,000; others EUR 1,500. Half if business starts in the second half-year; another municipality may charge only where the company has a permanent place of business there or works there over 60 working days a year.

m-40af905e.t: An undated price page of the Florin Piciorlung law office (florinpiciorlung.com, read 6 October 2026) shows how stale a firm's published price can be: next to a 'Corporate Package' at €1,150 plus VAT (government fees, paperwork, first-year registered office and secretary, certificates, Greek memorandum, seal, €1,000 capital) and a 'Corporate Plus' at €1,650 plus VAT with bank-account help, it lists €250 a year each for secretary, registered office, nominee shareholder and nominee director, and still lists an 'annual registration fee' of €350 payable to the Registrar - the company levy abolished from 2024. The same page also advertises formation 'From €1.200,- + VAT'.

m-33aa23c3.t: Per the firm, Polycarpos Philippou & Associates LLC prices yearly accounting, audit, VAT and payroll for a running company in three tiers by transactions a year, from €2,100 for up to 100, from €2,450 for 101-300 and from €3,450 for more than 300 (pricing page 'Fees current for 2026 · Content updated 28 August 2026', read 6 October 2026). All its fees exclude 19% VAT, government charges and actual expenses, which it bills at cost; it promises a fixed fee in an engagement letter and a refund of its professional fee if it does not deliver the service set out there, but no government or bank decision.

m-2e18b596.t: Published prices for an individual's yearly tax work in Cyprus, read 6 October 2026, are low next to company upkeep: Ioannou & Co Ltd prices tax filing for non-corporate clients at €80 each plus 19% VAT (fee page modified 19 July 2026); Fidesta Ltd charges €80 plus VAT for 'Execution of Income Tax return for Individuals (IR1)' (schedule of 18 March 2026) but prints no price for filing it, which for company returns it bills separately; EasyCorporate sells an individual's tax registration under the 60-day rule for €400 including VAT. None of the firms read publishes a bookkeeping package for a self-employed person; such work is quoted on request.

m-28de4f12.t: Harris Koufettas & Associates LLC, a Paphos law firm (HE366364), gives market ranges, not its own prices (page 'Last updated: April 9, 2026', read 6 October 2026): formation €1,200-€3,000 in year one (summary) or €1,500-€4,000 'through a professional service provider' (body); yearly upkeep €2,420-€4,000 dormant and €3,880-€6,920 small trading, per its survey of '10+ service providers'; bank-account help €500-€750. It says a Cyprus-resident founder who is his own director and secretary, with his home as registered office, pays €820-€1,400 a year dormant or €2,200-€4,000 trading; under Cap. 113 s. 171(1) a sole director may also be secretary only in a single-member company.

m-246ce5c2.t: Meridian Trust's '2025 Cyprus Company Formation Fees' page (cypruscompany.net, read 6 October 2026; prices exclude 19% VAT) gives 'a basic overview of the estimated costs', referring clients to it for current fees: €1,310 for incorporation with documents, minutes, share certificate, officer appointments and a first-year registered office and resident secretary, plus a €150 onboarding compliance fee, €1,460 in all; express incorporation €300 and name application €50 'if needed'. From year two: office €280, secretary €380, and 'if needed' resident directors €950 and nominee shareholders €300. VAT registration €500; bank help €750. It still lists an 'Annual Levy €350', abolished from 2024.

m-244c3dc8.t: No Cyprus firm was found on 6 October 2026 publishing its own price for preparing a café's licence applications or for change-of-use or building-permit work: CGP Christou LLC, a Larnaca practice on ETEK's register of consulting companies (C00226), offers only 'Get a quote', and Connor Legal's 2026 permit guide prices no service. Two professional associations do publish fee guidance for architects: POEEM's terms (posted 15 October 2020) set a minimum of €350 per unit for a change of use with no alterations, and the Cyprus Architects Association's 2024 model contract gives indicative, non-binding percentages of project value, such as 7.60% up to €150,000 for converting an existing building.

m-21ea8588.t: Separate service prices in Fidesta Ltd's own schedule (v1.1, PDF created 18 March 2026), all professional fees plus 19% VAT: tax registration and TIN €250; VAT registration €300; employer registration with Social Insurance €150, plus €50 per new employee; preparing and filing a Cyprus bank-account application €500 ('success is not guaranteed'); help with a European payment-service-provider account €400; bookkeeping from €500 a year; audited financial statements including tax-return filing from €800; annual return (HE32) €60; each VAT return from €200; payroll €50 per employee; share transfer €220 including an €80 state fee; non-standard senior-staff work €150 an hour.

m-112a3898.t: Re-fetched on 6 October 2026, the fee page of Ioannou & Co Ltd (Paphos, HE489547; modified 19 July 2026; prices exclude 19% VAT) hides only two rows from visitors, inside one HTML comment: nominee director €350 and nominee secretary €250 a year. Every other row renders, including the accounting-and-audit table by invoice lines (€1,700-€3,500 a year with UBO update, annual return and a director's tax declaration; dormant €700), tax filing for non-corporate clients €80, incorporation €1,000, registered address €250 a year, non-dom certificate €200, tax-residency certificate €200, an EU citizen's MEU1 registration certificate €300, mail forwarding €600 a year and change of officers €50.

m-0c4661ee.t: Per the firm, CYAUSE Audit Services Ltd, an ICPAC-registered accounting and audit firm in Nicosia, published on 11 February 2026 a quote it sent to one enquirer (read 6 October 2026), all plus VAT: incorporation €700 plus disbursements 'usually' €300-€700; first UBO declaration €300, then €75 a year; HE32 annual return €150 plus €20 disbursements; Registrar e-filing codes €50; tax and VAT registration €150 each; and yearly 'nominee fees' of €800 for a director, €500 for a secretary and €800 for a registered office, without saying which entity would act. Accounting and audit are priced separately by transaction volume.

m-c3735421.t: The Consumer Protection Service of the Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry enforces the Consumer Protection Law 112(I)/2021 ('Director' means the Director of that Service; amended in 2026 by Laws 30(I), 75(I) and 122(I)/2026). It also has a payments role: art. 99(1A) of the Payment Services Law 31(I)/2018 makes the Service the competent authority for merchants' compliance with arts 60 and 62 of that Law — prior disclosure of any charge or discount for using a payment instrument, and the rule in art. 62(5) that a payee may not request charges for the use of a specific payment instrument. Its powers under Law 112(I)/2021 were not read beyond the definitions. Read 4 October 2026.

m-f74929f7.t: By decision of the Tax Commissioner announced on 16 September 2026, the deadline for employers' annual PAYE withholding return (income tax and contributions withheld) for tax year 2025 is extended to 30 November 2026. A return filed after that date is late and, under art. 50A(a) of Law 4/1978, bears a fixed charge of €150 for a natural person, €500 for a legal person whose turnover or assets exceed €1,000,000 and €250 for any other legal person.

m-ef80d4c4.t: The recast Consumer Credit Directive (EU) 2023/2225 had to be transposed by 20 November 2025 and applies from 20 November 2026, bringing 'buy now, pay later' credit from third parties into scope. Its art. 2(2)(h) keeps outside a shop's own deferred payment with no third party offering credit, free of interest and charges except limited late-payment charges, paid within 50 days of delivery (14 days for online sellers that are not SMEs). As of 6 October 2026 cylaw's 2025-2026 lists (to Law 128(I)/2026, Gazette of 2 October 2026) show no law transposing it: the only consumer-credit amendment, Law 83(I)/2026 of 21 April 2026, re-harmonises the 2010 law with Directive 2008/48/EC.

m-ece0ba8c.t: The proposed regulation on European Business Wallets (COM(2025) 838 of 19 November 2025, procedure 2025/0358(COD)) - per Parliament's procedure summary, meant to 'streamline and secure interactions between businesses and public authorities across the EU', with representation mandates and a channel for official documents - has an ITRE report: the committee voted it on 10 September 2026 with a decision to open interinstitutional negotiations, and the report was tabled for plenary on 23 September 2026. As of 6 October 2026 OEIL shows 'Awaiting Parliament's position in 1st reading' and no forecast date. In the Council it is only Presidency information at the Telecoms Council of 1 December 2026.

m-da9bc1ca.t: Eurostat publishes a yearly business-demography news item - enterprise births, deaths and rates by member state, Cyprus included, for the business economy - in autumn: 25 October 2024 (data for 2022), 13 October 2025 (2023) and 1 October 2026 (2024: EU birth rate 10.4%, death rate 9.2% on preliminary death data; dataset bd_size). The edition with 2025 data is due in autumn 2027; its date was not published as of 6 October 2026. Eurostat defines a birth as a new combination of production factors and excludes mergers, break-ups and restructurings, so the count is not the number of companies formed at the Registrar.

m-d235bcec.t: The EU list of non-cooperative jurisdictions for tax purposes is reviewed twice a year: the revision of 17 February 2026 left 10 jurisdictions in Annex I (American Samoa, Anguilla, Guam, Palau, Panama, Russia, Turks and Caicos, US Virgin Islands, Vanuatu, Viet Nam), and the Council's indicative agenda puts conclusions on the next revision 'for approval' at ECOFIN on 9 October 2026; a February 2027 date is not published. In Cyprus the list drives the 17% special defence contribution on dividends and interest paid to linked (over 50%) companies in listed jurisdictions; the 5% low-tax-jurisdiction rule keys off the corporate tax rate, not this list.

m-b893ffa0.t: MONEYVAL's 72nd working groups and plenary meet in Strasbourg on 7-11 December 2026, per the FATF events calendar as archived on 11 July 2026; MONEYVAL's own site refused automated access on 6 October 2026, so 2027 dates were not seen (previous plenaries: 21-24 May and 2-6 December 2024, 10-13 June and 15-18 December 2025). The edition of MONEYVAL's 4th follow-up report on Cyprus created 27 June 2025 says the sixth-round on-site visit 'will take place in October 2028' and Cyprus 'will no longer be subject to the fifth-round follow-up process' (an earlier edition said it would stay in enhanced follow-up), so no Cyprus item is expected; no plenary agenda was seen.

m-b445783a.t: The new Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853 must be in force in national law by 9 December 2026 and applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 8 December 2026 (a corrigendum of 7 May 2026 replaced 'after 9 December'); the 1985 Directive keeps covering earlier products. For an online shop it widens who answers: where the maker is outside the EU, the importer and the authorised representative or, failing both, the fulfilment service provider (art. 8(1)(c)); where no EU operator can be identified, a distributor that fails within a month of a request to name one or its own supplier is liable (art. 8(3)). Cylaw's 2026 list shows no Cyprus transposing law.

m-b2f84ca6.t: No date is set for the Council decision on Cyprus's full Schengen accession as of 6 October 2026. The Commission's 2026 State of Schengen report (COM(2026) 150, 18 May 2026) lists 'Complete Cyprus' accession to the Schengen area' among priority actions for 2026-2027, after a monitoring activity in December 2025. Per the Cyprus Mail, a Commission spokesman said on 15 July 2026 that the College had adopted a report on Cyprus's application on 14 July and would present the State of Schengen report to the Council in September. The decision must be unanimous. The Presidency's results of the Home Affairs Council of 1 October 2026 mention only the 'overall state of the Schengen area'.

m-a20bae0b.t: The Cyprus Registrar of Companies publishes monthly statistics as three graph pages - newly registered business entities (year to date and by month), total registered entities, and main register filings - posted between the 4th and the 25th of the following month from October 2024 to September 2026 (latest: data to 31 August 2026, posted 23 September 2026). Full-year figures were posted on 10 January 2025 (for 2024) and 7 January 2026 (for 2025), so full-year 2026 figures can be expected in early January 2027; no publication schedule is announced.

m-94c6f496.t: Council of the EU presidencies in the calendar window are fixed by Council Decision (EU) 2016/1316: Ireland July-December 2026, Lithuania January-June 2027, Greece July-December 2027 (Cyprus held it January-June 2026). The presidency sets the agendas of Council meetings, so which files reach agreement in 2027 depends partly on the Lithuanian and Greek programmes; neither programme nor a 2027 meeting calendar was found published as of 6 October 2026.

m-8e3a34be.t: The last two deemed-dividend dates of Cyprus's special defence contribution fall in the window. Under art. 3Γ(1)(α) of Law 117(I)/2002 (as replaced by Law 245(I)/2025) a resident company is deemed to distribute 70% of its after-tax profits of 2024 and of 2025 at the end of two years from the end of the profit year - 31 December 2026 and 31 December 2027 - less dividends actually paid in the profit year and the two years after (art. 3Γ(4)); 17% is due only on the part attributable to individuals resident and domiciled in Cyprus on that date, paid with a declaration by 31 January of the third year after the profit year (art. 4(5)): 31 January 2027 and 2028.

m-8b2343c7.t: ECOFIN (EU finance ministers, Cyprus included) meets on 9 October 2026 in Luxembourg, 9 November 2026 in Brussels (budget format on 10 November) and 11 December 2026 in Brussels, per the Council's indicative agendas for the Irish Presidency of 25 June 2026. Items of interest: 9 October, conclusions revising the EU list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions; 11 December, 'political agreement' on the recast Council Directive on administrative cooperation in taxation (DAC) and the ECOFIN report on tax issues. Each meeting has an information point on current financial services proposals. Agendas are indicative.

m-82f2ee02.t: Cyprus must send its Draft Budgetary Plan for 2027 to the Commission and the Eurogroup by 15 October 2026, and the Commission must give its opinion 'in any event by 30 November' (Regulation (EU) No 473/2013, arts 6(1) and 7(1)). In the previous cycle the Council of Ministers approved the 2026 plan on 8 October 2025 and the Commission's opinion on Cyprus, C(2025) 9052, is dated 25 November 2025. As of 6 October 2026 the Ministry of Finance's list of plans shows no 2027 plan yet.

m-7c50a6f5.t: Cyprus's 2027 State Budget is tabled, not adopted, as of 6 October 2026. The Council of Ministers approved the budget bill and the Medium-Term Fiscal Framework 2027-2029 on Wednesday 16 September 2026, and the Minister of Finance submitted both to the House of Representatives on 24 September 2026 'for its consideration and approval'. His statement asks that the budget be 'adopted on time' and names no vote date.

m-79c6c1a7.t: No Cypriot parliamentary or presidential election falls between October 2026 and December 2027. The House of Representatives elected on 24 May 2026 sits for five years (Constitution art. 65), and the President's five-year term runs from installation until the new President is installed, the election being held before the term expires (art. 43(1), (3)); President Christodoulides said on 29 September 2026, as reported by the Cyprus Mail, that the next presidential election 'would not take place until February 2028'. No election date was set as of 6 October 2026.

m-71da6dd1.t: From 10 July 2027 an EU-wide cash ceiling applies directly in Cyprus: under art. 80 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 'persons trading in goods or providing services' may accept or make a cash payment only up to EUR 10,000, single or linked operations, with exceptions for payments between private individuals and for payments or deposits at the premises of banks, e-money issuers and payment service providers (those above the limit are reported to the FIU). Cyprus's own EUR 10,000 cap under Law 172(I)/2024 is equal, so the amount does not change; lower national limits remain allowed after consulting the ECB.

m-57f47185.t: European Council (heads of state or government, including Cyprus's President) meetings announced for the rest of 2026: 15-16 October 2026, an informal meeting on 13 November 2026, and 17-18 December 2026 in Brussels, per the Council's meeting page as archived on 6 August 2026 (last reviewed 22 July 2026); the Irish Presidency's calendar of 5 August 2026 also pencils a special European Council for 26-27 November 2026 'TBC'. Its conclusions give political direction, not law; 2027 meeting dates were not found published.

m-54aff5f7.t: Per Politis (28 September 2026), the House Finance Committee examines Cyprus's 2027 budget from 12 October to 16 November 2026 in eleven sessions: Ministry of Finance on 12 October; Energy, Commerce and Industry (the Registrar's ministry) on 19 October; Deputy Ministry of Tourism on 23 October; Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy on 6 November; Deputy Ministry of Migration on 9 November; Labour and Social Insurance on 16 November; written questions by 19 November. The House's own schedule was not read.

m-54895ea7.t: The European Semester's spring package - country reports assessing how each EU country, Cyprus included, implemented the 2025 country-specific recommendations, with new recommendations - was published by the Commission on 3 June 2026, and the Council's indicative agenda put adoption of the integrated recommendations on ECOFIN of 10 July 2026. The 2027 spring package date was not published as of 6 October 2026. Later Semester steps in the window include the Commission's opinion on Cyprus's 2027 Draft Budgetary Plan (by 30 November 2026) and the Alert Mechanism Report 2027 and euro-area recommendation, to be presented at ECOFIN on 11 December 2026 (indicative agenda).

m-542485f5.t: The proposed 'EU Inc.' regulation on a 28th corporate regime (COM(2026) 321 of 18 March 2026, procedure 2026/0074(COD)) is in committee as of 6 October 2026: the Parliament's Legislative Observatory shows 'Awaiting committee decision' in JURI (rapporteur René Repasi, draft report 29 June 2026, amendments 22 July 2026) and an indicative plenary first-reading date of 19 October 2026, a forecast, not a scheduled vote. At the Competitiveness Council of 24 September 2026 ministers were only informed by the Presidency of its state of play (the June indicative agenda had planned a policy debate); the Council's indicative agendas to December 2026 schedule no further step.

m-5406ba00.t: The Cyprus Ministry of Finance's presentation of the 2027 budget to the Council of Ministers (16 September 2026) reports that the newly enacted power to suspend a business and seal its premises for tax non-compliance 'is on track for implementation, with the first notices already delivered', and that a procedure for the newly enacted freezing of shares for unpaid tax is being drawn up. It gives no number of notices and no grounds. Of the grounds in art. 32A(1) of Law 4/1978 only failure to file returns counts from 1 January 2027; unpaid tax over EUR 20,000, missing or inaccurate invoices or receipts and obstructing an audit carry no such date.

m-5380ede7.t: The 6th ICPAC Mediterranean Finance Summit - a yearly conference carrying the name of the Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Cyprus and run by the events company QUBE Events - is set for 20-21 May 2027 at the Four Seasons Hotel, Limassol, per the organiser's page read on 6 October 2026; the 5th was held on 21-22 May 2026 in Limassol. The organiser's announced 2027 themes are AI-powered finance, growth and performance, risk and resilience, treasury leadership, leadership beyond finance and the future of finance; tax and company law are not among them.

m-4d59a16a.t: The first ViDA stage relevant to small online sellers is 1 January 2027: Member States must adopt and publish rules transposing Article 2 of Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 by 31 December 2026 and apply them from 1 January 2027. Among other points, Article 2 limits the EUR 10,000 threshold of art. 59c of the VAT Directive to goods dispatched from the seller's own Member State, and deems a seller registered in the union one-stop shop to have opted for taxation in the customer's state. Cylaw's 2025-2026 lists (to 2 October 2026) show no transposing law; the only 2026 VAT amendment, Law 109(I)/2026, lets the Tax Commissioner examine delayed reduced-rate housing applications until end-2026.

m-4d12d950.t: Cyprus counts a jurisdiction as 'non-cooperative' for special defence contribution only if it is in the last version of the EU list (Annex I) published in the Official Journal during the previous calendar year and also in the latest version in force (art. 2 of Law 117(I)/2002, read 6 October 2026). So the version published in 2026 - the one from the 9 October 2026 revision if it reaches the Official Journal before year-end - sets the list for 2027, a removal counts at once, and Viet Nam and Turks and Caicos, added on 17 February 2026, were not non-cooperative for this purpose in 2026.

m-36b91409.t: FATF plenary meetings in the calendar window, per the FATF events calendar as archived on 11 July 2026: 26-30 October 2026 (Paris), 22-26 February 2027, 21-25 June 2027 (Paris) and 18-22 October 2027 (Paris). Each plenary updates the FATF's lists of 'High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call for Action' and 'Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring' (last issued 19 June 2026); the EU's own list of high-risk third countries, which Cyprus obliged entities apply, is a separate Commission act.

m-26a668aa.t: The Cyprus Bar Association's triennial ordinary general meeting is convened by the Attorney General for Wednesday 14 October 2026, 15:00, at the Filoxenia Conference Centre, Nicosia (notice dated 21 September 2026). Its agenda includes electing the Bar's President (at least twelve years' practice) and four advocates as members of the Bar Council; candidacies were due by noon on 7 October 2026. Under s. 21 of the Advocates Law (Cap. 2) the meeting is due by 31 October every third year and the vote is held in the districts at a place and time the Attorney General sets. The Council, which also has members not elected at this meeting, is the AML supervisor of lawyers.

m-1a648efd.t: The Central Bank of Cyprus publishes two recurring reports with no announced dates. Economic Bulletin, twice a year: the December 2024 and 2025 editions appeared on 12 February 2025 and 30 January 2026, the June editions on 21 July 2025 and 1 July 2026, so the December 2026 edition falls due around January-February 2027. Financial Stability Report, yearly and titled by the preceding year: '2023' on 22 October 2024, '2024' on 16 July 2025, '2025' on 28 July 2026 (linked as a Greek file); the next, '2026', edition was not dated as of 6 October 2026. Both give the CBC's view of banks, credit and risks; neither sets rules.

m-17b9cf79.t: The Commission Work Programme 2027 is 'expected to be published on 20 October 2026' and to be presented to the General Affairs Council on 19 November 2026; the three institutions plan to put a Joint Declaration on the EU's 2027 legislative priorities to that Council on 15 December 2026 for signature at the European Council of 17 December 2026 (Council note 13103/26, 17 September 2026). The Commission's Letter of intent of 16 September 2026 lists 21 new initiatives, among them a 'Bank competitiveness and simplification package' and 'Tackling unjustified territorial supply constraints in the Single Market'.

m-16a32dd4.t: The date of the Cyprus House plenary vote on the 2027 State Budget was not published as of 6 October 2026: the Finance Minister's tabling statement of 24 September 2026 asks only that it be 'adopted on time', and no date or month was found in government or press reports read that day (the House's site could not be read). The two previous budgets were voted by the plenary in December: the 2026 budget on Wednesday 17 December 2025 (KYPE report; the Ministry of Finance welcomed the vote the same day) and the 2025 budget on 18 December 2024, 37 votes to 18 (per Nomoplatform).

m-136d040d.t: Nothing is scheduled for the proposed Late Payment Regulation (COM(2023) 533, procedure 2023/0323(COD)). As of 6 October 2026 the Parliament's Legislative Observatory shows it 'Awaiting Council's 1st reading position', with Parliament's first-reading vote of 23 April 2024 the last key event and no forecast date; the Council's indicative agendas for July-December 2026 (which as a rule omit 'A' items) do not list it; and the Commission's 2026 work programme of 21 October 2025 keeps it among pending proposals (Annex III), not among intended withdrawals. Until something moves, Directive 2011/7/EU as transposed nationally remains the rule.

m-12b2c491.t: The next Cyprus minimum-wage decision is due in late 2027. Under para 7 of the Minimum Wage Decree (K.D.P. 350/2022) the committee's report must reach the Minister of Labour 'at least two months before each revision' and the Minister then proposes an adjustment, which may be zero, to the Council of Ministers; with revisions every two years from 1 January 2024, the report for a 1 January 2028 revision is due by about 1 November 2027. The last two decrees were published on 20 December 2023 (K.D.P. 402/2023) and 31 December 2025 (K.D.P. 427/2025).

m-127c6eca.t: The Cyprus Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KEVE) holds its annual general meeting in December, with the President of the Republic and ministers attending and the Chamber presenting its proposals on the economy: the AGM of 12 December 2024 (President's speech published by the Presidency that evening) and the 98th AGM on Monday 8 December 2025 (per Ant1, archived copy). The 2026 date was not seen as of 6 October 2026 - the Chamber's site refused automated access. In 2024 the President used the meeting to announce the timing of the tax reform proposal ('early 2025').

m-0c6a6aee.t: Directive (EU) 2025/25, which creates the EU Company Certificate and the digital EU power of attorney and exempts both from legalisation, must be transposed - laws 'adopted and published' - by 31 July 2027 and applied from 31 July 2028; two provisions (art. 19(2)(i) and art. 19b of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as amended) follow a year later, in force by 1 August 2028 and applied from 1 August 2029. So a Cyprus transposing law is due within the calendar window, but nothing changes for founders before 31 July 2028.

m-06167bd4.t: The strike-off round for unpaid annual levy announced by the Cyprus Registrar of Companies on 30 September 2026 begins in December 2026 with a notice published in the Official Gazette; under s. 327(3) and (5) of the Companies Law, Cap. 113, the Registrar may strike a company off only after three months from that notice, unless cause to the contrary is shown by an objection in the prescribed form before they expire - so no removal in this round falls before about March 2027. The announcement gives no publication date. The separate track for overdue annual returns runs to 31 December 2026.

m-05d348e2.t: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1731 of 15 July 2026, adopted under art. 5a(23) of the eIDAS Regulation, amends wallet Implementing Regulations 2024/2977, 2024/2979, 2024/2980 and 2024/2982 'as regards applicable standards and specifications'. Published on 22 July 2026, it entered into force on 11 August 2026; two requirements - the user's portrait in the mandatory identification data and wallet checks of relying-party registration certificates - apply only from 11 August 2028. The wallet deadlines run from the entry into force of the art. 5a(23) acts; no text read on 6 October 2026 says whether this act moves the 24 December 2026 date derived from the 2024 acts.

m-e59d7408.t: On 10 December 2025 the Commission proposed suspending until 1 January 2035 the duty of producers established in one EU state to appoint an authorised representative when selling packaging or batteries to end users in another (COM(2025) 982: art. 45(3) of Regulation 2025/40 and art. 56(3) of Regulation 2023/1542) and, by a parallel directive, the same duty for electrical equipment (COM(2025) 983: art. 17(2) of Directive 2012/19/EU); states could still require it of third-country producers. Per the European Parliament's Legislative Train (updated 20 September 2026), Council talks on both were discontinued and the committee vote was planned for early October 2026; neither is adopted.

m-d88ae42f.t: The Finance Ministry's presentation of the 2027 budget bill, approved by the Council of Ministers on 16 September 2026, lists Tax Department compliance actions: letters to persons and businesses that have not registered or filed returns, 'followed by criminal prosecution' if they do not comply in time; on-site inspections; charges on property, freezing of bank balances and prosecution for unpaid withheld taxes; a procedure being drawn up for the 'newly passed' freezing of shares for tax debts; and the newly passed suspension of businesses and sealing of premises, notices already served. It names no new tax rate or measure for 2027; revised forecasts go to the Commission on 15 October 2026.

m-d77169d3.t: Under art. 44(1) of Regulation (EU) 2025/40 each Member State sets up its register of packaging producers within 18 months of the entry into force of the first implementing act on the register, which art. 44(14) required by 12 February 2026. The Commission published the draft act (a single format for registration and reporting, Ares(2026)7688068) on its Have-your-say portal on 6 August 2026 with comments until 10 September 2026; on 6 October 2026 the portal showed comments closed and no adoption. No register of packaging producers under the Regulation was found on the Cyprus Department of Environment's EPR page or Green Dot's site on 6 October 2026.

m-d5f9da69.t: Cyprus has a draft, but no tabled bill was found, for the first stage of the EU 'VAT in the digital age' Directive (EU) 2025/516, which Member States must adopt by 31 December 2026 and apply from 1 January 2027. The Ministry of Finance's draft, in consultation 30 April-28 May 2026, starts on 1 January 2027; for a seller established only in Cyprus and within the EUR 10,000 cross-border threshold, an opt-in to tax in the customer's state covers two calendar years and is deemed made by sellers in the Union one-stop shop. On 6 October 2026 the page reads 'under processing'; the Gazette search finds no text citing '2025/516', and CyLaw's 2026 laws have none.

m-d48014c5.t: The EU Pay Transparency Directive (EU) 2023/970 had to be transposed by 7 June 2026 (art. 34(1)); it gives job applicants a right to information on the initial pay or its range, for example in the vacancy notice or before the interview, and bars employers from asking about pay history (art. 5), with no size threshold. Cyprus has not enacted it as of 6 October 2026: the draft bill was consulted on from 5 November to 4 December 2025 ('completed'; results and a revised draft posted), CyLaw's 2026 laws (to Law 128(I)/2026) have none, and the Gazette search finds '2023/970' only in tender notices. By our reading, art. 5 binds a private employer only once the Cyprus law is in force.

m-d3b6a873.t: Under eIDAS as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183, each Member State must provide at least one EU Digital Identity Wallet within 24 months of the entry into force of the implementing acts under arts 5a(23) and 5c(6) (Implementing Regulations 2024/2977, 2979, 2980, 2981, 2982; in force 24.12.2024): by our count 24 December 2026. Private relying parties other than micro and small enterprises that must use strong user authentication by law or contract, including banks, must accept it on the user's voluntary request by 24 December 2027 (art. 5f(2)). Cyprus's tender to integrate the wallet into its 'Digital Citizen' app (TED 609805-2026, est. EUR 9,778,000) closes 13 October 2026.

m-ca1a1da6.t: Where to watch Cyprus bills, as tested on 6 October 2026: parliament.cy answers scripted requests with a Cloudflare security check (HTTP 403); drafts appear on the e-consultation portal with a status ('under processing', 'completed'); bills are printed 'for general information' in the Gazette's Annex Six (its page lists issues since 10 July 2026; older ones via full-text search); enacted laws are numbered on CyLaw (to Law 128(I)/2026, No. 98(I)/2026 absent). Annex Six does not show a bill's stage: the AML (Amendment) (No. 3) Bill of 2025, printed on 6 February 2026 before Law 25(I)/2026 of 20 March 2026 changed the same provisions, was printed again on 25 September 2026.

m-c99b1f85.t: The Commission proposed European Business Wallets on 19 November 2025 (COM(2025) 838, procedure 2025/0358(COD)): a digital wallet for companies; by 24 months after entry into force public sector bodies must let them identify and authenticate, sign or seal, submit documents and send or receive notifications through it to meet a reporting obligation or an administrative procedure, with up to 36 months for alternatives to its registered-delivery service (art. 16). It would apply one year after entry into force. As of 6 October 2026 it is a proposal, 'Awaiting Parliament's position in 1st reading'; ITRE adopted its report and a negotiating mandate on 10 September 2026; no next date is listed.

m-aa919749.t: Cyprus is not yet a full Schengen member on 6 October 2026: the Commission's Schengen page says Cyprus 'participates in the Schengen cooperation' but internal border controls 'have not yet been abolished by the Council' and integration 'is currently underway'. Per press, the Commission found Cyprus technically ready in July 2026 after a December 2025 monitoring mission; the remaining step is a unanimous Council decision of the Schengen states, and the item was not on the agenda of the Justice and Home Affairs Council in Luxembourg at the start of October 2026. No date for the decision is published.

m-a733069c.t: The revision of the Cyprus Registrar of Companies' fees has no published draft as of 6 October 2026. The Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry's Annual Action Plan 2026 schedules it for May 2026-May 2027 (item 7.4, 'bills/regulations'), within an €8 million 2024-2027 programme to modernise the Registrar's department. The e-consultation portal (searches 'τέλη', 'Εταιρειών', 'Εφόρου Εταιρειών') shows no Registrar fee draft, and the Registrar's news items of January to September 2026 announce none.

m-a657b5a4.t: For the EUR 3 duty on low-value imports, an 'item' is not each article: per the Commission's guidance (DG TAXUD, version of 2 June 2026), an item is goods in a consignment sharing the same tariff classification, description and, where given, origin (art. 1(61) of the Union Customs Code Delegated Act), and because of IT limits the duty 'will automatically apply per declaration line irrespective of the quantity' of articles on that line, provided the goods in the declaration are worth up to EUR 150 in total. The guidance says it is explanatory and not legally binding.

m-a1e352d1.t: The Cyprus Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry's Annual Action Plan 2026 (PDF created 31 October 2025) reschedules the revision of the Registrar's company fees to May 2026-May 2027 (item 7.4, 'bills/regulations'; the 2025 plan had December 2024-December 2025). It also lists Companies Section law changes arising from the new registry system for 12 September 2025-12 September 2026 (item 7.5) and the registry platform for November 2022-December 2026 (item 7.1, led by the Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy, Recovery and Resilience Plan funds, 6.8 in EUR million). As of 6 October 2026 CyLaw's index of 2026 regulatory acts shows no new Companies fees regulations.

m-99da884e.t: What the EU payments package would change for a small merchant, per the Council's release on the provisional agreement of 27 November 2025: firms providing card acceptance must make clear the fees they charge; merchants must ensure their normal trading name matches the name on customers' statements; retailers may offer cash withdrawals without a purchase, by chip and PIN, up to EUR 150; payee name and IBAN are checked before any transfer. As of 6 October 2026 neither the Payment Services Regulation nor PSD3 is adopted: both files read 'Awaiting Council's 1st reading position', indicative plenary date 14 December 2026.

m-994d2bcd.t: Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382 of 11 February 2026 deleted the EU customs-duty relief for consignments up to EUR 150 and, from 1 July 2026 until 1 July 2028, charges EUR 3 per item in a consignment worth up to EUR 150 where the import is VAT-exempt under the Import One-Stop Shop or comes by post; per the recitals, other importers pay the Common Customs Tariff. Next steps in the act: by 1 October 2026 and monthly after, the Commission checks for trade diversion and may propose the EUR 3 duty for all consignments up to EUR 150; by 1 December 2027 it assesses whether a central EU duty system will work by 1 July 2028 and may propose an extension.

m-98ffff04.t: Cyprus has drafted, not enacted, the transposition of the beneficial-owner register articles of Directive (EU) 2024/1640 (arts 11, 12, 13 and 15, due 10 July 2026). The Ministry of Finance's AML (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill of 2026, in public consultation from 30 June to 24 July 2026, would let the three register keepers - the Registrar of Companies, the General Registrar and CySEC - issue directives on who may access the registers and how far, what proves a legitimate interest, records of access, informing beneficial owners, and exemptions. On 6 October 2026 the page reads 'under processing'; the bill is in neither the Gazette's bills annex (10 July-2 October 2026) nor CyLaw's 2026 laws.

m-9716c449.t: Cyprus's Cabinet approved on 21 February 2024 an Interior Ministry bill, 'Ο περί Πιστοποίησης της Γνησιότητας της Υπογραφής Νόμος του 2023', to replace the Certifying Officers Law 165(I)/2012: certification of signatures and seals would pass to the Citizen Service Centres (KEP/KEPO) and to designated officials of departments with large volumes, the roughly 200 existing certifying officers would keep their appointments until retirement with no new ones, and certifications would be logged electronically. The Ministry said the bill would be tabled in the House. As of 6 October 2026 it still publishes a list of certifying officers dated September 2026; the bill's stage was not established.

m-8fff4f7d.t: A government bill would let the Cyprus Registrar of Companies strike off a company, and refuse any right, registration, filing or application under the Companies Law, where its purpose or operation aims or tends to undermine the Republic, national security or public order, or endangers state sovereignty, 'without any reasoning being required'; the Registrar says only which ground applies and may say it rests on undisclosable information (new s. 397, Companies (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill of 2026). The Attorney General's memorandum cites the continued occupation of part of Cyprus. Per press, the Cabinet approved it on 6 August and it was tabled on 17 September 2026; a bill on 6 October 2026.

m-8d964397.t: From 10 July 2027 the EU AML Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 binds legal entities created in the Union directly: obtain accurate, up-to-date beneficial-owner information within 28 calendar days of creation, update it within 28 days of a change and yearly (art. 62(2)); report it to the central register 'without undue delay' after creation, and any change within 28 calendar days (art. 63(2)). A Cyprus company now has 90 days from incorporation to file and 45 days for a change (K.D.P. 112/2021 paras 9(1), 10(2), as amended by K.D.P. 34/2024). The change window will shorten; for the first report the Regulation fixes no number of days. No Cyprus act adjusting this was found as of 6 October 2026.

m-89fbfeac.t: The recast EU Single Permit Directive (EU) 2024/1233, whose employer-change rules had to be in force by 21 May 2026, makes a third-country worker's permit more portable: Member States 'shall allow' a change of employer and may require notification, a labour-market check where they run one, or a minimum period with the first employer of at most six months; where notice is required they may suspend the change for up to 45 days and oppose it (art. 11(2)-(3)). As of 6 October 2026 no Cyprus transposing measure was found: EUR-Lex lists none for Cyprus, the Gazette search finds nothing citing '2024/1233', and CyLaw's 2026 laws have no Aliens and Immigration amendment.

m-87d14319.t: A draft Social Insurance (Amendment) Bill of 2026 on pension reform, put to consultation by the Social Insurance Services from 2 to 16 September 2026 (draft dated 18 August 2026; status 'under processing' on 6 October 2026), would add to the insurable earnings of a person employed in a private company in which he is a shareholder every dividend he receives from that company (amended definition of 'αποδοχές' in s. 2, read with para. 5 of Part I of the First Schedule). It is a draft, not a tabled bill; it would start on a date the Council of Ministers sets by notice in the Gazette, possibly different for different provisions (s. 42).

m-6a1d8d65.t: The EU late-payment regulation proposed on 12 September 2023 (COM(2023) 533, 2023/0323(COD)) would cap payment periods in commercial transactions at 30 calendar days from receipt of the invoice, provided the debtor has received the goods or services, between businesses and where a public authority pays a business (art. 3(1)), replacing Directive 2011/7/EU. As of 6 October 2026 it has stalled: Parliament adopted its first-reading position on 23 April 2024, the file's only later entry is the resumption of business on 13 November 2024, and it reads 'Awaiting Council's 1st reading position'. The Commission's 2026 work programme keeps it in Annex III 'Pending proposals', not among withdrawals.

m-6386aa9e.t: No date is set for Cyprus's small-entity reporting standard, on which all of Law 2(I)/2026 except art. 5 waits (s. 7). Under Law 1(I)/2026 ICPAC develops the standard and submits it to the Finance Minister, who approves it, informs the European Commission 'for their approval' and publishes in the Gazette the standards 'approved by the European Commission' (ss. 4-5). ICPAC announced its standard-setting committee on 26 May 2026 ('timeline ... at a later stage'); its due-process handbook (published then; the current PDF is dated 23 September 2026) requires a consultation document, comments 'generally' for 60 days. Its 'Consultation' and 'The Standard' pages held no document on 6 October 2026.

m-51af17ef.t: The Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry's Annual Action Plan 2026 (PDF created 31 October 2025) assigns the Registrar of Companies (ΤΕΕΔΙ) the drafting of a framework for the establishment and operation of limited partnerships 'with separate legal personality', scheduled September 2025-January 2027 (item 4.9, type 'legislation'). Today s. 47(6) of the Partnerships and Business Names Law, Cap. 116, says limited partnerships, with or without share capital, are not legal persons with separate legal personality. As of 6 October 2026 no such bill was found on the e-consultation portal, in the Gazette's bills annex or in CyLaw's 2026 laws.

m-4bcb0f06.t: AMLA's final draft standards on customer due diligence under art. 28(1) of the AML Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (final report of 30 September 2026, published 1 October) await Commission adoption as of 6 October 2026. As drafted they would apply to all obliged entities six months after entry into force, not from 10 July 2027. Identity is verified from an identity document, passport or equivalent, or by electronic identification or qualified trust services, also face to face; remote 'alternative solutions' only where neither can reasonably be used, with safeguards the entity must justify; all declared nationalities recorded, one verified; a company from its constitution and register extracts.

m-4afdd455.t: Since 5 October 2026 a request to register or change the bank account (IBAN) on a Cyprus tax file is accepted only through the Tax For All portal after logging in with CY Login, with form T.F. 2008 and an IBAN confirmation from the bank; requests made otherwise, e.g. by e-mail, are rejected (Tax Department announcement of 22 September 2026). The IBAN must be in the name of the beneficiary to whom payment may be made. An entity for which a CY Login objectively cannot be obtained, because the entity cannot be identified, files a signed form T.F. 2008-S through the portal without CY Login; the exception does not cover entities that simply have not yet obtained one.

m-43c53914.t: The digital euro Regulation proposed on 28 June 2023 (COM(2023) 369, 2023/0212(COD)) would oblige payees to accept the digital euro (art. 7(3)), but an enterprise with fewer than 10 persons or turnover or balance sheet up to EUR 2 million may refuse it 'unless it accepts comparable digital means of payment' (art. 9(a)), defined to include debit-card and instant payments at the point of interaction (art. 2(25)); so a micro shop or café taking debit cards would have to accept it. As of 6 October 2026 it is not adopted: the Council agreed its position on 19 December 2025, and Parliament's committee report of 23 June 2026 was confirmed as a mandate for negotiations on 9 July 2026.

m-2ded408a.t: The same pension-reform draft (consulted on 2-16 September 2026, 'under processing' on 6 October 2026) would make 'εισοδηματίες' - people with income from an office, dividends, interest, rents, royalties or property - pay a contribution of 15.82% of that income each year, up to the basic insurable earnings, where they are Cypriot or EU citizens ordinarily resident in the government-controlled areas and that year have no insurable employment, no contributions or credited earnings on their behalf and no voluntary insurance; the rate would rise to 17.1% from 2029, 18.5% from 2034 and 19.6% from 2039 (new s. 20B). The Ministry's summary adds third-country nationals under Regulation 883/2004.

m-2cce8b2b.t: A Digital Fairness Act for online consumer sales is planned, not proposed, as of 6 October 2026: the Commission's 2026 work programme (21 October 2025) lists it as a legislative initiative on Article 114 TFEU for Q4 2026, to 'tackle outstanding unfair and deceptive consumer practices', and the Commission's Have Your Say page shows a proposal for a directive as 'upcoming', planned for 1 October-31 December 2026. The Commission's call for evidence of 17 July 2025 says the impact assessment would explore targeted prohibitions on, for example, dark patterns, addictive design, personalised advertising and pricing, drip pricing and difficult cancellation of subscriptions; none is decided.

m-29389ff7.t: Under rule 84B of the Rules of Procedure of the Cyprus House of Representatives (published in the Gazette on 1 November 2019; parliament.cy unofficial codification of January 2020), members' bills pending before a committee at the end of a parliamentary term whose discussion has not yet begun, and members' bills tabled by MPs who were not re-elected, are deemed withdrawn at the start of the new term and struck off the committee's agenda; reviving one needs a new tabling. The rule names only members' bills, not government bills or regulations. A Nomoplatform 'pending' label on such a bill after the May 2026 elections is therefore not proof that it is live. Read 6 October 2026.

m-247fe785.t: Cyprus's state lender for small firms is in force: by decision No. 984 of 6 August 2026 (Gazette Annex Four Part I, No. 4970, 14 August 2026) the Council of Ministers, under s. 68 of the Cyprus Business Development Organisation Law 124(I)/2026, set 6 August 2026 as the Law's commencement date and appointed the organisation's (ΚΟΑΕ) board for 10 August 2026-9 August 2028. Under the Law it may give loans, guarantees, grants and advisory programmes only through published schemes, to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises registered and active in Cyprus, with EUR 60 million of State capital. Whether any scheme had been published by 6 October 2026 was not checked.

m-1e4507dc.t: From 10 July 2027 the EU AML Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 caps cash for goods and services: persons trading in goods or providing services may accept or make a cash payment only up to EUR 10,000, in one or linked operations (art. 80(1)); lower national limits may apply (art. 80(2)-(3)); payments between natural persons not acting professionally, and payments or deposits at banks, e-money issuers and payment service providers, are outside the cap (art. 80(4)). For a Cyprus shop or café the figure does not move: Cyprus has capped cash at EUR 10,000 since 31 December 2024 (Law 172(I)/2024). As of 6 October 2026 the Regulation is in force, not yet applicable.

m-18463591.t: The Commission proposed the '28th regime' company form, EU Inc., on 18 March 2026 (COM(2026) 321, procedure 2026/0074(COD)): a limited-liability company formed by one or more natural or legal persons, with no minimum capital and at least one director resident in the Union. Formed online with the EU templates, its preventive control and registration must be done within 48 hours at a cost of at most EUR 100 (5 working days without templates). As of 6 October 2026 it is a proposal only: the Parliament's file reads 'Awaiting committee decision', indicative plenary date 19 October 2026; it would apply from the last day of the 12th month after entry into force.

m-0ca53087.t: The EU Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853 must be transposed by 9 December 2026 (art. 22(1)). Where the manufacturer is outside the EU, the importer and the manufacturer's authorised representative are liable, and the fulfilment service provider where there is neither (art. 8(1)(c)); if no EU-based liable operator can be identified, a distributor that fails to name one, or its own supplier, within one month of the injured person's request is liable (art. 8(3)). Cyprus consulted on a bill from 25 February to 26 March 2026 ('completed', revised draft posted); on 6 October 2026 no law has been published.

m-091c37c4.t: No next step is dated for Cyprus's Companies (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill of 2026, which would let the Registrar strike off a company, or refuse any registration, filing or application under the Companies Law, on national-security or public-order grounds: as of 6 October 2026 Nomoplatform's record (file 23.01.067.138-2026) shows only its tabling and referral to the Energy, Commerce, Industry and Tourism Committee on 17 September 2026, stage 'pending'.
